yatra prītyai mayā kāryo vāsastava manohare |
meghāstatra na gantāraḥ kadācidapi matpriye ||
2.2.d:
ईश्वरः उवाच ।
यत्र प्रीत्यै मया कार्यो वासस्तव मनोहरे ।
मेघास्तत्र न गन्तारः कदाचिदपि मत्प्रिये ॥
2.2.m: The Lord said: / 'Wherever I must make an abode for your pleasure, O charming lady, / the clouds will never go there, O my beloved!

2.2.s:
meghā nitambaparyantaṃ sañcaranti mahībhṛtaḥ |
sadā prāleyasānostu varṣāsvapi manohare ||
2.2.d:
मेघा नितम्बपर्यन्तं सञ्चरन्ति महीभृतः ।
सदा प्रालेयसानोस्तु वर्षास्वपि मनोहरे ॥
2.2.m: Clouds move only as far as the hips of the mountain, / always on the slopes of snow, even in the rainy season, O charming lady.

2.2.s:
kailāsasya tathā devi pādagāḥ prāyaśo ghanāḥ |
sañcaranti na gacchanti tata ūrdhvaṃ kadācana ||
2.2.d:
कैलासस्य तथा देवि पादगाः प्रायशो घनाः ।
सञ्चरन्ति न गच्छन्ति तत ऊर्ध्वं कदाचन ॥
2.2.m: Likewise, O goddess, clouds mostly move at the foot of Kailāsa; / they never go above that.

2.2.s:
sumerorvā girerūrdhvaṃ na gacchanti balāhakāḥ |
jambūmūlaṃ samāsādya puṣkarāvartakādayaḥ ||
2.2.d:
सुमेरोर्वा गिरेरूर्ध्वं न गच्छन्ति बलाहकाः ।
जम्बूमूलं समासाद्य पुष्करावर्तकादयः ॥
2.2.m: Nor do clouds go above Mount Sumeru; / having reached the foot of the jambū tree, the puṣkarāvarta clouds and others [halt].

2.2.s:
ityukteṣu girīndreṣu yasyopari bhaveddhi te |
manorucirnivāsāya tamācakṣva drutaṃ hi me ||
2.2.d:
इत्युक्तेषु गिरीन्द्रेषु यस्योपरि भवेद्धि ते ।
मनोरुचिर्निवासाय तमाचक्ष्व द्रुतं हि मे ॥
2.2.m: Among these lords of mountains mentioned, upon whichever one your heart / has a desire for a dwelling, tell me quickly!

2.2.s:
svecchāvihāraistava kautukāni suvarṇapakṣānilavṛndavṛndaiḥ |
śabdottaraṅgairmadhurasvanaistai-rmudopageyāni girau himotthe ||
2.2.d:
स्वेच्छाविहारैस्तव कौतुकानि सुवर्णपक्षानिलवृन्दवृन्दैः ।
शब्दोत्तरङ्गैर्मधुरस्वनैस्तै-र्मुदोपगेयानि गिरौ हिमोत्थे ॥
2.2.m: In your roaming at will, your sports, with flocks of golden-winged breezes, / surging with sound, sweet-toned, are to be sung with joy on the snowy mountain.

2.2.s:
siddhāṅganāste racitāsanā bhuvaṃ kāṅkṣanti caivopahṛtaṃ sakautukam |
svecchāvihāre maṇikuṭṭime girau kurvanti ceṣyanti phalādidānakaiḥ ||
2.2.d:
सिद्धाङ्गनास्ते रचितासना भुवं काङ्क्षन्ति चैवोपहृतं सकौतुकम् ।
स्वेच्छाविहारे मणिकुट्टिमे गिरौ कुर्वन्ति चेष्यन्ति फलादिदानकैः ॥
2.2.m: The women of the Siddhas, having arranged their seats, desire the earth and what is offered with eagerness; / roaming at will on the mountain with jewel-inlaid floors, they perform [their sports] and wish [to welcome you] with gifts of fruits and the like.

2.2.s:
phaṇīndrakanyā girikanyakāśca yā nāgakanyāśca turaṅgamukhyāḥ |
sarvāstu tāste satataṃ sahāyatāṃ samācariṣyantyanumodavibhramaiḥ ||
2.2.d:
फणीन्द्रकन्या गिरिकन्यकाश्च या नागकन्याश्च तुरङ्गमुख्याः ।
सर्वास्तु तास्ते सततं सहायतां समाचरिष्यन्त्यनुमोदविभ्रमैः ॥
2.2.m: Daughters of serpent-lords, daughters of mountains, Nāga maidens, and the foremost Kinnara women— / all of them will constantly render service to you with charming gestures of joy.

2.2.s:
rūpaṃ tadevamatulaṃ vadanaṃ sucāru dṛṣṭvāṅganā nijavapurnijakāntisahyam |
helā nije vapuṣi rūpagaṇeṣu nityaṃ kartāra ityanimiṣekṣaṇacārurūpāḥ ||
2.2.d:
रूपं तदेवमतुलं वदनं सुचारु दृष्ट्वाङ्गना निजवपुर्निजकान्तिसह्यम् ।
हेला निजे वपुषि रूपगणेषु नित्यं कर्तार इत्यनिमिषेक्षणचारुरूपाः ॥
2.2.m: Seeing that peerless form and very lovely face, women will bear the beauty of their own bodies / with playful indifference toward their own form and multitudes of charms, lovely with unblinking eyes.

2.2.s:
yā menakā parvatarāja jāyā rūpairguṇaiḥ khyātavatī triloke |
sā cāpi te tatra mano'numodaṃ nityaṃ kariṣyatyanunāthanādyaiḥ ||
2.2.d:
या मेनका पर्वतराज जाया रूपैर्गुणैः ख्यातवती त्रिलोके ।
सा चापि ते तत्र मनोऽनुमोदं नित्यं करिष्यत्यनुनाथनाद्यैः ॥
2.2.m: Menakā, the wife of the king of mountains, renowned for her beauties and virtues throughout the three worlds— / she too will constantly bring joy to your heart there with entreaties and the like.

2.2.s:
purasthavargairgirirājavandyaiḥ prītiṃ vicinvadbhirudārarūpām |
śikṣā sadā te khalu śocitāpi kāryānvahaṃ prītiyutā guṇādyaiḥ ||
2.2.d:
पुरस्थवर्गैर्गिरिराजवन्द्यैः प्रीतिं विचिन्वद्भिरुदाररूपाम् ।
शिक्षा सदा ते खलु शोचितापि कार्यान्वहं प्रीतियुता गुणाद्यैः ॥
2.2.m: By the crowds dwelling in the city, praised by the king of mountains, seeking affection of a noble nature, / instruction to you, though always considered, is to be performed daily, filled with love through your virtues and charms.

2.2.s:
vicitraiḥ kokilālāpamodaiḥ kuñjagaṇāvṛtam |
sadā vasantaprabhavaṃ gantumicchasi kiṃ priye ||
2.2.d:
विचित्रैः कोकिलालापमोदैः कुञ्जगणावृतम् ।
सदा वसन्तप्रभवं गन्तुमिच्छसि किं प्रिये ॥
2.2.m: Filled with diverse bowers resplendent with the delightful calls of cuckoos, / an eternal source of spring—do you wish to go [there], beloved?

2.2.s:
nānābahujalāpūrṇasaraḥ śītasamāvṛtam |
padminīśataśoyuktamacalendraṃ himālayam ||
2.2.d:
नानाबहुजलापूर्णसरः शीतसमावृतम् ।
पद्मिनीशतशोयुक्तमचलेन्द्रं हिमालयम् ॥
2.2.m: To the lord of mountains, the Himālaya, filled with lakes abounding in varied waters, surrounded by cool breezes, / endowed with hundreds of lotus beds;

2.2.s:
sarvakāmapradairvṛkṣaiḥ śādvalaiḥ kalpasaṃjñakaiḥ |
sakṣaṇaṃ paśya kusumānyathāśvakarigovrajam ||
2.2.d:
सर्वकामप्रदैर्वृक्षैः शाद्वलैः कल्पसंज्ञकैः ।
सक्षणं पश्य कुसुमान्यथाश्वकरिगोव्रजम् ॥
2.2.m: with trees granting all desires, with grassy lawns called wish-fulfilling, / see for a moment flowers as well as herds of horses, elephants, and cattle;

2.2.s:
praśāntaśvāpadagaṇaṃ munibhiryatibhirvṛtam |
devālaye mahāmāye nānāmṛgagaṇairyutam ||
2.2.d:
प्रशान्तश्वापदगणं मुनिभिर्यतिभिर्वृतम् ।
देवालये महामाये नानामृगगणैर्युतम् ॥
2.2.m: where herds of wild beasts are pacified, surrounded by sages and ascetics, / in the abode of gods, O great illusory power, filled with multitudes of varied animals;

2.2.s:
sphāṭikaiḥ svarṇavaprādyai rājataiśca virājitam |
mānasādisaroraṅgairabhitaḥ pariśobhitam ||
2.2.d:
स्फाटिकैः स्वर्णवप्राद्यै राजतैश्च विराजितम् ।
मानसादिसरोरङ्गैरभितः परिशोभितम् ॥
2.2.m: shining with ramparts of crystal, gold, and silver, / beautified on all sides by expanses of lakes such as Mānasa;

2.2.s:
hiraṇmayai ratnanālaiḥ paṅkajairmukulairvṛtam |
śiśumāraistathāsaṅkhyaiḥ kacchapairmakaraiḥ karaiḥ ||
2.2.d:
हिरण्मयै रत्ननालैः पङ्कजैर्मुकुलैर्वृतम् ।
शिशुमारैस्तथासङ्ख्यैः कच्छपैर्मकरैः करैः ॥
2.2.m: filled with golden lotuses and buds with stalks of jewels, / and with innumerable porpoises, turtles, makaras, and crocodiles;

2.2.s:
niṣevitaṃ mañjulaiśca tathā nīlotpalādibhiḥ |
deveśi tasmānmuktaiśca sarvagandhaiśca kuṅkumaiḥ ||
2.2.d:
निषेवितं मञ्जुलैश्च तथा नीलोत्पलादिभिः ।
देवेशि तस्मान्मुक्तैश्च सर्वगन्धैश्च कुङ्कुमैः ॥
2.2.m: resorted to by lovely blue water-lilies and the like, / O queen of the gods, and by all perfumes, saffron, and pearls;

2.2.s:
lasadgandhajalaiḥ śubhrairāpūrṇaiḥ svacchakāntibhiḥ |
śādvalaistaruṇaistuṅgaistīrasthairupaśobhitam ||
2.2.d:
लसद्गन्धजलैः शुभ्रैरापूर्णैः स्वच्छकान्तिभिः ।
शाद्वलैस्तरुणैस्तुङ्गैस्तीरस्थैरुपशोभितम् ॥
2.2.m: filled with bright, shining, fragrant waters of clear luster, / adorned with young, tall grasslands standing on the banks;

2.2.s:
nṛtyadbhiriva śākhoṭairvarjayantaṃ svasambhavam |
kāmadevaiḥ sārasaiśca mattacakrāṅgaśobhitaiḥ ||
2.2.d:
नृत्यद्भिरिव शाखोटैर्वर्जयन्तं स्वसम्भवम् ।
कामदेवैः सारसैश्च मत्तचक्राङ्गशोभितैः ॥
2.2.m: dispelling its own origin with śākhoṭa trees that seem to dance, / beautified by cranes, lovely as love-gods, and impassioned geese;

2.2.s:
madhurārāvibhirmodakāribhirbhramarādibhiḥ |
śabdāyamānaṃ ca mudā kāmoddīpanakārakam ||
2.2.d:
मधुराराविभिर्मोदकारिभिर्भ्रमरादिभिः ।
शब्दायमानं च मुदा कामोद्दीपनकारकम् ॥
2.2.m: resounding joyfully with sweetly buzzing, delight-causing bees and the like, / awakening passionate desire;

2.2.s:
vāsavasya kuberasya yamasya varuṇasya ca |
agneḥ koṇaparājasya mārutasya parasya ca ||
2.2.d:
वासवस्य कुबेरस्य यमस्य वरुणस्य च ।
अग्नेः कोणपराजस्य मारुतस्य परस्य च ॥
2.2.m: or the lofty Meru, the abode of the gods, whose peak is adorned with the cities / of Vāsava, Kubera, Yama, Varuṇa, / of Agni, of the lord of the corner (Nirṛti), of Māruta, and of the supreme [deity];

2.2.s:
purībhiḥ śobhiśikharaṃ meroruccaiḥ surālayam |
rambhāśacīmenakādirambhorugaṇasevitam ||
2.2.d:
पुरीभिः शोभिशिखरं मेरोरुच्चैः सुरालयम् ।
रम्भाशचीमेनकादिरम्भोरुगणसेवितम् ॥
2.2.m: attended by groups of round-thighed celestial nymphs such as Rambhā, Śacī, and Menakā—

2.2.s:
kiṃ tvamicchasi sarveṣāṃ parvatānāṃ hi bhūbhṛtām |
sārabhūte mahāramye saṃvihartuṃ mahāgirau ||
2.2.d:
किं त्वमिच्छसि सर्वेषां पर्वतानां हि भूभृताम् ।
सारभूते महारम्ये संविहर्तुं महागिरौ ॥
2.2.m: do you wish to sport upon this great mountain, / the very essence of all mountains and earth-supporters, exceedingly delightful?'

2.2.s:
tatra devī sakhiyutā sāpsarogaṇamaṇḍitā |
nityaṃ kariṣyati śacī tava yogyāṃ sahāyatām ||
2.2.d:
तत्र देवी सखियुता साप्सरोगणमण्डिता ।
नित्यं करिष्यति शची तव योग्यां सहायताम् ॥
2.2.m: There, O goddess, together with her friends and adorned by hosts of apsarases, / Śacī will constantly provide you with fitting companionship.

2.2.s:
athavā mama kailāse parvatendre sadāśraye |
sthānamicchasi vitteśapurīparivirājite ||
2.2.d:
अथवा मम कैलासे पर्वतेन्द्रे सदाश्रये ।
स्थानमिच्छसि वित्तेशपुरीपरिविराजिते ॥
2.2.m: Or do you desire a place on my Kailāsa, chief of mountains, an everlasting abode, / resplendent with the city of the lord of wealth,

2.2.s:
gaṅgājalaughaprayate pūrṇacandrasamaprabhe |
darīṣu sānuṣu sadā brahmakanyābhyudīrite ||
2.2.d:
गङ्गाजलौघप्रयते पूर्णचन्द्रसमप्रभे ।
दरीषु सानुषु सदा ब्रह्मकन्याभ्युदीरिते ॥
2.2.m: purified by torrents of Gaṅgā’s water, radiant like the full moon, / where daughters of Brahmā ever sing in the caves and upon the slopes,

2.2.s:
nānāmṛgagaṇairyukte padmākaraśatāvṛte |
sarvairguṇaiśca sadvastusumerorapi sundare ||
2.2.d:
नानामृगगणैर्युक्ते पद्माकरशतावृते ।
सर्वैर्गुणैश्च सद्वस्तुसुमेरोरपि सुन्दरे ॥
2.2.m: abounding with diverse herds of deer, covered with hundreds of lotus pools, / and beautiful through all good qualities even beyond Sumeru?

2.2.s:
sthāneṣveteṣu yatrāpi tavāntaḥkaraṇe spṛhā |
taṃ drutaṃ me samācakṣva vāsakartāsmi tatra te ||
2.2.d:
स्थानेष्वेतेषु यत्रापि तवान्तःकरणे स्पृहा ।
तं द्रुतं मे समाचक्ष्व वासकर्तास्मि तत्र ते ॥
2.2.m: Whichever of these places your heart desires, / tell me quickly; I will make your dwelling there."

2.2.s:
brahmovāca |
itīrite śaṅkareṇa tadā dākṣāyaṇī śanaiḥ |
idamāha mahādevaṃ lakṣaṇaṃ svaprakāśanam ||
2.2.d:
ब्रह्मोवाच ।
इतीरिते शङ्करेण तदा दाक्षायणी शनैः ।
इदमाह महादेवं लक्षणं स्वप्रकाशनम् ॥
2.2.m: Brahmā said: / When Śaṅkara had spoken thus, the daughter of Dakṣa then slowly / addressed Mahādeva with words revealing her inner intention:

2.2.s:
satyuvāca |
himādrāveva vasitumahamicche tvayā saha |
nacirātkuru saṃvāsaṃ tasminneva mahāgirau ||
2.2.d:
सत्युवाच ।
हिमाद्रावेव वसितुमहमिच्छे त्वया सह ।
नचिरात्कुरु संवासं तस्मिन्नेव महागिरौ ॥
2.2.m: Satī said: / "I wish to dwell only on the Himālaya with you; / without delay make our abode on that very great mountain."

2.2.s:
brahmovāca |
atha tadvākyamākarṇya haraḥ paramamohitaḥ |
himādriśikharaṃ tuṅgaṃ dākṣāyaṇyā samaṃ yayau ||
2.2.d:
ब्रह्मोवाच ।
अथ तद्वाक्यमाकर्ण्य हरः परममोहितः ।
हिमाद्रिशिखरं तुङ्गं दाक्षायण्या समं ययौ ॥
2.2.m: Brahmā said: / Then, hearing her words, Hara, deeply infatuated, / went together with the daughter of Dakṣa to the lofty peak of the Himālaya.

2.2.s:
siddhāṅganāgaṇayutamagamyaṃ caiva pakṣibhiḥ |
agamacchikharaṃ ramyaṃ sarasīvanarājitam ||
2.2.d:
सिद्धाङ्गनागणयुतमगम्यं चैव पक्षिभिः ।
अगमच्छिखरं रम्यं सरसीवनराजितम् ॥
2.2.m: Crowded with hosts of wives of siddhas, impassable even to birds, / he reached that delightful peak adorned with lakes and woods.

2.2.s:
vicitrarūpaiḥ kamalaiḥ śikharaṃ ratnakarburam |
bālārkasadṛśaṃ śambhurāsasāda satīsakhaḥ ||
2.2.d:
विचित्ररूपैः कमलैः शिखरं रत्नकर्बुरम् ।
बालार्कसदृशं शम्भुराससाद सतीसखः ॥
2.2.m: To that peak variegated with lotus blossoms of diverse forms, speckled with gems, / and resembling the morning sun, Śambhu arrived accompanied by Satī.

2.2.s:
sphaṭikābhramaye tasmin śādvaladrumarājite |
vicitrapuṣpāvalibhiḥ sarasībhiśca saṃyute ||
2.2.d:
स्फटिकाभ्रमये तस्मिन् शाद्वलद्रुमराजिते ।
विचित्रपुष्पावलिभिः सरसीभिश्च संयुते ॥
2.2.m: On that [peak] made of crystal and cloud, adorned with rows of grassy lawns and trees, / filled with diverse rows of flowers and with lakes,

2.2.s:
praphullataruśākhāgraṃ guñjad bhramarasevitam |
paṅkeruhaiḥ praphullaiśca nīlotpalacayaistathā ||
2.2.d:
प्रफुल्लतरुशाखाग्रं गुञ्जद् भ्रमरसेवितम् ।
पङ्केरुहैः प्रफुल्लैश्च नीलोत्पलचयैस्तथा ॥
2.2.m: where blooming tree-tops were frequented by humming bees, / with blossoming lotuses and clusters of blue water-lilies,

2.2.s:
śobhitaṃ cakravākādyaiḥ kādambairhaṃsasaṅkulaiḥ |
pramattasārasaiḥ krauñcairnīlaskandhaiśca śabditaiḥ ||
2.2.d:
शोभितं चक्रवाकाद्यैः कादम्बैर्हंससङ्कुलैः ।
प्रमत्तसारसैः क्रौञ्चैर्नीलस्कन्धैश्च शब्दितैः ॥
2.2.m: embellished with ruddy geese, kādambas, and flocks of swans, / noisy with impassioned sarus cranes, krauñcas, and peacocks,

2.2.s:
puṃskokilānāṃ ninadairmadhurairgaṇasevitaiḥ |
turaṅgavadanaiḥ siddhairapsarobhiśca guhyakaiḥ ||
2.2.d:
पुंस्कोकिलानां निनदैर्मधुरैर्गणसेवितैः ।
तुरङ्गवदनैः सिद्धैरप्सरोभिश्च गुह्यकैः ॥
2.2.m: echoing with the sweet melodies of male cuckoos, frequented by the attendants, / horse-faced beings, siddhas, apsarases, and guhyakas,

2.2.s:
vidyādharībhirdevībhiḥ kinnarībhirvihāritam |
purandhrībhiḥ pārvatībhiḥ kanyābhirabhisaṅgatam ||
2.2.d:
विद्याधरीभिर्देवीभिः किन्नरीभिर्विहारितम् ।
पुरन्ध्रीभिः पार्वतीभिः कन्याभिरभिसङ्गतम् ॥
2.2.m: sported in by vidyādharīs, goddesses, and kinnarīs, / visited by married women, mountain maidens, and young girls,

2.2.s:
vipañcītāntrikāmattamṛdaṅgapaṭahasvanaiḥ |
nṛtyadbhirapsarobhiśca kautukotthaiśca śobhitam ||
2.2.d:
विपञ्चीतान्त्रिकामत्तमृदङ्गपटहस्वनैः ।
नृत्यद्भिरप्सरोभिश्च कौतुकोत्थैश्च शोभितम् ॥
2.2.m: resonant with the sounds of vīṇās, stringed instruments, impassioned mṛdaṅgas and drums, / and adorned by dancing apsarases and joyous wonders,

2.2.s:
devikābhirdīrghikābhirgandhibhiḥ susamāvṛtam |
praphullakusumairnityaṃ sukuñjairupaśobhitam ||
2.2.d:
देविकाभिर्दीर्घिकाभिर्गन्धिभिः सुसमावृतम् ।
प्रफुल्लकुसुमैर्नित्यं सुकुञ्जैरुपशोभितम् ॥
2.2.m: surrounded everywhere by fragrant rivulets and ponds, / and ever adorned by fine bowers with blossoming flowers—

2.2.s:
śailarājapurābhyarṇe śikhare vṛṣabhadhvajaḥ |
saha satyā ciraṃ reme evambhūteṣu śobhanam ||
2.2.d:
शैलराजपुराभ्यर्णे शिखरे वृषभध्वजः ।
सह सत्या चिरं रेमे एवम्भूतेषु शोभनम् ॥
2.2.m: on such a splendid peak near the city of the king of mountains, / Vṛṣabhadhvaja sported with Satī for a long time.

2.2.s:
tasmin svargasame sthāne divyamānena śaṅkaraḥ |
daśavarṣasahasrāṇi reme satyā samaṃ mudā ||
2.2.d:
तस्मिन् स्वर्गसमे स्थाने दिव्यमानेन शङ्करः ।
दशवर्षसहस्राणि रेमे सत्या समं मुदा ॥
2.2.m: In that place resembling heaven, by divine reckoning, / Śaṅkara sported with Satī in joy for ten thousand years.

2.2.s:
sa kadācittataḥ sthānādanyadyāti sthalaṃ haraḥ |
kadācinmeruśikharaṃ devīdevavṛtaṃ sadā ||
2.2.d:
स कदाचित्ततः स्थानादन्यद्याति स्थलं हरः ।
कदाचिन्मेरुशिखरं देवीदेववृतं सदा ॥
2.2.m: Sometimes Hara would go from that place to another spot; / sometimes to the peak of Meru, ever surrounded by goddesses and gods;

2.2.s:
dvīpānnānā tathodyānavanāni vasudhātalam |
gatvā gatvā punastatrābhyetya reme satīsukham ||
2.2.d:
द्वीपान्नाना तथोद्यानवनानि वसुधातलम् ।
गत्वा गत्वा पुनस्तत्राभ्येत्य रेमे सतीसुखम् ॥
2.2.m: to various continents, pleasure-gardens, forests, and to the surface of the earth; / having gone and gone again, returning there, he delighted in the pleasure of Satī.

2.2.s:
na yajñe sa divārātrau na brahmaṇi tapassamam |
satyāṃ hi manasā śambhuḥ prītimeva cakāra ha ||
2.2.d:
न यज्ञे स दिवारात्रौ न ब्रह्मणि तपस्समम् ।
सत्यां हि मनसा शम्भुः प्रीतिमेव चकार ह ॥
2.2.m: Neither in sacrifice by day or night, nor in Brahman or equal austerities, / but in Satī alone did Śambhu place his heart's delight.

2.2.s:
evaṃ mahādevamukhaṃ satyapaśyatsma sarvadā |
mahādevo'pi sarvatra sadādrākṣītsatīmukham ||
2.2.d:
एवं महादेवमुखं सत्यपश्यत्स्म सर्वदा ।
महादेवोऽपि सर्वत्र सदाद्राक्षीत्सतीमुखम् ॥
2.2.m: Thus Satī was always gazing upon Mahādeva's face, / and Mahādeva too everywhere constantly looked upon Satī's face.

2.2.s:
evamanyonyasaṃsargādanurāgamahīruham |
vardhayāmāsatuḥ kālīśivau bhāvāmbusecanaiḥ ||
śrīgaṇeśāya namaḥ ||
śrīgaurīśaṅkarābhyāṃ namaḥ ||
śrīśivamahāpurāṇam ||
dvitīyāyāṃ rudrasaṃhitāyāṃ dvitīyaḥ satīkhaṇḍe
2.2.d:
एवमन्योन्यसंसर्गादनुरागमहीरुहम् ।
वर्धयामासतुः कालीशिवौ भावाम्बुसेचनैः ॥
श्रीगणेशाय नमः ॥
श्रीगौरीशङ्कराभ्यां नमः ॥
श्रीशिवमहापुराणम् ॥
द्वितीयायां रुद्रसंहितायां द्वितीयः सतीखण्डे
2.2.m:
Thus, through mutual communion, the great tree of love / did Kālī and Śiva nurture with the sprinklings of the waters of affection.

Thus ends the twenty-second chapter, entitled 'The Description of the Sporting of Śiva and Śivā,' in the second section, the Satīkhaṇḍa, of the second Rudrasaṃhitā in the glorious Śivamahāpurāṇa.

2.2.s:
brahmovāca |
evaṃ kṛtvā vihāraṃ vai śaṅkareṇa ca sā satī |
santuṣṭā sābhavaccāti virāgā samajāyata ||
2.2.d:
ब्रह्मोवाच ।
एवं कृत्वा विहारं वै शङ्करेण च सा सती ।
सन्तुष्टा साभवच्चाति विरागा समजायत ॥
2.2.m: Brahmā said: / Having thus sported with Śaṅkara, Satī / became fully satisfied, and dispassion arose [within her].

2.2.s:
ekasmindivase devī satī rahasi saṅgatā |
śivaṃ praṇamya sadbhaktyā nyasyoccaiḥ sukṛtāñjaliḥ ||
2.2.d:
एकस्मिन्दिवसे देवी सती रहसि सङ्गता ।
शिवं प्रणम्य सद्भक्त्या न्यस्योच्चैः सुकृताञ्जलिः ॥
2.2.m: One day, coming upon Śiva in private, / the goddess Satī bowed with true devotion, raised high her folded hands,

2.2.s:
suprasannaṃ prabhuṃ natvā sā dakṣatanayā satī |
uvāca sāñjalirbhaktyā vinayāvanatā tataḥ ||
2.2.d:
सुप्रसन्नं प्रभुं नत्वा सा दक्षतनया सती ।
उवाच साञ्जलिर्भक्त्या विनयावनता ततः ॥
2.2.m: and, bowing to the gracious lord, that daughter of Dakṣa, Satī, / with joined palms in devotion and bent low in humility, then said:

2.2.s:
satyuvāca |
devadeva mahādeva karuṇāsāgara prabho |
dīnoddhara mahāyogin kṛpāṃ kuru mamopari ||
2.2.d:
सत्युवाच ।
देवदेव महादेव करुणासागर प्रभो ।
दीनोद्धर महायोगिन् कृपां कुरु ममोपरि ॥
2.2.m: Satī said: / "O god of gods, Mahādeva, ocean of compassion, O lord, / uplifter of the wretched, great yogin, have mercy upon me!

2.2.s:
tvaṃ paraḥ puruṣaḥ svāmī rajaḥsattvatamaḥ paraḥ |
nirguṇaḥ saguṇaḥ sākṣī nirvikārī mahāprabhuḥ ||
2.2.d:
त्वं परः पुरुषः स्वामी रजःसत्त्वतमः परः ।
निर्गुणः सगुणः साक्षी निर्विकारी महाप्रभुः ॥
2.2.m: You are the Supreme Person, the master, beyond passion, goodness, and darkness, / without attributes yet possessing attributes, the witness, unchangeable, the great lord.

2.2.s:
dhanyāhaṃ te priyā jātā kāminī suvihāriṇī |
jātastvaṃ me patiḥ svāmin bhaktavātsalyato hara ||
2.2.d:
धन्याहं ते प्रिया जाता कामिनी सुविहारिणी ।
जातस्त्वं मे पतिः स्वामिन् भक्तवात्सल्यतो हर ॥
2.2.m: Blessed am I to have become your beloved wife, sporting well with you; / you have become my husband, O master Hara, out of affection toward devotees.

2.2.s:
kṛto bahusamā nātha vihāraḥ paramastvayā |
santuṣṭāhaṃ maheśāna nivṛttaṃ me manastataḥ ||
2.2.d:
कृतो बहुसमा नाथ विहारः परमस्त्वया ।
सन्तुष्टाहं महेशान निवृत्तं मे मनस्ततः ॥
2.2.m: For many years, O lord, supreme delight was shared with you; / I am satisfied, O Maheśāna, and my mind has turned away from that.

2.2.s:
jñātumicchāmi deveśa paraṃ tattvaṃ sukhāvaham |
yena saṃsāraduḥkhādvai tarejjīvo'ñjasā hara ||
2.2.d:
ज्ञातुमिच्छामि देवेश परं तत्त्वं सुखावहम् ।
येन संसारदुःखाद्वै तरेज्जीवोऽञ्जसा हर ॥
2.2.m: I wish to know, O lord of gods, the supreme truth that brings bliss, / by which a living being may easily cross beyond the misery of worldly existence, O Hara.

2.2.s:
yatkṛtvā viṣayī jīvaḥ sa labhetparamaṃ padam |
saṃsārī na bhavennātha tattvaṃ vada kṛpāṃ kuru ||
2.2.d:
यत्कृत्वा विषयी जीवः स लभेत्परमं पदम् ।
संसारी न भवेन्नाथ तत्त्वं वद कृपां कुरु ॥
2.2.m: Having accomplished which an attached living being attains the supreme state / and is no longer subject to worldly existence, tell me that truth, O lord; have mercy."

2.2.s:
brahmovāca |
ityapṛcchatsma sadbhaktyā śaṅkaraṃ sā satī mune |
ādiśaktirmaheśānī jīvoddhārāya kevalam ||
2.2.d:
ब्रह्मोवाच ।
इत्यपृच्छत्स्म सद्भक्त्या शङ्करं सा सती मुने ।
आदिशक्तिर्महेशानी जीवोद्धाराय केवलम् ॥
2.2.m: Brahmā said: / Thus, O sage, Satī, the Primordial Power and sovereign lady, / questioned Śaṅkara with true devotion solely for the deliverance of living beings.

2.2.s:
ākarṇya tacchivaḥ svāmī svecchayopāttavigrahaḥ |
avocatparamaprītaḥ satīṃ yogaviraktadhīḥ ||
2.2.d:
आकर्ण्य तच्छिवः स्वामी स्वेच्छयोपात्तविग्रहः ।
अवोचत्परमप्रीतः सतीं योगविरक्तधीः ॥
2.2.m: Hearing that, Śiva, the master who assumes a form by his own will, / his mind unattached to yoga, spoke to Satī with supreme delight.

2.2.s:
śiva uvāca |
śṛṇu devi pravakṣyāmi dākṣāyaṇi maheśvari |
paraṃ tattvaṃ tadevānuśayī mukto bhavedyataḥ ||
2.2.d:
शिव उवाच ।
शृणु देवि प्रवक्ष्यामि दाक्षायणि महेश्वरि ।
परं तत्त्वं तदेवानुशयी मुक्तो भवेद्यतः ॥
2.2.m: Śiva said: / "Listen, O goddess, daughter of Dakṣa, Maheśvarī, I shall explain / the supreme truth, by following which the sleeper awakens and is liberated.

2.2.s:
paratattvaṃ vijānīhi vijñānaṃ parameśvarī |
dvitīyaṃ smaraṇaṃ yatra nāhaṃ brahmeti śuddhadhīḥ ||
2.2.d:
परतत्त्वं विजानीहि विज्ञानं परमेश्वरी ।
द्वितीयं स्मरणं यत्र नाहं ब्रह्मेति शुद्धधीः ॥
2.2.m: Know the supreme truth to be direct realization, O Parameśvarī, / where there is no second thought, [only the realization:] 'I am Brahman,' for one of pure intellect.

2.2.s:
taddurlabhaṃ triloke'smiṃstajjñātā viralaḥ priye |
yādṛśo yaḥ sa dāso'haṃ brahma sākṣātparātparaḥ ||
2.2.d:
तद्दुर्लभं त्रिलोकेऽस्मिंस्तज्ज्ञाता विरलः प्रिये ।
यादृशो यः स दासोऽहं ब्रह्म साक्षात्परात्परः ॥
2.2.m: That is hard to attain in this triple world, and one who knows it is rare, O beloved; / whoever is such a one, I am his servant, [for he is] Brahman directly, higher than the highest.

2.2.s:
tanmātā mama bhaktiśca bhuktimuktiphalapradā |
sulabhā matprasādāddhi navadhā sā prakīrtitā ||
2.2.d:
तन्माता मम भक्तिश्च भुक्तिमुक्तिफलप्रदा ।
सुलभा मत्प्रसादाद्धि नवधा सा प्रकीर्तिता ॥
2.2.m: Its mother is devotion to me, granting the fruits of enjoyment and liberation; / easily attained through my grace, it is proclaimed to be of nine kinds.

2.2.s:
bhaktau jñāne na bhedo hi tatkartuḥ sarvadā sukham |
vijñānaṃ na bhavatyeva sati bhaktivirodhinaḥ ||
2.2.d:
भक्तौ ज्ञाने न भेदो हि तत्कर्तुः सर्वदा सुखम् ।
विज्ञानं न भवत्येव सति भक्तिविरोधिनः ॥
2.2.m: Indeed there is no difference between devotion and knowledge; for the one who practices it there is always happiness; / direct realization never arises, O Satī, for an opponent of devotion.

2.2.s:
bhaktyādhīḥ sadāhaṃ vai tatprabhāvād gṛheṣvapi |
nīcānāṃ jātihīnānāṃ yāmi devi na saṃśayaḥ ||
2.2.d:
भक्त्याधीः सदाहं वै तत्प्रभावाद् गृहेष्वपि ।
नीचानां जातिहीनानां यामि देवि न संशयः ॥
2.2.m: I am ever controlled by devotion; through its influence / I go even into the houses of the lowly and the outcaste, O goddess, without a doubt.

2.2.s:
sā bhaktirdvividhā devi saguṇā nirguṇā matā |
vaidhī svābhāvikī yā yā varā sā tvavarā smṛtā ||
2.2.d:
सा भक्तिर्द्विविधा देवि सगुणा निर्गुणा मता ।
वैधी स्वाभाविकी या या वरा सा त्ववरा स्मृता ॥
2.2.m: That devotion is considered twofold, O goddess: with attributes and without attributes; / as prescribed by rule and as spontaneous: the latter is superior, whereas the former is regarded as inferior.

2.2.s:
naiṣṭhikyanaiṣṭhikī bhedād dvividhe dvividhe hi te |
ṣaḍvidhā naiṣṭhikī jñeyā dvitīyaikavidhā smṛtā ||
2.2.d:
नैष्ठिक्यनैष्ठिकी भेदाद् द्विविधे द्विविधे हि ते ।
षड्विधा नैष्ठिकी ज्ञेया द्वितीयैकविधा स्मृता ॥
2.2.m: By division into steadfast and non-steadfast, those two are each twofold: / the steadfast is to be known as sixfold, while the second is remembered as single in kind.

2.2.s:
vihitāvihitābhedāttāmanekāṃ vidurbudhāḥ |
tayorbahuvidhatvācca tattvaṃ tvanyatra varṇitam ||
2.2.d:
विहिताविहिताभेदात्तामनेकां विदुर्बुधाः ।
तयोर्बहुविधत्वाच्च तत्त्वं त्वन्यत्र वर्णितम् ॥
2.2.m: The wise know it to be manifold through the distinction of enjoined and unenjoined; / and because of their manifold nature, the truth [about them] is described elsewhere.

2.2.s:
te navāṅge ubhe jñeye varṇite munibhiḥ priye |
varṇayāmi navāṅgāni premataḥ śṛṇu dakṣaje ||
2.2.d:
ते नवाङ्गे उभे ज्ञेये वर्णिते मुनिभिः प्रिये ।
वर्णयामि नवाङ्गानि प्रेमतः शृणु दक्षजे ॥
2.2.m: Both are to be known as having nine limbs, as described by sages, O beloved; / I shall describe those nine limbs; listen with love, O daughter of Dakṣa!"

2.2.s:
śravaṇaṃ kīrtanaṃ caiva smaraṇaṃ sevanaṃ tathā |
dāsyaṃ tathārcanaṃ devi vandanaṃ mama sarvadā ||
2.2.d:
श्रवणं कीर्तनं चैव स्मरणं सेवनं तथा ।
दास्यं तथार्चनं देवि वन्दनं मम सर्वदा ॥
2.2.m: Hearing, singing, remembering, and serving, / as well as servitude, worshipping, and bowing down to me at all times, O goddess,

2.2.s:
sakhyamātmārpaṇaṃ ceti navāṅgāni vidurbudhāḥ |
upāṅgāni śive tasyā bahūni kathitāni vai ||
2.2.d:
सख्यमात्मार्पणं चेति नवाङ्गानि विदुर्बुधाः ।
उपाङ्गानि शिवे तस्या बहूनि कथितानि वै ॥
2.2.m: along with friendship and self-surrender—the wise know these as the nine limbs. / Many subsidiary limbs of it have indeed been declared, O Śivā.

2.2.s:
śṛṇu devi navāṅgānāṃ lakṣaṇāni pṛthak pṛthak |
mama bhaktermano dattvā bhuktimuktipradāni hi ||
2.2.d:
शृणु देवि नवाङ्गानां लक्षणानि पृथक् पृथक् ।
मम भक्तेर्मनो दत्त्वा भुक्तिमुक्तिप्रदानि हि ॥
2.2.m: Listen, O goddess, to the characteristics of the nine limbs one by one, / which grant enjoyment and liberation when one applies the mind to devotion to me.

2.2.s:
kathādernityasammānaṃ kurvandehādibhirmudā |
sthirāsanena tatpānaṃ yattacchravaṇamucyate ||
2.2.d:
कथादेर्नित्यसम्मानं कुर्वन्देहादिभिर्मुदा ।
स्थिरासनेन तत्पानं यत्तच्छ्रवणमुच्यते ॥
2.2.m: Constantly showing respect for stories [about me] and the like with the body and other faculties in joy, / and drinking it in from a firm posture: that is called 'hearing'.

2.2.s:
hṛdākāśena sampaśyan janmakarmāṇi vai mama |
prītyoccoccāraṇaṃ teṣāmetatkīrtanamucyate ||
2.2.d:
हृदाकाशेन सम्पश्यन् जन्मकर्माणि वै मम ।
प्रीत्योच्चोच्चारणं तेषामेतत्कीर्तनमुच्यते ॥
2.2.m: Beholding my births and deeds within the space of the heart, / and loudly reciting them with love: this is called 'singing'.

2.2.s:
vyāpakaṃ devi māṃ dṛṣṭvā nityaṃ sarvatra sarvadā |
nirbhayatvaṃ sadā loke smaraṇaṃ tadudāhṛtam ||
2.2.d:
व्यापकं देवि मां दृष्ट्वा नित्यं सर्वत्र सर्वदा ।
निर्भयत्वं सदा लोके स्मरणं तदुदाहृतम् ॥
2.2.m: Seeing me as omnipresent, O goddess, always, everywhere, and at all times, / with fearlessness at all times in the world: that is declared to be 'remembering'.

2.2.s:
aruṇodayamārabhya sevākāle'ñcitā hṛdā |
nirbhayatvaṃ sadā loke smaraṇaṃ tadudāhṛtam ||
2.2.d:
अरुणोदयमारभ्य सेवाकालेऽञ्चिता हृदा ।
निर्भयत्वं सदा लोके स्मरणं तदुदाहृतम् ॥
2.2.m: Starting from sunrise, with a heart adorned at the time of service, / with fearlessness at all times in the world: that is declared to be 'remembering'.

2.2.s:
sadā sevyānukūlyena sevanaṃ taddhi gogaṇaiḥ |
hṛdayāmṛtabhogena priyaṃ dāsyamudāhṛtam ||
2.2.d:
सदा सेव्यानुकूल्येन सेवनं तद्धि गोगणैः ।
हृदयामृतभोगेन प्रियं दास्यमुदाहृतम् ॥
2.2.m: Constant service in conformity with the one to be served, performed with the organs of action, / delightful through the experience of the heart's nectar: this is declared to be 'servitude'.

2.2.s:
sadā bhṛtyānukūlyena vidhinā me parātmane |
arpaṇaṃ ṣoḍaśānāṃ vai pādyādīnāṃ tadarcanam ||
2.2.d:
सदा भृत्यानुकूल्येन विधिना मे परात्मने ।
अर्पणं षोडशानां वै पाद्यादीनां तदर्चनम् ॥
2.2.m: Constant offering according to rule, in conformity with a servant's duty, / of the sixteen offerings such as water for the feet to me, the Supreme Self: that is 'worship'.

2.2.s:
mantroccāraṇadhyānābhyāṃ manasā vacasā kramāt |
yadaṣṭāṅgena bhūsparśaṃ tadvai vandanamucyate ||
2.2.d:
मन्त्रोच्चारणध्यानाभ्यां मनसा वचसा क्रमात् ।
यदष्टाङ्गेन भूस्पर्शं तद्वै वन्दनमुच्यते ॥
2.2.m: Touching the earth with the eight limbs in sequence, / with recitation of mantras and meditation, by mind and by speech: that indeed is called 'bowing down'.

2.2.s:
maṅgalāmaṅgalaṃ yadyatkarotītīśvaro hi me |
sarvaṃ tanmaṅgalāyeti viśvāsaḥ sakhyalakṣaṇam ||
2.2.d:
मङ्गलामङ्गलं यद्यत्करोतीतीश्वरो हि मे ।
सर्वं तन्मङ्गलायेति विश्वासः सख्यलक्षणम् ॥
2.2.m: The conviction that 'Whatever the Lord does to me, auspicious or inauspicious, / is all for my good' is the mark of 'friendship'.

2.2.s:
kṛtvā dehādikaṃ tasya prītyai sarvaṃ tadarpaṇam |
nirvāhāya ca śūnyatvaṃ yattadātmasamarpaṇam ||
2.2.d:
कृत्वा देहादिकं तस्य प्रीत्यै सर्वं तदर्पणम् ।
निर्वाहाय च शून्यत्वं यत्तदात्मसमर्पणम् ॥
2.2.m: Surrendering the body and all else for his pleasure, / and leaving oneself empty of concern for sustenance: that is 'self-surrender'.

2.2.s:
navāṅgānīti madbhakterbhuktimuktipradāni ca |
mama priyāṇi cātīva jñānotpattikarāṇi ca ||
2.2.d:
नवाङ्गानीति मद्भक्तेर्भुक्तिमुक्तिप्रदानि च ।
मम प्रियाणि चातीव ज्ञानोत्पत्तिकराणि च ॥
2.2.m: These nine limbs of devotion to me grant enjoyment and liberation; / they are exceedingly dear to me and produce knowledge.

2.2.s:
upāṅgāni ca madbhakterbahūni kathitāni vai |
bilvādisevanādīni samūhyāni vicārataḥ ||
2.2.d:
उपाङ्गानि च मद्भक्तेर्बहूनि कथितानि वै ।
बिल्वादिसेवनादीनि समूह्यानि विचारतः ॥
2.2.m: Many subsidiary limbs of devotion to me have also been taught; / services such as tending the bilva tree are to be inferred through reasoning.

2.2.s:
itthaṃ sāṅgopāṅgabhaktirmama sarvottamā priye |
jñānavairāgyajananī muktidāsī virājate ||
2.2.d:
इत्थं साङ्गोपाङ्गभक्तिर्मम सर्वोत्तमा प्रिये ।
ज्ञानवैराग्यजननी मुक्तिदासी विराजते ॥
2.2.m: Thus, devotion to me, complete with limbs and subsidiary limbs, is supreme, O beloved; / it gives birth to knowledge and dispassion, and shines forth with liberation as its handmaiden.

2.2.s:
sarvakarmaphalotpattiḥ sarvadā tvatsamapriyā |
yaccitte sā sthitā nityaṃ sarvadā so'ti matpriyaḥ ||
2.2.d:
सर्वकर्मफलोत्पत्तिः सर्वदा त्वत्समप्रिया ।
यच्चित्ते सा स्थिता नित्यं सर्वदा सोऽति मत्प्रियः ॥
2.2.m: It is the source of the fruit of all actions, always as dear to me as you are; / the person in whose mind it constantly resides is forever exceedingly dear to me.

2.2.s:
trailokye bhaktisadṛśaḥ panthā nāsti sukhāvahaḥ |
caturyugeṣu deveśi kalau tu suviśeṣataḥ ||
2.2.d:
त्रैलोक्ये भक्तिसदृशः पन्था नास्ति सुखावहः ।
चतुर्युगेषु देवेशि कलौ तु सुविशेषतः ॥
2.2.m: In the three worlds there is no path that brings happiness like devotion, / in all four yugas, O ruler of the gods, but especially in the Kaliyuga.

2.2.s:
kalau tu jñānavairāgyau vṛddharūpau nirutsavau |
grāhakābhāvato devi jātau jarjaratāmati ||
2.2.d:
कलौ तु ज्ञानवैराग्यौ वृद्धरूपौ निरुत्सवौ ।
ग्राहकाभावतो देवि जातौ जर्जरतामति ॥
2.2.m: In the Kaliyuga, however, knowledge and dispassion have grown old and lack vitality; / for want of recipients, O goddess, they have become utterly decayed.

2.2.s:
kalau pratyakṣaphaladā bhaktiḥ sarvayugeṣvapi |
tatprabhāvādahaṃ nityaṃ tadvaśo nātra saṃśayaḥ ||
2.2.d:
कलौ प्रत्यक्षफलदा भक्तिः सर्वयुगेष्वपि ।
तत्प्रभावादहं नित्यं तद्वशो नात्र संशयः ॥
2.2.m: In the Kaliyuga, devotion yields visible fruit, as it does in all yugas; / through its power I am always under its sway—there is no doubt about this.

2.2.s:
yo bhaktimānpumām̐lloke sadāhaṃ tatsahāyakṛt |
vighnahartā ripustasya daṇḍyo nātra ca saṃśayaḥ ||
2.2.d:
यो भक्तिमान्पुमाम्̐ल्लोके सदाहं तत्सहायकृत् ।
विघ्नहर्ता रिपुस्तस्य दण्ड्यो नात्र च संशयः ॥
2.2.m: Whoever is a devotee in the world, I always assist him; / I am the remover of obstacles, and his enemy is to be punished—there is no doubt of this.

2.2.s:
bhaktahetorahaṃ devi kālaṃ krodhapariplutaḥ |
adahaṃ vahninā netrabhavena nijarakṣakaḥ ||
bhaktahetorahaṃ devi ravyuparyabhavaṃ kila |
atikrodhānvitaḥ śūlaṃ gṛhītvānvajayaṃ purā | 43 ||
2.2.d:
भक्तहेतोरहं देवि कालं क्रोधपरिप्लुतः ।
अदहं वह्निना नेत्रभवेन निजरक्षकः ॥
भक्तहेतोरहं देवि रव्युपर्यभवं किल ।
अतिक्रोधान्वितः शूलं गृहीत्वान्वजयं पुरा । 43 ॥
2.2.m:
For the sake of a devotee, O goddess, overwhelmed with fury, / I, the protector of my own, burned Death with the fire born of my eye.

For the sake of a devotee, O goddess, I confronted the Sun; / filled with great wrath, I took up my trident and conquered him in former times.

2.2.s:
bhaktahetorahaṃ devi rāvaṇaṃ sagaṇaṃ krudhā |
tyajāmi sma kṛto naiva pakṣapāto hi tasya vai ||
2.2.d:
भक्तहेतोरहं देवि रावणं सगणं क्रुधा ।
त्यजामि स्म कृतो नैव पक्षपातो हि तस्य वै ॥
2.2.m: For the sake of a devotee, O goddess, I angrily abandoned / Rāvaṇa along with his host; I showed him no partiality at all.

2.2.s:
bhaktahetorahaṃ devi vyāsaṃ hi kumatigraham |
kāśyā nyasārayaṃ krodhāddaṇḍayitvā ca nandinā ||
2.2.d:
भक्तहेतोरहं देवि व्यासं हि कुमतिग्रहम् ।
काश्या न्यसारयं क्रोधाद्दण्डयित्वा च नन्दिना ॥
2.2.m: For the sake of a devotee, O goddess, I angrily expelled Vyāsa, / who was seized by evil counsel, from Kāśī after having him punished by Nandin.

2.2.s:
kiṃ bahūktena deveśi bhaktyādhīnaḥ sadā hyaham |
tatkartuḥ puruṣasyātivaśago nātra saṃśayaḥ ||
2.2.d:
किं बहूक्तेन देवेशि भक्त्याधीनः सदा ह्यहम् ।
तत्कर्तुः पुरुषस्यातिवशगो नात्र संशयः ॥
2.2.m: What more need be said, O ruler of the gods? I am always dependent on devotion; / I am entirely submissive to the person who practices it—there is no doubt about this.

2.2.s:
brahmovāca |
itthamākarṇya bhaktestu mahattvaṃ dakṣajā satī |
jaharṣātīva manasi praṇanāma śivaṃ mudā ||
2.2.d:
ब्रह्मोवाच ।
इत्थमाकर्ण्य भक्तेस्तु महत्त्वं दक्षजा सती ।
जहर्षातीव मनसि प्रणनाम शिवं मुदा ॥
2.2.m: Brahmā said: / Having heard the greatness of devotion in this manner, Satī, Dakṣa’s daughter, / rejoiced exceedingly in her heart and bowed down to Śiva with joy.

2.2.s:
punaḥ papraccha sadbhaktyā tatkāṇḍaviṣayaṃ mune |
śāstraṃ sukhakaraṃ loke jīvoddhāraparāyaṇam ||
2.2.d:
पुनः पप्रच्छ सद्भक्त्या तत्काण्डविषयं मुने ।
शास्त्रं सुखकरं लोके जीवोद्धारपरायणम् ॥
2.2.m: Again, with true devotion, she inquired about the section on that subject, O sage, / the scripture that brings happiness to the world and is dedicated to the salvation of living beings,

2.2.s:
sayantramantraśāstraṃ ca tanmāhātmyaṃ viśeṣataḥ |
anyāni dharmavastūni jīvoddhārakarāṇi hi ||
2.2.d:
सयन्त्रमन्त्रशास्त्रं च तन्माहात्म्यं विशेषतः ।
अन्यानि धर्मवस्तूनि जीवोद्धारकराणि हि ॥
2.2.m: and the scripture of yantras and mantras, especially its eulogy, / and other righteous matters that bring about the salvation of living beings.

2.2.s:
śaṅkaro'pi tadākarṇya satīpraśnaṃ prahṛṣṭadhīḥ |
varṇayāmāsa suprītyā jīvoddhārāya kṛtsnaśaḥ ||
2.2.d:
शङ्करोऽपि तदाकर्ण्य सतीप्रश्नं प्रहृष्टधीः ।
वर्णयामास सुप्रीत्या जीवोद्धाराय कृत्स्नशः ॥
2.2.m: Hearing Satī's question, Śaṅkara too, with a delighted mind, / recounted everything in full with great affection for the salvation of living beings.

2.2.s:
tantraśāstraṃ sayantraṃ hi sapañcāṅgaṃ maheśvaraḥ |
babhāṣe mahimānaṃ ca tattaddevavarasya vai ||
2.2.d:
तन्त्रशास्त्रं सयन्त्रं हि सपञ्चाङ्गं महेश्वरः ।
बभाषे महिमानं च तत्तद्देववरस्य वै ॥
2.2.m: The Great Lord spoke of the Tantra scripture together with yantras and the five limbs, / and the greatness of each respective supreme deity,

2.2.s:
setihāsakathāṃ teṣāṃ bhaktamāhātmyameva ca |
savarṇāśramadharmāṃśca nṛpadharmān munīśvara ||
2.2.d:
सेतिहासकथां तेषां भक्तमाहात्म्यमेव च ।
सवर्णाश्रमधर्मांश्च नृपधर्मान् मुनीश्वर ॥
2.2.m: the historical tales of them, the eulogy of devotees, / the duties of the social classes and stages of life, and the duties of kings, O best of sages,

2.2.s:
sutastrīdharmamāhātmyaṃ varṇāśramamanaśvaram |
vaidyaśāstraṃ tathā jyotiḥśāstraṃ jīvasukhāvaham ||
2.2.d:
सुतस्त्रीधर्ममाहात्म्यं वर्णाश्रममनश्वरम् ।
वैद्यशास्त्रं तथा ज्योतिःशास्त्रं जीवसुखावहम् ॥
2.2.m: the eulogy of the duties of sons and women, the imperishable [order of] classes and stages of life, / medical science, and the science of astrology that brings happiness to living beings.

2.2.s:
sāmudrikaṃ paraṃ śāstramanyacchāstrāṇi bhūriśaḥ |
kṛpāṃ kṛtvā maheśāno varṇayāmāsa tattvataḥ ||
2.2.d:
सामुद्रिकं परं शास्त्रमन्यच्छास्त्राणि भूरिशः ।
कृपां कृत्वा महेशानो वर्णयामास तत्त्वतः ॥
2.2.m: The Great Lord, out of compassion, accurately explained / the supreme science of palmistry and numerous other scriptures.

2.2.s:
itthaṃ trilokasukhadau sarvajñau ca satīśivau |
lokopakārakaraṇadhṛtasadguṇavigrahau ||
2.2.d:
इत्थं त्रिलोकसुखदौ सर्वज्ञौ च सतीशिवौ ।
लोकोपकारकरणधृतसद्गुणविग्रहौ ॥
2.2.m: In this way, Satī and Śiva, who bestow happiness on the three worlds and are omniscient, / assuming forms composed of noble virtues to benefit the world,

2.2.s:
cikrīḍāte bahuvidhaṃ kailāse himavad girau |
anyasthaleṣu ca tadā parabrahmasvarūpiṇau ||
śrīgaṇeśāya namaḥ ||
śrīgaurīśaṅkarābhyāṃ namaḥ ||
śrīśivamahāpurāṇam ||
dvitīyāyāṃ rudrasaṃhitāyāṃ dvitīyaḥ satīkhaṇḍe
2.2.d:
चिक्रीडाते बहुविधं कैलासे हिमवद् गिरौ ।
अन्यस्थलेषु च तदा परब्रह्मस्वरूपिणौ ॥
श्रीगणेशाय नमः ॥
श्रीगौरीशङ्कराभ्यां नमः ॥
श्रीशिवमहापुराणम् ॥
द्वितीयायां रुद्रसंहितायां द्वितीयः सतीखण्डे
2.2.m:
sported in various ways on Kailāsa, on the Himavat mountain, / and in other places at that time, being the very nature of supreme Brahman.

Thus ends the twenty-third chapter, named 'Description of the Power of Devotion,' in the Satī Section, the second [part] of the Rudrasaṃhitā, in the glorious Śivamahāpurāṇa.

2.2.s:
nārada uvāca |
brahman vidhe prajānātha mahāprājña kṛpākara |
śrāvitaṃ śaṅkarayaśaḥ satīśaṅkarayoḥ śubham ||
2.2.d:
नारद उवाच ।
ब्रह्मन् विधे प्रजानाथ महाप्राज्ञ कृपाकर ।
श्रावितं शङ्करयशः सतीशङ्करयोः शुभम् ॥
2.2.m: Nārada said: / O Brahmā, O creator, O lord of creatures, O greatly wise one, O bestower of mercy, / the auspicious fame of Śaṅkara, of Satī and Śaṅkara, has been recited.

2.2.s:
idānīṃ brūhi satprītyā paraṃ tadyaśa uttamam |
kimakārṣṭāṃ hi tatsthau vai caritaṃ dampatī śivau ||
2.2.d:
इदानीं ब्रूहि सत्प्रीत्या परं तद्यश उत्तमम् ।
किमकार्ष्टां हि तत्स्थौ वै चरितं दम्पती शिवौ ॥
2.2.m: Now, with true affection, tell of their supreme, excellent renown; / what deed did the couple, the two auspicious ones residing there, perform?

2.2.s:
brahmovāca |
satīśivacaritraṃ ca śṛṇu me premato mune |
laukikīṃ gatimāśritya cikrīḍāte sadānvaham ||
2.2.d:
ब्रह्मोवाच ।
सतीशिवचरित्रं च शृणु मे प्रेमतो मुने ।
लौकिकीं गतिमाश्रित्य चिक्रीडाते सदान्वहम् ॥
2.2.m: Brahmā said: / Listen with love from me to the conduct of Satī and Śiva, O sage; / adopting worldly conduct, they sported day after day.

2.2.s:
tataḥ satī mahādevī viyogamalabhanmune |
svapataḥ śaṅkarasyeti vadantyeke subuddhayaḥ ||
2.2.d:
ततः सती महादेवी वियोगमलभन्मुने ।
स्वपतः शङ्करस्येति वदन्त्येके सुबुद्धयः ॥
2.2.m: Then Satī, the great goddess, experienced separation, O sage, / while Śaṅkara was sleeping: so say some who possess good intellect.

2.2.s:
vāgarthāviva sampṛktau śaktīśau sarvadā citau |
kathaṃ ghaṭeta ca tayorviyogastattvato mune ||
2.2.d:
वागर्थाविव सम्पृक्तौ शक्तीशौ सर्वदा चितौ ।
कथं घटेत च तयोर्वियोगस्तत्त्वतो मुने ॥
2.2.m: United like word and meaning, Śakti and the Lord, always of the nature of consciousness— / how could separation truly occur between the two, O sage?

2.2.s:
līlārucitvādathavā saṅghaṭetākhilaṃ ca tat |
kurute yadyadīśau ca satīśau bhavarītigau ||
2.2.d:
लीलारुचित्वादथवा सङ्घटेताखिलं च तत् ।
कुरुते यद्यदीशौ च सतीशौ भवरीतिगौ ॥
2.2.m: Or else all that might happen because of their taste for divine play; / whatever the two rulers, Satī and the Lord, do, follows worldly conduct.

2.2.s:
sā tyaktā dakṣajā dṛṣṭvā patinā janakādhvare |
śambhoranādarāttatra dehaṃ tatyāja saṅgatā ||
2.2.d:
सा त्यक्ता दक्षजा दृष्ट्वा पतिना जनकाध्वरे ।
शम्भोरनादरात्तत्र देहं तत्याज सङ्गता ॥
2.2.m: Seeing that she was abandoned by her husband, Dakṣa’s daughter, having gone there, / cast off her body at her father’s sacrifice because of the disrespect shown to Śambhu.

2.2.s:
punarhimālaye saivāvirbhūtā nāmataḥ satī |
pārvatīti śivaṃ prāpa taptvā bhūri vivāhataḥ ||
2.2.d:
पुनर्हिमालये सैवाविर्भूता नामतः सती ।
पार्वतीति शिवं प्राप तप्त्वा भूरि विवाहतः ॥
2.2.m: Again, she herself manifested in the Himālaya by the name of Satī; / as Pārvatī, having practiced intense austerity, she obtained Śiva through marriage.

2.2.s:
sūta uvāca |
ityākarṇya vacastasya brahmaṇaḥ sa tu nāradaḥ |
papraccha ca vidhātāraṃ śivāśivamahadyaśaḥ ||
2.2.d:
सूत उवाच ।
इत्याकर्ण्य वचस्तस्य ब्रह्मणः स तु नारदः ।
पप्रच्छ च विधातारं शिवाशिवमहद्यशः ॥
2.2.m: Sūta said: / Having heard these words of Brahmā, Nārada / questioned the creator about the great glory of Śivā and Śiva.

2.2.s:
nārada uvāca |
viṣṇuśiṣya mahābhāga vidhe me vada vistarāt |
śivāśivacaritraṃ tadbhavācāraparānugam ||
2.2.d:
नारद उवाच ।
विष्णुशिष्य महाभाग विधे मे वद विस्तरात् ।
शिवाशिवचरित्रं तद्भवाचारपरानुगम् ॥
2.2.m: Nārada said: / O disciple of Viṣṇu, O fortunate one, O creator, tell me in detail / the conduct of Śivā and Śiva that conforms to worldly conduct.

2.2.s:
kimarthaṃ śaṅkaro jāyāṃ tatyāja prāṇataḥ priyām |
tasmādācakṣva me tāta vicitramiti manmahe ||
2.2.d:
किमर्थं शङ्करो जायां तत्याज प्राणतः प्रियाम् ।
तस्मादाचक्ष्व मे तात विचित्रमिति मन्महे ॥
2.2.m: For what reason did Śaṅkara abandon his wife, who was dearer to him than life? / Therefore tell me, father; we consider this an extraordinary thing.

2.2.s:
kuto'dhvare'jaḥ putrasyānādaro'bhūcchivasya te |
kathaṃ tatyāja sā dehaṃ gatvā tatra pituḥ kratau ||
2.2.d:
कुतोऽध्वरेऽजः पुत्रस्यानादरोऽभूच्छिवस्य ते ।
कथं तत्याज सा देहं गत्वा तत्र पितुः क्रतौ ॥
2.2.m: Why was your son Śiva disrespected at the sacrifice by the Unborn [Daksha]? / How did she, having gone there to her father's sacrifice, cast off her body?

2.2.s:
tataḥ kimabhavattatra kimakārṣīnmaheśvaraḥ |
tatsarvaṃ me samācakṣva śraddhāyuk tacchrutāvaham ||
2.2.d:
ततः किमभवत्तत्र किमकार्षीन्महेश्वरः ।
तत्सर्वं मे समाचक्ष्व श्रद्धायुक् तच्छ्रुतावहम् ॥
2.2.m: What happened there after that? What did Maheśvara do? / Tell me all that; I am filled with faith to hear it.

2.2.s:
brahmovāca |
śṛṇu tāta paraprītyā munibhiḥ saha nārada |
sutavarya mahāprājña caritaṃ śaśimaulinaḥ ||
2.2.d:
ब्रह्मोवाच ।
शृणु तात परप्रीत्या मुनिभिः सह नारद ।
सुतवर्य महाप्राज्ञ चरितं शशिमौलिनः ॥
2.2.m: Brahmā said: / Listen with great love together with the sages, Nārada, / O best of sons, O greatly wise one, to the deeds of the moon-crested lord.

2.2.s:
namaskṛtya maheśānaṃ haryādisurasevitam |
parabrahma pravakṣyāmi taccaritraṃ mahādbhutam ||
2.2.d:
नमस्कृत्य महेशानं हर्यादिसुरसेवितम् ।
परब्रह्म प्रवक्ष्यामि तच्चरित्रं महाद्भुतम् ॥
2.2.m: Having bowed to Maheśāna, who is served by Hari and the other gods, / the Supreme Brahman, I shall narrate his exceedingly wonderful deeds.

2.2.s:
sarveyaṃ śivalīlā hi bahulīlākaraḥ prabhuḥ |
svatantro nirvikārī ca satī sāpi hi tadvidhā ||
2.2.d:
सर्वेयं शिवलीला हि बहुलीलाकरः प्रभुः ।
स्वतन्त्रो निर्विकारी च सती सापि हि तद्विधा ॥
2.2.m: Indeed, all this is Śiva's divine play; the lord performs manifold play, / independent and changeless; and Satī too is of the same nature.

2.2.s:
anyathā kaḥ samartho hi tatkarmakaraṇe mune |
paramātmā parabrahma sa eva parameśvaraḥ ||
2.2.d:
अन्यथा कः समर्थो हि तत्कर्मकरणे मुने ।
परमात्मा परब्रह्म स एव परमेश्वरः ॥
2.2.m: Otherwise, who indeed is capable of performing such acts, O sage? / He alone is the Supreme Self, the Supreme Brahman, the Parameśvara,

2.2.s:
yaṃ sadā bhajate śrīśo'haṃ cāpi sakalāḥ surāḥ |
munayaśca mahātmānaḥ siddhāśca sanakādayaḥ ||
2.2.d:
यं सदा भजते श्रीशोऽहं चापि सकलाः सुराः ।
मुनयश्च महात्मानः सिद्धाश्च सनकादयः ॥
2.2.m: Whom the Lord of Śrī, and I, and all the gods constantly worship, / as well as the high-souled sages, and the perfected ones headed by Sanaka;

2.2.s:
śeṣaḥ sadā yaśo yasya mudā gāyati nityaśaḥ |
pāraṃ na labhate tāta sa prabhuḥ śaṅkaraḥ śivaḥ ||
2.2.d:
शेषः सदा यशो यस्य मुदा गायति नित्यशः ।
पारं न लभते तात स प्रभुः शङ्करः शिवः ॥
2.2.m: Whose glory Śeṣa always sings daily with joy, / yet does not reach its end, father; he is the Lord Śaṅkara, Śiva.

2.2.s:
tasyaiva līlayā sarvo'yamiti tattvavibhramaḥ |
tatra doṣo na kasyāpi sarvavyāpī sa prerakaḥ ||
2.2.d:
तस्यैव लीलया सर्वोऽयमिति तत्त्वविभ्रमः ।
तत्र दोषो न कस्यापि सर्वव्यापी स प्रेरकः ॥
2.2.m: It is solely through his divine play that all this confusion regarding true reality occurs; / no fault lies with anyone there; he is the all-pervading instigator.

2.2.s:
ekasminsamaye rudraḥ satyā tribhavane bhavaḥ |
vṛṣamāruhya paryāṭadrasāṃ līlāviśāradaḥ ||
2.2.d:
एकस्मिन्समये रुद्रः सत्या त्रिभवने भवः ।
वृषमारुह्य पर्याटद्रसां लीलाविशारदः ॥
2.2.m: At one time, Rudra, the Bhava of the three worlds, skilled in divine play, / mounted his bull and roamed the earth together with Satī.

2.2.s:
āgatya daṇḍakāraṇyaṃ paryaṭan sāgarāmbarām |
darśayan tatragāṃ śobhāṃ satyai satyapaṇaḥ prabhuḥ ||
2.2.d:
आगत्य दण्डकारण्यं पर्यटन् सागराम्बराम् ।
दर्शयन् तत्रगां शोभां सत्यै सत्यपणः प्रभुः ॥
2.2.m: Having come to the Daṇḍaka forest while wandering over the ocean-clad earth, / the lord whose promise is truth showed Satī the splendor found there.

2.2.s:
tatra rāmaṃ dadarśāsau lakṣmaṇenānvitaṃ haraḥ |
anviṣyantaṃ priyāṃ sītāṃ rāvaṇena hṛtāṃ chalāt ||
2.2.d:
तत्र रामं ददर्शासौ लक्ष्मणेनान्वितं हरः ।
अन्विष्यन्तं प्रियां सीतां रावणेन हृतां छलात् ॥
2.2.m: There Hara saw Rāma accompanied by Lakṣmaṇa, / searching for his beloved Sītā, who had been abducted deceitfully by Rāvaṇa,

2.2.s:
hā sīteti proccarantaṃ virahāviṣṭamānasam |
yatastataśca paśyantaṃ rudantaṃ hi muhurmuhuḥ ||
2.2.d:
हा सीतेति प्रोच्चरन्तं विरहाविष्टमानसम् ।
यतस्ततश्च पश्यन्तं रुदन्तं हि मुहुर्मुहुः ॥
2.2.m: Crying out aloud, "Ah, Sītā!", his mind possessed by the pain of separation, / looking this way and that, and weeping again and again,

2.2.s:
samicchantaṃ ca tatprāptiṃ pṛcchantaṃ tadgatiṃ hṛdā |
kujādibhyo naṣṭadhiyamatrapaṃ śokavihvalam ||
2.2.d:
समिच्छन्तं च तत्प्राप्तिं पृच्छन्तं तद्गतिं हृदा ।
कुजादिभ्यो नष्टधियमत्रपं शोकविह्वलम् ॥
2.2.m: Longing to recover her, inquiring in his heart of her whereabouts / from trees and the like, his mind distraught, unashamed, overwhelmed by grief,

2.2.s:
sūryavaṃśodbhavaṃ vīraṃ bhūpaṃ daśarathātmajam |
bharatāgrajamānandarahitaṃ vigataprabham ||
2.2.d:
सूर्यवंशोद्भवं वीरं भूपं दशरथात्मजम् ।
भरताग्रजमानन्दरहितं विगतप्रभम् ॥
2.2.m: The heroic king born in the solar lineage, Daśaratha's son, / the elder brother of Bharata, devoid of joy and robbed of his luster.

2.2.s:
pūrṇakāmo varādhīnaṃ prāṇamatsma mudā haraḥ |
rāmaṃ bhramantaṃ vipine salakṣmaṇamudāradhīḥ ||
2.2.d:
पूर्णकामो वराधीनं प्राणमत्स्म मुदा हरः ।
रामं भ्रमन्तं विपिने सलक्ष्मणमुदारधीः ॥
2.2.m: Hara, whose desires are fulfilled, with noble mind, joyfully bowed / to Rāma, who was subject to a boon, as he roamed the forest with Lakṣmaṇa.

2.2.s:
jayetyuktvānyato'gacchannadāttasmai svadarśanam |
rāmāya vipine tasmin śaṅkaro bhaktavatsalaḥ ||
2.2.d:
जयेत्युक्त्वान्यतोऽगच्छन्नदात्तस्मै स्वदर्शनम् ।
रामाय विपिने तस्मिन् शङ्करो भक्तवत्सलः ॥
2.2.m: Saying "Victory!", Śaṅkara, who is affectionate toward devotees, went elsewhere / without revealing himself to Rāma in that forest.

2.2.s:
itīdṛśīṃ satī dṛṣṭvā śivalīlāṃ vimohanīm |
suvismitā śivaṃ prāha śivamāyāvimohitā ||
2.2.d:
इतीदृशीं सती दृष्ट्वा शिवलीलां विमोहनीम् ।
सुविस्मिता शिवं प्राह शिवमायाविमोहिता ॥
2.2.m: Seeing such a deluding divine play of Śiva, Satī, / greatly astonished and bewildered by Śiva's māyā, spoke to Śiva:

2.2.s:
satyuvāca |
devadeva parabrahma sarveśa parameśvara |
sevante tvāṃ sadā sarve haribrahmādayaḥ surāḥ ||
2.2.d:
सत्युवाच ।
देवदेव परब्रह्म सर्वेश परमेश्वर ।
सेवन्ते त्वां सदा सर्वे हरिब्रह्मादयः सुराः ॥
2.2.m: Satī said: / O God of gods, Supreme Brahman, Lord of all, Parameśvara, / all the gods headed by Hari and Brahmā constantly serve you.

2.2.s:
tvaṃ praṇamyo hi sarveṣāṃ sevyo dhyeyaśca sarvadā |
vedāntavedyo yatnena nirvikārī paraprabhuḥ ||
2.2.d:
त्वं प्रणम्यो हि सर्वेषां सेव्यो ध्येयश्च सर्वदा ।
वेदान्तवेद्यो यत्नेन निर्विकारी परप्रभुः ॥
2.2.m: Indeed, you are to be bowed to, served, and meditated upon by all at all times; / known through the Vedānta with effort, changeless, the supreme Lord.

2.2.s:
kāvimau puruṣau nātha virahavyākulākṛtī |
vicarantau vane kliṣṭau dīnau vīrau dhanurdharau ||
2.2.d:
काविमौ पुरुषौ नाथ विरहव्याकुलाकृती ।
विचरन्तौ वने क्लिष्टौ दीनौ वीरौ धनुर्धरौ ॥
2.2.m: Who are these two men, O lord, appearing distraught by separation, / wandering in the forest, afflicted, wretched, [yet] heroic bowmen?

2.2.s:
tayorjyeṣṭhaṃ kañjaśyāmaṃ dṛṣṭvā vai kena hetunā |
muditaḥ suprasannātmābhavo bhakta ivādhunā ||
2.2.d:
तयोर्ज्येष्ठं कञ्जश्यामं दृष्ट्वा वै केन हेतुना ।
मुदितः सुप्रसन्नात्माभवो भक्त इवाधुना ॥
2.2.m: Having seen the elder of the two, dark as a lotus, for what reason / have you now become delighted, with a thoroughly joyful mind, like a devotee?

2.2.s:
iti me saṃśayaṃ svāmin śaṅkara chettumarhasi |
sevyasya sevake naiva ghaṭate praṇatiḥ prabho ||
2.2.d:
इति मे संशयं स्वामिन् शङ्कर छेत्तुमर्हसि ।
सेव्यस्य सेवके नैव घटते प्रणतिः प्रभो ॥
2.2.m: O Lord Śaṅkara, you ought to dispel this doubt of mine; / O lord, an obeisance by the one who is worshipped to a servant is never fitting.

2.2.s:
brahmovāca |
ādiśaktiḥ satī devī śivā sā parameśvarī |
śivamāyāvaśī bhūtvā papracchetthaṃ śivaṃ prabhum ||
2.2.d:
ब्रह्मोवाच ।
आदिशक्तिः सती देवी शिवा सा परमेश्वरी ।
शिवमायावशी भूत्वा पप्रच्छेत्थं शिवं प्रभुम् ॥
2.2.m: Brahmā said: / The goddess Satī, the Primordial Energy, Śivā, the Supreme Mistress, / having fallen under the power of Śiva's māyā, thus questioned Lord Śiva.

2.2.s:
tadākarṇya vacaḥ satyāḥ śaṅkaraḥ parameśvaraḥ |
tadā vihasya sa prāha satīṃ līlāviśāradaḥ ||
2.2.d:
तदाकर्ण्य वचः सत्याः शङ्करः परमेश्वरः ।
तदा विहस्य स प्राह सतीं लीलाविशारदः ॥
2.2.m: Hearing those words of Satī, Śaṅkara, the Parameśvara, / skilled in divine play, then smiled and spoke to Satī:

2.2.s:
parameśvara uvāca |
śṛṇu devi sati prītyā yathārthaṃ vacmi nacchalam |
varadānaprabhāvāttu praṇāmaṃ caivamādarāt ||
2.2.d:
परमेश्वर उवाच ।
शृणु देवि सति प्रीत्या यथार्थं वच्मि नच्छलम् ।
वरदानप्रभावात्तु प्रणामं चैवमादरात् ॥
2.2.m: Parameśvara said: / Listen with love, O goddess Satī, I speak the truth without deception; / but it is by the power of granting a boon that such an obeisance was made with respect.

2.2.s:
rāmalakṣmaṇanāmānau bhrātarau vīrasammatau |
sūryavaṃśodbhavau devi prājñau daśarathātmajau ||
2.2.d:
रामलक्ष्मणनामानौ भ्रातरौ वीरसम्मतौ ।
सूर्यवंशोद्भवौ देवि प्राज्ञौ दशरथात्मजौ ॥
2.2.m: The two brothers named Rāma and Lakṣmaṇa are esteemed heroes; / born of the solar race, O goddess, they are the wise sons of Daśaratha.

2.2.s:
gauravarṇau laghurbandhuḥ śeṣeśo lakṣmaṇābhidhaḥ |
jyeṣṭho rāmābhidho viṣṇuḥ pūrṇāṃśo nirupadravaḥ ||
2.2.d:
गौरवर्णौ लघुर्बन्धुः शेषेशो लक्ष्मणाभिधः ।
ज्येष्ठो रामाभिधो विष्णुः पूर्णांशो निरुपद्रवः ॥
2.2.m: The younger brother named Lakṣmaṇa is fair in complexion, the Lord Śeṣa; / the elder, named Rāma, is Viṣṇu, a complete portion, free from afflictions.

2.2.s:
avatīrṇaḥ kṣitau sādhurakṣaṇāya bhavāya naḥ |
ityuktvā virarāmāsau śambhuḥ sūtikaraḥ prabhuḥ ||
2.2.d:
अवतीर्णः क्षितौ साधुरक्षणाय भवाय नः ।
इत्युक्त्वा विररामासौ शम्भुः सूतिकरः प्रभुः ॥
2.2.m: He has descended to the earth for the protection of the virtuous and for our welfare. / Having spoken thus, the lord Sambhu, the author of creation, paused.

2.2.s:
śrutvāpītthaṃ vacaḥ śambhorna viśaśvāsa tanmanaḥ |
śivamāyā balavatī saiva trailokyamohinī ||
2.2.d:
श्रुत्वापीत्थं वचः शम्भोर्न विशश्वास तन्मनः ।
शिवमाया बलवती सैव त्रैलोक्यमोहिनी ॥
2.2.m: Even having heard such words of Śambhu, her mind did not believe; / Śiva's māyā is powerful, and it deludes the three worlds.

2.2.s:
aviśvastaṃ mano jñātvā tasyāḥ śambhuḥ sanātanaḥ |
avocadvacanaṃ ceti prabhurlīlāviśāradaḥ ||
2.2.d:
अविश्वस्तं मनो ज्ञात्वा तस्याः शम्भुः सनातनः ।
अवोचद्वचनं चेति प्रभुर्लीलाविशारदः ॥
2.2.m: Knowing her mind to be unconvinced, the eternal Śambhu, / the lord skilled in divine play, spoke these words:

2.2.s:
śiva uvāca |
śṛṇu madvacanaṃ devi na viśvasiti cenmanaḥ |
tava rāmaparikṣāṃ hi kuru tatra svayā dhiyā ||
2.2.d:
शिव उवाच ।
शृणु मद्वचनं देवि न विश्वसिति चेन्मनः ।
तव रामपरिक्षां हि कुरु तत्र स्वया धिया ॥
2.2.m: Śiva said: / Listen to my words, O goddess: if your mind does not believe, / then test Rāma yourself with your own intellect.

2.2.s:
vinaśyati yathā mohastatkuru tvaṃ sati priye |
gatvā tatra sthitastāvad vaṭe bhava parīkṣikā ||
2.2.d:
विनश्यति यथा मोहस्तत्कुरु त्वं सति प्रिये ।
गत्वा तत्र स्थितस्तावद् वटे भव परीक्षिका ॥
2.2.m: Act so that your delusion may be destroyed, O dear Satī; / having gone there while I remain at the banyan tree, test him.

2.2.s:
brahmovāca |
śivājñayā satī tatra gatvācintayadīśvarī |
kuryāṃ parīkṣāṃ ca kathaṃ rāmasya vanacāriṇaḥ ||
2.2.d:
ब्रह्मोवाच ।
शिवाज्ञया सती तत्र गत्वाचिन्तयदीश्वरी ।
कुर्यां परीक्षां च कथं रामस्य वनचारिणः ॥
2.2.m: Brahmā said: / By Śiva's command, the goddess Satī went there and thought: / "How shall I test Rāma who wanders the forest?

2.2.s:
sītārūpamahaṃ dhṛtvā gaccheyaṃ rāmasannidhau |
yadi rāmo hariḥ sarvaṃ vijñāsyati na cānyathā ||
2.2.d:
सीतारूपमहं धृत्वा गच्छेयं रामसन्निधौ ।
यदि रामो हरिः सर्वं विज्ञास्यति न चान्यथा ॥
2.2.m: Assuming the form of Sītā, I shall go near Rāma; / if Rāma is Hari, he will know everything, and not otherwise."

2.2.s:
itthaṃ vicārya sītā sā bhūtvā rāmasamīpataḥ |
agamattatparīkṣārthaṃ satī mohaparāyaṇā ||
2.2.d:
इत्थं विचार्य सीता सा भूत्वा रामसमीपतः ।
अगमत्तत्परीक्षार्थं सती मोहपरायणा ॥
2.2.m: Having thus considered and assumed the form of Sītā, Satī, / intent on her delusion, went near Rāma in order to test him.

2.2.s:
sītārūpāṃ satīṃ dṛṣṭvā japannāma śiveti ca |
vihasya tatpravijñāya natvāvocad raghūdvahaḥ ||
2.2.d:
सीतारूपां सतीं दृष्ट्वा जपन्नाम शिवेति च ।
विहस्य तत्प्रविज्ञाय नत्वावोचद् रघूद्वहः ॥
2.2.m: Seeing Satī in the form of Sītā, repeating the name "Śiva", / the descendant of Raghu smiled, understood, bowed, and said:

2.2.s:
śrīrāma uvāca |
prematastvaṃ sati brūhi kva śambhuste namo gataḥ |
ekākī vipine kasmādāgatā patinā vinā ||
2.2.d:
श्रीराम उवाच ।
प्रेमतस्त्वं सति ब्रूहि क्व शम्भुस्ते नमो गतः ।
एकाकी विपिने कस्मादागता पतिना विना ॥
2.2.m: Śrī Rāma said: / Tell me with affection, O Satī, where has your Śambhu gone? Salutations to you. / Why have you come alone to the forest without your husband?

2.2.s:
tyaktvā svarūpaṃ kasmātte dhṛtaṃ rūpamidaṃ sati |
brūhi tatkāraṇaṃ devi kṛpāṃ kṛtvā mamopari ||
2.2.d:
त्यक्त्वा स्वरूपं कस्मात्ते धृतं रूपमिदं सति ।
ब्रूहि तत्कारणं देवि कृपां कृत्वा ममोपरि ॥
2.2.m: Having cast off your own form, why have you assumed this form, O Satī? / Tell me the reason for that, O goddess, having taken pity on me.

2.2.s:
brahmovāca |
iti rāmavacaḥ śrutvā cakitāsītsatī tadā |
smṛtvā śivoktaṃ matvā cāvitathaṃ lajjitā bhṛśam ||
2.2.d:
ब्रह्मोवाच ।
इति रामवचः श्रुत्वा चकितासीत्सती तदा ।
स्मृत्वा शिवोक्तं मत्वा चावितथं लज्जिता भृशम् ॥
2.2.m: Brahmā said: / Hearing these words of Rāma, Satī was then astonished; / remembering what Śiva had said and knowing it to be true, she was greatly ashamed.

2.2.s:
rāmaṃ vijñāya viṣṇuṃ taṃ svarūpaṃ saṃvidhāya ca |
smṛtvā śivapadaṃ citte satyuvāca prasannadhīḥ ||
2.2.d:
रामं विज्ञाय विष्णुं तं स्वरूपं संविधाय च ।
स्मृत्वा शिवपदं चित्ते सत्युवाच प्रसन्नधीः ॥
2.2.m: Recognizing that Rāma was Viṣṇu, reassuming her own form, / and remembering the feet of Śiva in her heart, Satī spoke with a serene mind:

2.2.s:
śivo mayā gaṇaiścaiva paryaṭan vasudhāṃ prabhuḥ |
ihāgacchacca vipine svatantraḥ parameśvaraḥ ||
2.2.d:
शिवो मया गणैश्चैव पर्यटन् वसुधां प्रभुः ।
इहागच्छच्च विपिने स्वतन्त्रः परमेश्वरः ॥
2.2.m: "Lord Śiva, the independent Parameśvara, roaming the earth / along with me and his attendants, came here to the forest.

2.2.s:
apaśyadatra sa tvāṃ hi sītānveṣaṇatatparam |
salakṣmaṇaṃ virahiṇaṃ sītayā kliṣṭamānasam ||
2.2.d:
अपश्यदत्र स त्वां हि सीतान्वेषणतत्परम् ।
सलक्ष्मणं विरहिणं सीतया क्लिष्टमानसम् ॥
2.2.m: He saw you here, intent on searching for Sītā, / accompanied by Lakṣmaṇa, pining in separation, your mind afflicted by [the loss of] Sītā.

2.2.s:
natvā tvāṃ sa gato mūle vaṭasya sthita eva hi |
praśaṃsan mahimānaṃ te vaiṣṇavaṃ paramaṃ mudā ||
2.2.d:
नत्वा त्वां स गतो मूले वटस्य स्थित एव हि ।
प्रशंसन् महिमानं ते वैष्णवं परमं मुदा ॥
2.2.m: Having bowed to you, he went and stayed at the foot of the banyan tree, / joyfully praising your supreme greatness as Viṣṇu.

2.2.s:
caturbhujaṃ hariṃ tvāṃ no dṛṣṭvaiva mudito'bhavat |
yathedaṃ rūpamamalaṃ paśyannānandamāptavān ||
2.2.d:
चतुर्भुजं हरिं त्वां नो दृष्ट्वैव मुदितोऽभवत् ।
यथेदं रूपममलं पश्यन्नानन्दमाप्तवान् ॥
2.2.m: He was not delighted by seeing you as the four-armed Hari / in the way he found joy upon beholding this spotless form of yours."

2.2.s:
tacchrutvā vacanaṃ śambhorbhramamānīya cetasi |
tadājñayā parīkṣāṃ te kṛtavatyasmi rāghava ||
2.2.d:
तच्छ्रुत्वा वचनं शम्भोर्भ्रममानीय चेतसि ।
तदाज्ञया परीक्षां ते कृतवत्यस्मि राघव ॥
2.2.m: Hearing those words of Śambhu, and having fallen into doubt in my mind, / I tested you, O descendant of Raghu, by his command.

2.2.s:
jñātaṃ me rāma viṣṇustvaṃ dṛṣṭā te prabhutākhilā |
niḥsaṃśayā tadāpi tacchṛṇu tvaṃ ca mahāmate ||
2.2.d:
ज्ञातं मे राम विष्णुस्त्वं दृष्टा ते प्रभुताखिला ।
निःसंशया तदापि तच्छृणु त्वं च महामते ॥
2.2.m: I know, O Rāma, that you are Viṣṇu; all your lordship has been seen [by me]. / Yet, [even so], listen to this, O highly intelligent one, so that I may be free from doubt:

2.2.s:
kathaṃ praṇamyastvaṃ tasya satyaṃ brūhi mamāgrataḥ |
kuru niḥsaṃśayāṃ tvaṃ māṃ śamalaṃ prāpnuhi drutam ||
2.2.d:
कथं प्रणम्यस्त्वं तस्य सत्यं ब्रूहि ममाग्रतः ।
कुरु निःसंशयां त्वं मां शमलं प्राप्नुहि द्रुतम् ॥
2.2.m: How is it that you are to be bowed to by him? Speak the truth before me! / Make me free from doubt, and quickly relieve [my] agitation.

2.2.s:
brahmovāca |
ityākarṇya vacastasyā rāmaścotphullalocanaḥ |
asmaratsvaṃ prabhuṃ śambhuṃ premābhūd hṛdi cādhikam ||
2.2.d:
ब्रह्मोवाच ।
इत्याकर्ण्य वचस्तस्या रामश्चोत्फुल्ललोचनः ।
अस्मरत्स्वं प्रभुं शम्भुं प्रेमाभूद् हृदि चाधिकम् ॥
2.2.m: Brahmā said: / Hearing her words, Rāma, his eyes blooming [wide], / remembered his lord Śambhu, and devotion increased even more in his heart.

2.2.s:
satyā vinājñayā śambhusamīpaṃ nāgamanmune |
saṃvarṇya mahimānaṃ ca prāvocadrāghavaḥ satīm ||
śrīgaṇeśāya namaḥ ||
śrīgaurīśaṅkarābhyāṃ namaḥ ||
śrīśivamahāpurāṇam ||
dvitīyāyāṃ rudrasaṃhitāyāṃ dvitīyaḥ satīkhaṇḍe
2.2.d:
सत्या विनाज्ञया शम्भुसमीपं नागमन्मुने ।
संवर्ण्य महिमानं च प्रावोचद्राघवः सतीम् ॥
श्रीगणेशाय नमः ॥
श्रीगौरीशङ्कराभ्यां नमः ॥
श्रीशिवमहापुराणम् ॥
द्वितीयायां रुद्रसंहितायां द्वितीयः सतीखण्डे
2.2.m:
He did not go near Śambhu without Satī's permission, O sage; / and, recounting his majesty, the descendant of Raghu spoke to Satī:

Thus ends the twenty-fourth chapter, entitled "The Account of the Testing of Rāma," in the second section, the Satīkhaṇḍa, of the second Rudrasaṃhitā in the glorious Śivamahāpurāṇa.

2.2.s:
śrīrāma uvāca |
ekadā hi purā devi śambhuḥ paramasūtikṛt |
viśvakarmāṇamāhūya svaloke parataḥ pare ||
2.2.d:
श्रीराम उवाच ।
एकदा हि पुरा देवि शम्भुः परमसूतिकृत् ।
विश्वकर्माणमाहूय स्वलोके परतः परे ॥
2.2.m: The glorious Rāma said: / Once long ago, O goddess, Śambhu, the supreme creator, / summoned Viśvakarman in his own realm beyond the highest.

2.2.s:
tena svadhenuśālāyāṃ kārayāmāsa vistṛtam |
ramyaṃ ca bhavanaṃ samyak tatra siṃhāsanaṃ varam ||
2.2.d:
तेन स्वधेनुशालायां कारयामास विस्तृतम् ।
रम्यं च भवनं सम्यक् तत्र सिंहासनं वरम् ॥
2.2.m: By him he had a vast and beautiful mansion properly built / in his own cowshed, and an excellent lion-throne therein.

2.2.s:
tatra cchatraṃ mahādivyaṃ sarvadādbhutamuttamam |
kārayāmāsa vighnārthaṃ śaṅkaro viśvakarmaṇā ||
2.2.d:
तत्र च्छत्रं महादिव्यं सर्वदाद्भुतमुत्तमम् ।
कारयामास विघ्नार्थं शङ्करो विश्वकर्मणा ॥
2.2.m: Śaṅkara had Viśvakarman make there a most celestial umbrella, / ever wonderful and supreme, for the sake of warding off obstacles.

2.2.s:
śakrādīnāṃ juhāvāśu samastān devatāgaṇān |
siddhagandharvanāgādīnupadevāṃśca kṛtsnaśaḥ ||
2.2.d:
शक्रादीनां जुहावाशु समस्तान् देवतागणान् ।
सिद्धगन्धर्वनागादीनुपदेवांश्च कृत्स्नशः ॥
2.2.m: He quickly summoned all the hosts of gods headed by Śakra, / and the Siddhas, Gandharvas, Nāgas, and all the minor gods without exception;

2.2.s:
devān sarvānāgamāṃśca vidhiputrān munīnapi |
devīḥ sarvā apsarobhirnānāvastusamanvitāḥ ||
2.2.d:
देवान् सर्वानागमांश्च विधिपुत्रान् मुनीनपि ।
देवीः सर्वा अप्सरोभिर्नानावस्तुसमन्विताः ॥
2.2.m: all the gods, the Āgamas, the sons of Brahmā, and the sages, / and all the goddesses accompanied by Apsarases, endowed with various objects.

2.2.s:
devānāṃ ca tatharṣīṇāṃ siddhānāṃ phaṇināmapi |
ānayan maṅgalakarāḥ kanyāḥ ṣoḍaśa ṣoḍaśa ||
2.2.d:
देवानां च तथर्षीणां सिद्धानां फणिनामपि ।
आनयन् मङ्गलकराः कन्याः षोडश षोडश ॥
2.2.m: They brought sixteen auspicious maidens each / belonging to the gods, the sages, the Siddhas, and the serpents.

2.2.s:
vīṇāmṛdaṅgapramukhavādyānnānāvidhān mune |
utsavaṃ kārayāmāsa vādayitvā sugāyanaiḥ ||
rājābhiṣekayogyāni dravyāṇi sakalauṣadhaiḥ pratyakṣatīrthapāthobhiḥ pañcakumbhāṃśca pūritān | 8 ||
2.2.d:
वीणामृदङ्गप्रमुखवाद्यान्नानाविधान् मुने ।
उत्सवं कारयामास वादयित्वा सुगायनैः ॥
राजाभिषेकयोग्यानि द्रव्याणि सकलौषधैः प्रत्यक्षतीर्थपाथोभिः पञ्चकुम्भांश्च पूरितान् । 8 ॥
2.2.m:
Various musical instruments, headed by the lute and the mṛdaṅga drum, O sage, / he caused to be played by fine singers, making a festival.

Materials fit for a royal consecration, with all medicinal herbs, / and five pitchers filled with waters from visible holy places—

2.2.s:
tathānyāḥ saṃvidhā divyā ānayatsvagaṇaistadā |
brahmaghoṣaṃ mahārāvaṃ kārayāmāsa śaṅkaraḥ ||
2.2.d:
तथान्याः संविधा दिव्या आनयत्स्वगणैस्तदा ।
ब्रह्मघोषं महारावं कारयामास शङ्करः ॥
2.2.m: and other divine provisions he then had brought by his attendants; / and Śaṅkara had the great roar of chanting the Veda resound.

2.2.s:
atho hariṃ samāhūya vaikuṇṭhātprītamānasaḥ |
tadbhaktyā pūrṇayā devi modati sma maheśvaraḥ ||
2.2.d:
अथो हरिं समाहूय वैकुण्ठात्प्रीतमानसः ।
तद्भक्त्या पूर्णया देवि मोदति स्म महेश्वरः ॥
2.2.m: Then, having summoned Hari from Vaikuṇṭha with a delighted mind, / Maheśvara rejoiced, O goddess, in full devotion to him.

2.2.s:
sumuhūrte mahādevastatra siṃhāsane vare |
upaveśya hariṃ prītyā bhūṣayāmāsa sarvaśaḥ ||
2.2.d:
सुमुहूर्ते महादेवस्तत्र सिंहासने वरे ।
उपवेश्य हरिं प्रीत्या भूषयामास सर्वशः ॥
2.2.m: At an auspicious hour Mahādeva, having affectionately seated Hari / on that excellent throne, adorned him completely.

2.2.s:
ābaddharamyamukuṭaṃ kṛtakautukamaṅgalam |
abhyaṣiñcanmaheśastu svayaṃ brahmāṇḍamaṇḍape ||
2.2.d:
आबद्धरम्यमुकुटं कृतकौतुकमङ्गलम् ।
अभ्यषिञ्चन्महेशस्तु स्वयं ब्रह्माण्डमण्डपे ॥
2.2.m: With an attractive diadem bound on, and auspicious rites of curious wonder performed, / Maheśa himself consecrated [him] in the pavilion of the universe.

2.2.s:
dattavānnikhilaiśvaryaṃ yannaijaṃ nānyagāmi yat |
tatastuṣṭāva taṃ śambhuḥ svatantro bhaktavatsalaḥ ||
2.2.d:
दत्तवान्निखिलैश्वर्यं यन्नैजं नान्यगामि यत् ।
ततस्तुष्टाव तं शम्भुः स्वतन्त्रो भक्तवत्सलः ॥
2.2.m: He bestowed all sovereign power—his very own, which went to none other; / and then Śambhu, independent and affectionate toward devotees, praised him.

2.2.s:
brahmāṇaṃ lokakartāramavocadvacanaṃ tvidam |
vyāpayansvaṃ varādhīnaṃ svatantraṃ bhaktavatsalaḥ ||
2.2.d:
ब्रह्माणं लोककर्तारमवोचद्वचनं त्विदम् ।
व्यापयन्स्वं वराधीनं स्वतन्त्रं भक्तवत्सलः ॥
2.2.m: He spoke these words to Brahmā, the creator of the world, / displaying his own [sovereignty], obedient to the boon, independent, affectionate toward devotees:

2.2.s:
maheśa uvāca |
ataḥ prabhṛti lokeśa mannideśādayaṃ hariḥ |
mama vandyaḥ svayaṃ viṣṇurjātaḥ sarvaḥ śṛṇoti hi ||
2.2.d:
महेश उवाच ।
अतः प्रभृति लोकेश मन्निदेशादयं हरिः ।
मम वन्द्यः स्वयं विष्णुर्जातः सर्वः शृणोति हि ॥
2.2.m: Maheśa said: / "Henceforth, O lord of the world, by my decree this Hari, / Viṣṇu himself, is worthy of my worship; let everyone hear!

2.2.s:
sarvairdevādibhistāta praṇama tvamamuṃ harim |
varṇayantu hariṃ vedā mamaite māmivājñayā ||
2.2.d:
सर्वैर्देवादिभिस्तात प्रणम त्वममुं हरिम् ।
वर्णयन्तु हरिं वेदा ममैते मामिवाज्ञया ॥
2.2.m: Together with all the gods and others, dear one, bow down to this Hari! / Let these Vedas of mine praise Hari at my command, just as [they praise] me."

2.2.s:
śrīrāma uvāca |
ityuktvātha svayaṃ rudro'namadvai garuḍadhvajam |
viṣṇubhaktiprasannātmā varado bhaktavatsalaḥ ||
2.2.d:
श्रीराम उवाच ।
इत्युक्त्वाथ स्वयं रुद्रोऽनमद्वै गरुडध्वजम् ।
विष्णुभक्तिप्रसन्नात्मा वरदो भक्तवत्सलः ॥
2.2.m: The glorious Rāma said: / Having spoken thus, Rudra himself, the giver of boons, affectionate toward devotees, / his soul pleased with devotion to Viṣṇu, bowed down to the one who has Garuḍa on his banner.

2.2.s:
tato brahmādibhirdevaiḥ sarvarūpasuraistathā |
munisiddhādibhiścaiva vandito'bhūddharistadā ||
2.2.d:
ततो ब्रह्मादिभिर्देवैः सर्वरूपसुरैस्तथा ।
मुनिसिद्धादिभिश्चैव वन्दितोऽभूद्धरिस्तदा ॥
2.2.m: Then Hari was praised by the gods headed by Brahmā, / by all manner of celestials, and by sages, Siddhas, and the like.

2.2.s:
tato maheśo haraye'śaṃsaddiviṣadāṃ puraḥ |
mahāvarān suprasanno dattavān bhaktavatsalaḥ ||
2.2.d:
ततो महेशो हरयेऽशंसद्दिविषदां पुरः ।
महावरान् सुप्रसन्नो दत्तवान् भक्तवत्सलः ॥
2.2.m: Then Maheśa praised Hari in the presence of the dwellers of heaven; / highly pleased, affectionate toward devotees, he gave him great boons.

2.2.s:
maheśa uvāca |
tvaṃ kartā sarvalokānāṃ bhartā hartā madājñayā |
dātā dharmārthakāmānāṃ śāstā durṇayakāriṇām ||
2.2.d:
महेश उवाच ।
त्वं कर्ता सर्वलोकानां भर्ता हर्ता मदाज्ञया ।
दाता धर्मार्थकामानां शास्ता दुर्णयकारिणाम् ॥
2.2.m: Maheśa said: / "You are the creator, maintainer, and destroyer of all worlds by my command, / the giver of virtue, wealth, and desire, the chastiser of those who act unlawfully.

2.2.s:
jagadīśo jagatpūjyo mahābalaparākramaḥ |
ajeyastvaṃ raṇe kvāpi mamāpi hi bhaviṣyasi ||
2.2.d:
जगदीशो जगत्पूज्यो महाबलपराक्रमः ।
अजेयस्त्वं रणे क्वापि ममापि हि भविष्यसि ॥
2.2.m: Lord of the universe, worthy of worship by the universe, possessed of great strength and prowess, / you will be invincible anywhere in battle, even to me.

2.2.s:
śaktitrayaṃ gṛhāṇa tvamicchādi prāpitaṃ mayā |
nānālīlāprabhāvatvaṃ svatantratvaṃ bhavatraye ||
2.2.d:
शक्तित्रयं गृहाण त्वमिच्छादि प्रापितं मया ।
नानालीलाप्रभावत्वं स्वतन्त्रत्वं भवत्रये ॥
2.2.m: Receive the three powers, will and the others, granted by me, / the majesty of various sports, and independence in the three worlds.

2.2.s:
tvaddveṣṭāro hare nūnaṃ mayā śāsyāḥ prayatnataḥ |
tvadbhaktānāṃ mayā viṣṇo deyaṃ nirvāṇamuttamam ||
2.2.d:
त्वद्द्वेष्टारो हरे नूनं मया शास्याः प्रयत्नतः ।
त्वद्भक्तानां मया विष्णो देयं निर्वाणमुत्तमम् ॥
2.2.m: Those who hate you, O Hari, must surely be chastised by me with diligence; / to your devotees, O Viṣṇu, supreme liberation must be given by me.

2.2.s:
māyāṃ cāpi gṛhāṇemāṃ duḥpraṇodyāṃ surādibhiḥ |
yayā sammohitaṃ viśvamacidrūpaṃ bhaviṣyati ||
2.2.d:
मायां चापि गृहाणेमां दुःप्रणोद्यां सुरादिभिः ।
यया सम्मोहितं विश्वमचिद्रूपं भविष्यति ॥
2.2.m: And receive this Maya, hard to be repelled by gods and others, / by which the universe, deluded, will become insentient.

2.2.s:
mama bāhurmadīyastvaṃ dakṣiṇo'sau vidhirhare |
asyāpi hi vidheḥ pātā janitāpi bhaviṣyasi ||
2.2.d:
मम बाहुर्मदीयस्त्वं दक्षिणोऽसौ विधिर्हरे ।
अस्यापि हि विधेः पाता जनितापि भविष्यसि ॥
2.2.m: You are my arm; this right arm of mine is Brahmā, O Hari; / you will be the protector and also the progenitor of this very Brahmā.

2.2.s:
hṛdayaṃ mama yo rudraḥ sa evāhaṃ na saṃśayaḥ |
pūjyastava sadā so'pi brahmādīnāmapi dhruvam ||
2.2.d:
हृदयं मम यो रुद्रः स एवाहं न संशयः ।
पूज्यस्तव सदा सोऽपि ब्रह्मादीनामपि ध्रुवम् ॥
2.2.m: That Rudra who is my heart is indeed myself, there is no doubt; / he too is ever to be worshipped by you, and surely by Brahmā and the others.

2.2.s:
atra sthitvā jagatsarvaṃ pālaya tvaṃ viśeṣataḥ |
nānāvatārabhedaiśca sadā nānotikartṛbhiḥ ||
2.2.d:
अत्र स्थित्वा जगत्सर्वं पालय त्वं विशेषतः ।
नानावतारभेदैश्च सदा नानोतिकर्तृभिः ॥
2.2.m: Remaining here, protect the whole universe especially, / by means of various incarnations that continually perform various acts.

2.2.s:
mama loke tavedaṃ vai sthānaṃ ca paramarddhimat |
goloka iti vikhyātaṃ bhaviṣyati mahojjvalam ||
2.2.d:
मम लोके तवेदं वै स्थानं च परमर्द्धिमत् ।
गोलोक इति विख्यातं भविष्यति महोज्ज्वलम् ॥
2.2.m: This realm of yours in my world, supremely prosperous, / will be renowned as Goloka, exceedingly radiant.

2.2.s:
bhaviṣyanti hare ye te'vatārā bhuvi rakṣakāḥ |
madbhaktāstān dhruvaṃ drakṣye prītānatha nijād varāt ||
2.2.d:
भविष्यन्ति हरे ये तेऽवतारा भुवि रक्षकाः ।
मद्भक्तास्तान् ध्रुवं द्रक्ष्ये प्रीतानथ निजाद् वरात् ॥
2.2.m: Whatever incarnations of yours protect the earth, O Hari, / those devotees of mine I shall surely look upon, pleased by my own boon."

2.2.s:
śrīrāma uvāca |
akhaṇḍaiśvaryamāsādya hareritthaṃ haraḥ svayam |
kailāse svagaṇaistasmin svairaṃ krīḍatyumāpatiḥ ||
2.2.d:
श्रीराम उवाच ।
अखण्डैश्वर्यमासाद्य हरेरित्थं हरः स्वयम् ।
कैलासे स्वगणैस्तस्मिन् स्वैरं क्रीडत्युमापतिः ॥
2.2.m: The glorious Rāma said: / Having thus conferred undivided sovereignty upon Hari, Hara himself, / the lord of Umā, sports freely on that Kailāsa with his attendants.

2.2.s:
tadāprabhṛti lakṣmīśo gopaveṣo'bhavattathā |
ayāsīttatra suprītyā gopagopīgavāṃ patiḥ ||
2.2.d:
तदाप्रभृति लक्ष्मीशो गोपवेषोऽभवत्तथा ।
अयासीत्तत्र सुप्रीत्या गोपगोपीगवां पतिः ॥
2.2.m: From that time forth the lord of Lakṣmī took the guise of a cowherd, / and with great delight went there as the lord of the cowherds, cowherdesses, and cows.

2.2.s:
so'pi viṣṇuḥ prasannātmā jugopa nikhilaṃ jagat |
nānāvatārasandhartāvanakartā śivājñayā ||
2.2.d:
सोऽपि विष्णुः प्रसन्नात्मा जुगोप निखिलं जगत् ।
नानावतारसन्धर्तावनकर्ता शिवाज्ञया ॥
2.2.m: Viṣṇu too, joyful in soul, protected the entire universe, / assuming various incarnations and acting as protector by the command of Śiva.

2.2.s:
idānīṃ sa caturddhātrāvātaracchaṅkarājñayā |
rāmo'haṃ tatra bharato lakṣmaṇaḥ śatruheti ca ||
2.2.d:
इदानीं स चतुर्द्धात्रावातरच्छङ्कराज्ञया ।
रामोऽहं तत्र भरतो लक्ष्मणः शत्रुहेति च ॥
2.2.m: Now he has descended here in four forms by the command of Śaṅkara: / I am Rāma, and among them are Bharata, Lakṣmaṇa, and the slayer of foes [Śatrughna].

2.2.s:
atha pitrājñayā devi sasītālakṣmaṇaḥ sati |
āgato'haṃ vane cādya duḥkhito daivato'bhavam ||
2.2.d:
अथ पित्राज्ञया देवि ससीतालक्ष्मणः सति ।
आगतोऽहं वने चाद्य दुःखितो दैवतोऽभवम् ॥
2.2.m: Then, by the command of my father, O goddess, O chaste Satī, with Sītā and Lakṣmaṇa / I came to the forest, and today I have become distressed by destiny.

2.2.s:
niśācareṇa me jāyā hṛtā sīteti kenacit |
anveṣyāmi priyāṃ cātra virahī bandhunā vane ||
2.2.d:
निशाचरेण मे जाया हृता सीतेति केनचित् ।
अन्वेष्यामि प्रियां चात्र विरही बन्धुना वने ॥
2.2.m: My wife Sītā has been abducted by some demon; / separated from her, I search for my beloved here in the forest with my brother.

2.2.s:
darśanaṃ te yadi prāptaṃ sarvathā kuśalaṃ mama |
bhaviṣyati na sandeho mātaste kṛpayā sati ||
2.2.d:
दर्शनं ते यदि प्राप्तं सर्वथा कुशलं मम ।
भविष्यति न सन्देहो मातस्ते कृपया सति ॥
2.2.m: Since sight of you has been attained, my welfare in every way / will come to pass, there is no doubt, O Mother, by your grace, O Satī.

2.2.s:
sītāprāptivaraṃ devi bhaviṣyati na saṃśayaḥ |
taṃ hatvā duḥkhadaṃ pāpaṃ rākṣasaṃ tvadanugrahāt ||
2.2.d:
सीताप्राप्तिवरं देवि भविष्यति न संशयः ।
तं हत्वा दुःखदं पापं राक्षसं त्वदनुग्रहात् ॥
2.2.m: The boon of recovering Sītā will come to pass, O goddess, there is no doubt, / having slain that wicked demon who caused distress, by your favor.

2.2.s:
mahadbhāgyaṃ mamādyaiva yadyakārṣṭāṃ kṛpāṃ yuvām |
yasmin sakaruṇau syātāṃ sa dhanyaḥ puruṣo varaḥ ||
2.2.d:
महद्भाग्यं ममाद्यैव यद्यकार्ष्टां कृपां युवाम् ।
यस्मिन् सकरुणौ स्यातां स धन्यः पुरुषो वरः ॥
2.2.m: Great is my good fortune this very day, since you two have shown mercy; / he upon whom you two are compassionate is blessed, the best of men.

2.2.s:
itthamābhāṣya bahudhā supraṇamya satīṃ śivām |
tadājñayā vane tasmin vicacāra raghūdvahaḥ ||
2.2.d:
इत्थमाभाष्य बहुधा सुप्रणम्य सतीं शिवाम् ।
तदाज्ञया वने तस्मिन् विचचार रघूद्वहः ॥
2.2.m: Having spoken thus in many ways and bowed low to the auspicious Satī, / the scion of Raghu roamed in that forest with her permission.

2.2.s:
athākarṇya satī vākyaṃ rāmasya prayatātmanaḥ |
hṛṣṭābhūtsā praśaṃsantaṃ śivabhaktirataṃ hṛdi ||
2.2.d:
अथाकर्ण्य सती वाक्यं रामस्य प्रयतात्मनः ।
हृष्टाभूत्सा प्रशंसन्तं शिवभक्तिरतं हृदि ॥
2.2.m: Then, hearing the words of Rāma whose self was restrained, / she was delighted at heart by him who praised [Śiva] and was devoted to Śiva's devotion.

2.2.s:
smṛtvā svakarma manasākārṣīcchokaṃ suvistaram |
pratyāgacchadudāsīnā vivarṇā śivasannidhau ||
2.2.d:
स्मृत्वा स्वकर्म मनसाकार्षीच्छोकं सुविस्तरम् ।
प्रत्यागच्छदुदासीना विवर्णा शिवसन्निधौ ॥
2.2.m: Remembering in her mind her own deed, she felt great sorrow; / she returned to Śiva's presence, indifferent and pale.

2.2.s:
pathi sācintayad devī sañcalantī punaḥ punaḥ |
nāṅgīkṛtaṃ śivoktaṃ me rāmaṃ prati kudhīḥ kṛtā ||
2.2.d:
पथि साचिन्तयद् देवी सञ्चलन्ती पुनः पुनः ।
नाङ्गीकृतं शिवोक्तं मे रामं प्रति कुधीः कृता ॥
2.2.m: On the way, walking repeatedly, the goddess thought: / "Śiva's word was not accepted by me; an evil mind was shown toward Rāma.

2.2.s:
kimuttaramahaṃ dāsye gatvā śaṅkarasannidhau |
iti sañcintya bahudhā paścāttāpo'bhavattadā ||
2.2.d:
किमुत्तरमहं दास्ये गत्वा शङ्करसन्निधौ ।
इति सञ्चिन्त्य बहुधा पश्चात्तापोऽभवत्तदा ॥
2.2.m: What answer shall I give when I arrive before Śaṅkara?" / Thinking thus in many ways, repentance then came upon her.

2.2.s:
gatvā śambhusamīpaṃ ca praṇanāma śivaṃ hṛdā |
viṣaṇṇavadanā śokavyākulā vigataprabhā ||
2.2.d:
गत्वा शम्भुसमीपं च प्रणनाम शिवं हृदा ।
विषण्णवदना शोकव्याकुला विगतप्रभा ॥
2.2.m: Approaching Śambhu, she bowed to Śiva with her heart, / with dejected face, bewildered by grief, and bereft of luster.

2.2.s:
atha tāṃ duḥkhitāṃ dṛṣṭvā papraccha kuśalaṃ haraḥ |
provāca vacanaṃ prītyā tatparīkṣā kṛtā katham ||
2.2.d:
अथ तां दुःखितां दृष्ट्वा पप्रच्छ कुशलं हरः ।
प्रोवाच वचनं प्रीत्या तत्परीक्षा कृता कथम् ॥
2.2.m: Then, seeing her distressed, Hara asked after her welfare / and lovingly spoke these words: "How was that test performed?"

2.2.s:
śrutvā śivavaco nāhaṃ kimapi praṇatānanā |
satī śokaviṣaṇṇā sā tasthau tatra samīpataḥ ||
2.2.d:
श्रुत्वा शिववचो नाहं किमपि प्रणतानना ।
सती शोकविषण्णा सा तस्थौ तत्र समीपतः ॥
2.2.m: Hearing Śiva's words, Satī, bowed-faced and dejected with sorrow, / said nothing; she stood there near him.

2.2.s:
atha dhyātvā maheśastu bubodha caritaṃ hṛdā |
dakṣajāyā mahāyogī nānālīlāviśāradaḥ ||
2.2.d:
अथ ध्यात्वा महेशस्तु बुबोध चरितं हृदा ।
दक्षजाया महायोगी नानालीलाविशारदः ॥
2.2.m: Then Maheśa, the great yogin skilled in diverse divine sports, / meditating in his heart, understood the conduct of Dakṣa's daughter.

2.2.s:
sasmāra svapaṇaṃ pūrvaṃ yatkṛtaṃ harikopataḥ |
tatprārthito'tha rudro'sau maryādāpratipālakaḥ ||
2.2.d:
सस्मार स्वपणं पूर्वं यत्कृतं हरिकोपतः ।
तत्प्रार्थितोऽथ रुद्रोऽसौ मर्यादाप्रतिपालकः ॥
2.2.m: He remembered his former vow, which had been made out of anger from Hari; / then that Rudra, who protects proper conduct, was prayed to.

2.2.s:
viṣādo'bhūtprabhostatra manasyevamuvāca ha |
dharmavaktā dharmakartā dharmāvanakaraḥ sadā ||
2.2.d:
विषादोऽभूत्प्रभोस्तत्र मनस्येवमुवाच ह ।
धर्मवक्ता धर्मकर्ता धर्मावनकरः सदा ॥
2.2.m: Despondency arose in the Lord's mind, and he spoke thus: / he who speaks dharma, performs dharma, and ever protects dharma.

2.2.s:
śiva uvāca |
kuryāṃ ceddakṣajāyāṃ hi snehaṃ pūrvaṃ yathā mahān |
naśyenmama paṇaḥ śuddho lokalīlānusāriṇaḥ ||
2.2.d:
शिव उवाच ।
कुर्यां चेद्दक्षजायां हि स्नेहं पूर्वं यथा महान् ।
नश्येन्मम पणः शुद्धो लोकलीलानुसारिणः ॥
2.2.m: Śiva said: / "If I show great affection for Dakṣa's daughter as before, / my pure vow, as one conforming to worldly sport, would perish."

2.2.s:
brahmovāca |
itthaṃ vicārya bahudhā hṛdā tāmatyajatsatīm |
paṇaṃ na nāśayāmāsa vedadharmaprapālakaḥ ||
2.2.d:
ब्रह्मोवाच ।
इत्थं विचार्य बहुधा हृदा तामत्यजत्सतीम् ।
पणं न नाशयामास वेदधर्मप्रपालकः ॥
2.2.m: Brahmā said: / Reflecting thus in many ways in his heart, he abandoned that Satī; / the protector of Vedic dharma did not break his vow.

2.2.s:
tato vihāya manasā satīṃ tāṃ parameśvaraḥ |
jagāma svagiriṃ bhedaṃ jagāvaddhā sa hi prabhuḥ ||
2.2.d:
ततो विहाय मनसा सतीं तां परमेश्वरः ।
जगाम स्वगिरिं भेदं जगावद्धा स हि प्रभुः ॥
2.2.m: Then, abandoning that Satī in his mind, Parameśvara / went to his mountain; for the Lord was truly established in non-duality.

2.2.s:
calantaṃ pathi taṃ vyomavāṇyuvāca maheśvaram |
sarvān saṃśrāvayaṃstatra dakṣajāṃ ca viśeṣataḥ ||
2.2.d:
चलन्तं पथि तं व्योमवाण्युवाच महेश्वरम् ।
सर्वान् संश्रावयंस्तत्र दक्षजां च विशेषतः ॥
2.2.m: As he was walking on the path, a heavenly voice spoke to Maheśvara, / letting everyone hear there, and especially Dakṣa's daughter.

2.2.s:
vyomavāṇyuvāca |
dhanyastvaṃ parameśāna tvatsamo'dya tathā paṇaḥ |
na ko'pyanyastriloke'smin mahāyogī mahāprabhuḥ ||
2.2.d:
व्योमवाण्युवाच ।
धन्यस्त्वं परमेशान त्वत्समोऽद्य तथा पणः ।
न कोऽप्यन्यस्त्रिलोकेऽस्मिन् महायोगी महाप्रभुः ॥
2.2.m: The heavenly voice said: / "Blessed are you, Parameśāna! There is no other vow today like yours; / no one else is such a great yogin and great lord in this three-fold world."

2.2.s:
brahmovāca |
śrutvā vyomavaco devī śivaṃ papraccha viprabhā |
kaṃ paṇaṃ kṛtavānnātha brūhi me parameśvara ||
2.2.d:
ब्रह्मोवाच ।
श्रुत्वा व्योमवचो देवी शिवं पप्रच्छ विप्रभा ।
कं पणं कृतवान्नाथ ब्रूहि मे परमेश्वर ॥
2.2.m: Brahmā said: / Hearing the heavenly voice, the goddess, deprived of luster, asked Śiva: / "What vow did you make, O Lord? Tell me, Parameśvara!"

2.2.s:
iti pṛṣṭo'pi giriśaḥ satyā hitakaraḥ prabhuḥ |
nodvāhaṃ svaṃ paṇaṃ tasyai yat haryagre'karotpurā ||
2.2.d:
इति पृष्टोऽपि गिरिशः सत्या हितकरः प्रभुः ।
नोद्वाहं स्वं पणं तस्यै यत् हर्यग्रेऽकरोत्पुरा ॥
2.2.m: Though asked thus by Satī, Giriśa, the beneficent Lord, / did not reveal to her his vow, which he had formerly made before Hari.

2.2.s:
tadā satī śivaṃ dhyātvā svapatiṃ prāṇavallabham |
sarvaṃ bubodha hetuṃ taṃ priyatyāgamayaṃ mune ||
2.2.d:
तदा सती शिवं ध्यात्वा स्वपतिं प्राणवल्लभम् ।
सर्वं बुबोध हेतुं तं प्रियत्यागमयं मुने ॥
2.2.m: Then Satī, meditating on Śiva, her husband and beloved of her life, / understood the entire reason, O sage, which consisted of the abandonment of his beloved.

2.2.s:
tato'tīva śuśocāśu budhvā sā tyāgamātmanaḥ |
śambhunā dakṣajā tasmānniḥśvasantī muhurmuhuḥ ||
2.2.d:
ततोऽतीव शुशोचाशु बुध्वा सा त्यागमात्मनः ।
शम्भुना दक्षजा तस्मान्निःश्वसन्ती मुहुर्मुहुः ॥
2.2.m: Then, realizing her abandonment by Śambhu, Dakṣa's daughter / grieved exceedingly, sighing repeatedly from that cause.

2.2.s:
śivastasyāḥ samājñāya guptaṃ cakre manobhavam |
satyai paṇaṃ svakīyaṃ hi kathā bahvīrvadan prabhuḥ ||
2.2.d:
शिवस्तस्याः समाज्ञाय गुप्तं चक्रे मनोभवम् ।
सत्यै पणं स्वकीयं हि कथा बह्वीर्वदन् प्रभुः ॥
2.2.m: Knowing her [state], Śiva concealed his mind's feeling / and his vow from Satī, the Lord speaking many tales.

2.2.s:
satyā prāpa sa kailāsaṃ kathayan vividhāḥ kathāḥ |
vare sthitvā nijaṃ rūpaṃ dadhau yogī samādhibhṛt ||
2.2.d:
सत्या प्राप स कैलासं कथयन् विविधाः कथाः ।
वरे स्थित्वा निजं रूपं दधौ योगी समाधिभृत् ॥
2.2.m: Telling various stories, he reached Kailāsa with Satī; / staying in an excellent place, the yogin absorbed in meditation held fast to his own nature.

2.2.s:
tatra tasthau satī dhāmni mahāvyākulamānasā |
na bubodha caritraṃ tatkaścicca śivayormune ||
2.2.d:
तत्र तस्थौ सती धाम्नि महाव्याकुलमानसा ।
न बुबोध चरित्रं तत्कश्चिच्च शिवयोर्मुने ॥
2.2.m: Satī stayed there in the abode, her mind exceedingly agitated; / and no one, O sage, understood that conduct of the two Śivas.

2.2.s:
mahānkālo vyatīyāya tayoritthaṃ mahāmune |
svopāttadehayoḥ prabhvorlokalīlānusāriṇoḥ ||
2.2.d:
महान्कालो व्यतीयाय तयोरित्थं महामुने ।
स्वोपात्तदेहयोः प्रभ्वोर्लोकलीलानुसारिणोः ॥
