sarve yūyaṃ bāliśatvādavadānārthamāgatāḥ |
avadānaṃ prayacchāmi āgacchata mamāntikam ||
2.2.d:
वीरभद्र उवाच ।
सर्वे यूयं बालिशत्वादवदानार्थमागताः ।
अवदानं प्रयच्छामि आगच्छत ममान्तिकम् ॥
2.2.m: Vīrabhadra said: / 'All of you have come out of foolishness to receive your portions; / I shall give the portion! Come near me!

2.2.s:
he śakra he śuce bhāno he śaśin he dhanādhipa |
he pāśapāṇe he vāyo nirṛte yama śeṣa he ||
2.2.d:
हे शक्र हे शुचे भानो हे शशिन् हे धनाधिप ।
हे पाशपाणे हे वायो निरृते यम शेष हे ॥
2.2.m: O Śakra, O Agni, O Sun, O Moon, O Lord of Wealth! / O Bearer of the Noose, O Wind, O Nirṛti, O Yama, O Śeṣa!

2.2.s:
he surāsurasaṅghā hīhaita yūyaṃ vicakṣaṇāḥ |
avadānāni dāsyāmi ātṛptyādyāsatāṃ varān ||
2.2.d:
हे सुरासुरसङ्घा हीहैत यूयं विचक्षणाः ।
अवदानानि दास्यामि आतृप्त्याद्यासतां वरान् ॥
2.2.m: O hosts of gods and asuras, come here, you clever ones! / I will distribute the sacrificial portions; until satiety, receive the best!'

2.2.s:
brahmovāca |
evamuktvā sitairbāṇairjaghānātha ruṣānvitaḥ |
nikhilāṃstān surān sadyo vīrabhadro gaṇāgraṇīḥ |
tairbāṇairnihatāḥsarve vāsavādyāḥ sureśvarāḥ ||
palāyanaparā bhūtvā jagmuste ca diśo daśa |
gateṣu lokapāleṣu vidruteṣu sureṣu ca ||
yajñavāṭopakaṇṭhe hi vīrabhadro'gamad gaṇaiḥ | 39 ||
2.2.d:
ब्रह्मोवाच ।
एवमुक्त्वा सितैर्बाणैर्जघानाथ रुषान्वितः ।
निखिलांस्तान् सुरान् सद्यो वीरभद्रो गणाग्रणीः ।
तैर्बाणैर्निहताःसर्वे वासवाद्याः सुरेश्वराः ॥
पलायनपरा भूत्वा जग्मुस्ते च दिशो दश ।
गतेषु लोकपालेषु विद्रुतेषु सुरेषु च ॥
यज्ञवाटोपकण्ठे हि वीरभद्रोऽगमद् गणैः । 39 ॥
2.2.m:
Brahmā said: / Having spoken thus, filled with wrath, Vīrabhadra, the leader of the attendants, / immediately struck down all those gods with sharp white arrows; / struck by those arrows, all the lords of gods led by Indra,

intent on flight, fled in the ten directions; / when the world-protectors had left and the gods had fled,

Vīrabhadra went with his attendants to the vicinity of the sacrificial enclosure.

2.2.s:
tadā te ṛṣayaḥ sarve subhītā hi rameśvaram |
vijñaptukāmāḥ sahasā śīghramūcurnatā bhṛśam ||
2.2.d:
तदा ते ऋषयः सर्वे सुभीता हि रमेश्वरम् ।
विज्ञप्तुकामाः सहसा शीघ्रमूचुर्नता भृशम् ॥
2.2.m: Then all those sages, thoroughly terrified, wishing to entreat / the Lord of Ramā [Viṣṇu], immediately and hastily spoke, bowing deeply.

2.2.s:
ṛṣaya ūcuḥ |
devadeva ramānātha sarveśvara mahāprabho |
rakṣa yajñaṃ hi dakṣasya yajño'si tvaṃ na saṃśayaḥ ||
2.2.d:
ऋषय ऊचुः ।
देवदेव रमानाथ सर्वेश्वर महाप्रभो ।
रक्ष यज्ञं हि दक्षस्य यज्ञोऽसि त्वं न संशयः ॥
2.2.m: The sages said: / O god of gods, O lord of Ramā, O lord of all, O great lord! / Protect indeed the sacrifice of Dakṣa; you are the sacrifice, there is no doubt.

2.2.s:
yajñakarmā yajñarūpo yajñāṅgo yajñarakṣakaḥ |
rakṣa yajñamato rakṣa tvatto'nyo na hi rakṣakaḥ ||
2.2.d:
यज्ञकर्मा यज्ञरूपो यज्ञाङ्गो यज्ञरक्षकः ।
रक्ष यज्ञमतो रक्ष त्वत्तोऽन्यो न हि रक्षकः ॥
2.2.m: You are the ritual of sacrifice, the form of sacrifice, the limbs of sacrifice, the protector of sacrifice. / Protect, therefore protect the sacrifice! There is no protector other than you.

2.2.s:
brahmovāca |
ityākarṇya vacasteṣāmṛṣīṇāṃ vacanaṃ hariḥ |
yoddhukāmo'bhavadviṣṇurvīrabhadreṇa tena vai ||
2.2.d:
ब्रह्मोवाच ।
इत्याकर्ण्य वचस्तेषामृषीणां वचनं हरिः ।
योद्धुकामोऽभवद्विष्णुर्वीरभद्रेण तेन वै ॥
2.2.m: Brahmā said: / Having heard that speech, the words of those sages, Hari, / [namely] Viṣṇu, became eager to fight with that Vīrabhadra.

2.2.s:
caturbhujaḥ susannaddho cakrāyudhadharaḥ karaiḥ |
mahābalo'maragaṇairyajñavāṭātsa niryayau ||
2.2.d:
चतुर्भुजः सुसन्नद्धो चक्रायुधधरः करैः ।
महाबलोऽमरगणैर्यज्ञवाटात्स निर्ययौ ॥
2.2.m: Four-armed, well-equipped, bearing the discus weapon in his hands, / very powerful, he went forth from the sacrificial arena with the hosts of immortals.

2.2.s:
vīrabhadraḥ śūlapāṇirnānāgaṇasamanvitaḥ |
dadarśa viṣṇuṃ sannaddhaṃ yoddhukāmaṃ mahāprabhum ||
2.2.d:
वीरभद्रः शूलपाणिर्नानागणसमन्वितः ।
ददर्श विष्णुं सन्नद्धं योद्धुकामं महाप्रभुम् ॥
2.2.m: Vīrabhadra, trident in hand, accompanied by diverse attendants, / beheld Viṣṇu, the great lord, equipped and eager to fight.

2.2.s:
taṃ dṛṣṭvā vīrabhadro'bhūd bhrukuṭīkuṭilānanaḥ |
kṛtānta iva pāpiṣṭhaṃ mṛgendra iva vāraṇam ||
2.2.d:
तं दृष्ट्वा वीरभद्रोऽभूद् भ्रुकुटीकुटिलाननः ।
कृतान्त इव पापिष्ठं मृगेन्द्र इव वारणम् ॥
2.2.m: Seeing him, Vīrabhadra became fierce with knit brows, / like Death looking upon a wretched sinner, or a lion upon an elephant.

2.2.s:
tathāvidhaṃ hariṃ dṛṣṭvā vīrabhadro'rimardanaḥ |
avadattvaritaḥ kruddho gaṇairvīraiḥ samāvṛtaḥ ||
2.2.d:
तथाविधं हरिं दृष्ट्वा वीरभद्रोऽरिमर्दनः ।
अवदत्त्वरितः क्रुद्धो गणैर्वीरैः समावृतः ॥
2.2.m: Seeing Hari in such a state, Vīrabhadra, the crusher of foes, / surrounded by valiant attendants, swiftly spoke in anger.

2.2.s:
vīrabhadra uvāca |
re re hare mahādevaśapathollaṅghanaṃ tvayā |
kathamadya kṛtaṃ citte garvaḥ kimabhavattava ||
2.2.d:
वीरभद्र उवाच ।
रे रे हरे महादेवशपथोल्लङ्घनं त्वया ।
कथमद्य कृतं चित्ते गर्वः किमभवत्तव ॥
2.2.m: Vīrabhadra said: / Hey, hey, Hari! How have you today transgressed the oath to Mahādeva? / Has pride arisen in your mind?

2.2.s:
tava śrīrudraśapathollaṅghane śaktirasti kim |
ko vā tvamasi ko vā te rakṣa'ko'sti jagattraye ||
2.2.d:
तव श्रीरुद्रशपथोल्लङ्घने शक्तिरस्ति किम् ।
को वा त्वमसि को वा ते रक्षऽकोऽस्ति जगत्त्रये ॥
2.2.m: Do you have the power to transgress the solemn oath of the glorious Rudra? / Or who are you, or who in the three worlds is your protector?

2.2.s:
atra tvamāgataḥ kasmādvayaṃ tannaiva vidmahe |
dakṣasya yajñapātā tvaṃ kathaṃ jāto'si tadvada ||
2.2.d:
अत्र त्वमागतः कस्माद्वयं तन्नैव विद्महे ।
दक्षस्य यज्ञपाता त्वं कथं जातोऽसि तद्वद ॥
2.2.m: Why have you come here? We do not know at all. / How have you become the protector of Dakṣa's sacrifice? Speak that!

2.2.s:
dākṣāyaṇyā kṛtaṃ yacca tanna dṛṣṭaṃ kimu tvayā |
proktaṃ yacca dadhīcena śrutaṃ tanna kimu tvayā cāpi dakṣayajñe'smin avadānārthamāgataḥ |
avadānaṃ prayacchāmi tava cāpi mahābhuja ||
2.2.d:
दाक्षायण्या कृतं यच्च तन्न दृष्टं किमु त्वया ।
प्रोक्तं यच्च दधीचेन श्रुतं तन्न किमु त्वया चापि दक्षयज्ञेऽस्मिन् अवदानार्थमागतः ।
अवदानं प्रयच्छामि तव चापि महाभुज ॥
2.2.m: Did you not see what was done by the daughter of Dakṣa? / Did you not hear what was spoken by Dadhīca? / And having come to this sacrifice of Dakṣa for a display of prowess, / I shall grant you a display of prowess as well, O mighty-armed one!

2.2.s:
vakṣo vidārayiṣyāmi triśūlena hare tava |
kastavāsti samāyāto rakṣako'dya mamāntikam ||
2.2.d:
वक्षो विदारयिष्यामि त्रिशूलेन हरे तव ।
कस्तवास्ति समायातो रक्षकोऽद्य ममान्तिकम् ॥
2.2.m: I shall tear open your chest, O Hari, with my trident! / Who has come as your protector today before me?

2.2.s:
pātayiṣyāmi bhūpṛṣṭhe jvālayiṣyāmi vahninā |
dagdhaṃ bhavantamadhunā peṣayiṣyāmi satvaram ||
2.2.d:
पातयिष्यामि भूपृष्ठे ज्वालयिष्यामि वह्निना ।
दग्धं भवन्तमधुना पेषयिष्यामि सत्वरम् ॥
2.2.m: I shall cast you upon the earth; I shall burn you with fire! / When you are burnt, I shall swiftly crush you now.

2.2.s:
re re hare durācāra maheśavimukhādhama |
śrīmahārudramāhātmyaṃ kinna jānāsi pāvanam ||
2.2.d:
रे रे हरे दुराचार महेशविमुखाधम ।
श्रीमहारुद्रमाहात्म्यं किन्न जानासि पावनम् ॥
2.2.m: Hey, hey, ill-behaved Hari, vile one averse to the Great Lord! / Do you not know the purifying eulogy of the glorious Mahārudra?

2.2.s:
athāpi tvaṃ mahābāho yoddhukāmo'grataḥ sthitaḥ |
neṣyāmi punarāvṛttiṃ yadi tiṣṭhestvamātmanā ||
2.2.d:
अथापि त्वं महाबाहो योद्धुकामोऽग्रतः स्थितः ।
नेष्यामि पुनरावृत्तिं यदि तिष्ठेस्त्वमात्मना ॥
2.2.m: Yet, O mighty-armed one, you stand before me eager to fight. / I shall ensure you never return, if you stand [your ground] by yourself!

2.2.s:
brahmovāca |
tasya tadvacanaṃ śrutvā vīrabhadrasya buddhimān |
uvāca vihasan prītyā viṣṇustatra sureśvaraḥ ||
2.2.d:
ब्रह्मोवाच ।
तस्य तद्वचनं श्रुत्वा वीरभद्रस्य बुद्धिमान् ।
उवाच विहसन् प्रीत्या विष्णुस्तत्र सुरेश्वरः ॥
2.2.m: Brahmā said: / Hearing those words of Vīrabhadra, the wise / Viṣṇu, the lord of gods, there spoke with a smile and with affection.

2.2.s:
viṣṇuruvāca |
śṛṇu tvaṃ vīrabhadrādya pravakṣyāmi tvadagrataḥ |
na rudravimukhaṃ māṃ tvaṃ vada śaṅkarasevakam ||
2.2.d:
विष्णुरुवाच ।
शृणु त्वं वीरभद्राद्य प्रवक्ष्यामि त्वदग्रतः ।
न रुद्रविमुखं मां त्वं वद शङ्करसेवकम् ॥
2.2.m: Viṣṇu said: / Listen today, O Vīrabhadra; I shall speak before you. / Do not call me averse to Rudra, [when I am] a servant of Śaṅkara.

2.2.s:
anena prārthitaḥ pūrvaṃ yajñārthaṃ ca punaḥ punaḥ |
dakṣeṇāviditārthena karmaniṣṭhena mauḍhyataḥ ||
2.2.d:
अनेन प्रार्थितः पूर्वं यज्ञार्थं च पुनः पुनः ।
दक्षेणाविदितार्थेन कर्मनिष्ठेन मौढ्यतः ॥
2.2.m: I was previously besought again and again for the sake of the sacrifice by this / Dakṣa, who was ignorant of the true reality and devoted to ritual actions out of foolishness.

2.2.s:
ahaṃ bhaktaparādhīnastathā so'pi maheśvaraḥ |
dakṣo bhakto hi me tāta tasmādatrāgato makhe ||
2.2.d:
अहं भक्तपराधीनस्तथा सोऽपि महेश्वरः ।
दक्षो भक्तो हि मे तात तस्मादत्रागतो मखे ॥
2.2.m: I am subservient to my devotees, and so also is Maheśvara. / Dakṣa is indeed my devotee, dear one; therefore I have come here to the sacrifice.

2.2.s:
śṛṇu pratijñāṃ me vīra rudrakopasamudbhava |
rudratejaḥsvarūpo hi supratāpālaya prabho ||
2.2.d:
शृणु प्रतिज्ञां मे वीर रुद्रकोपसमुद्भव ।
रुद्रतेजःस्वरूपो हि सुप्रतापालय प्रभो ॥
2.2.m: Hear my pledge, O hero, born from the wrath of Rudra, / having the very nature of Rudra's brilliance, O abode of great splendor, O master!

2.2.s:
ahaṃ nivārayāmi tvāṃ tvaṃ ca māṃ vinivāraya |
tadbhaviṣyati yadbhāvi kariṣye'haṃ parākramam ||
2.2.d:
अहं निवारयामि त्वां त्वं च मां विनिवारय ।
तद्भविष्यति यद्भावि करिष्येऽहं पराक्रमम् ॥
2.2.m: I shall check you, and you must check me. / Whatever is to happen will happen; I shall display my valor.

2.2.s:
brahmovāca |
ityuktavati govinde prahasya sa mahābhujaḥ |
avadatsuprasanno'smi tvāṃ jñātvāsmatprabhoḥ priyam ||
2.2.d:
ब्रह्मोवाच ।
इत्युक्तवति गोविन्दे प्रहस्य स महाभुजः ।
अवदत्सुप्रसन्नोऽस्मि त्वां ज्ञात्वास्मत्प्रभोः प्रियम् ॥
2.2.m: Brahmā said: / When Govinda had spoken thus, smiling, that mighty-armed one / said, "I am well pleased, knowing you to be dear to our master."

2.2.s:
tato vihasya suprīto vīrabhadro gaṇāgraṇīḥ |
praśrayāvanato'vādīdviṣṇuṃ devaṃ hi tattvataḥ ||
2.2.d:
ततो विहस्य सुप्रीतो वीरभद्रो गणाग्रणीः ।
प्रश्रयावनतोऽवादीद्विष्णुं देवं हि तत्त्वतः ॥
2.2.m: Then, smiling and well pleased, Vīrabhadra, leader of the attendants, / bowed down in humility and spoke to god Viṣṇu in accordance with truth.

2.2.s:
vīrabhadra uvāca |
tava bhāvaparīkṣārthamityuktaṃ me mahāprabho |
idānīṃ tattvato vacmi śṛṇu tvaṃ sāvadhānataḥ ||
2.2.d:
वीरभद्र उवाच ।
तव भावपरीक्षार्थमित्युक्तं मे महाप्रभो ।
इदानीं तत्त्वतो वच्मि शृणु त्वं सावधानतः ॥
2.2.m: Vīrabhadra said: / This was spoken by me in order to test your intention, O great lord. / Now I speak truly; listen with attention.

2.2.s:
yathā śivastathā tvaṃ hi yathā tvaṃ ca tathā śivaḥ |
iti vedā varṇayanti śivaśāsanato hare ||
2.2.d:
यथा शिवस्तथा त्वं हि यथा त्वं च तथा शिवः ।
इति वेदा वर्णयन्ति शिवशासनतो हरे ॥
2.2.m: Just as Śiva is, so indeed are you; and just as you are, so is Śiva. / Thus the Vedas describe, according to Śiva's decree, O Hari.

2.2.s:
śivājñayā vayaṃ sarve sevakāḥ śaṅkarasya vai |
tathāpi ca ramānātha pravādocitamādarāt ||
2.2.d:
शिवाज्ञया वयं सर्वे सेवकाः शङ्करस्य वै ।
तथापि च रमानाथ प्रवादोचितमादरात् ॥
2.2.m: By Śiva's command, we are all indeed servants of Śaṅkara. / Even so, O lord of Ramā, in accordance with what is fitting for custom and out of respect—

2.2.s:
brahmovāca |
tacchrutvā vacanaṃ tasya vīrabhadrasya so'cyutaḥ |
prahasya cedaṃ provāca vīrabhadramidaṃ vacaḥ ||
2.2.d:
ब्रह्मोवाच ।
तच्छ्रुत्वा वचनं तस्य वीरभद्रस्य सोऽच्युतः ।
प्रहस्य चेदं प्रोवाच वीरभद्रमिदं वचः ॥
2.2.m: Brahmā said: / Having heard those words of Vīrabhadra, that Acyuta, / smiling, addressed these words to Vīrabhadra:

2.2.s:
viṣṇuruvāca |
yuddhaṃ kuru mahāvīra mayā sārdhamaśaṅkitaḥ |
tavāstraiḥ pūryamāṇo'haṃ gamiṣyāmi svamāśramam ||
2.2.d:
विष्णुरुवाच ।
युद्धं कुरु महावीर मया सार्धमशङ्कितः ।
तवास्त्रैः पूर्यमाणोऽहं गमिष्यामि स्वमाश्रमम् ॥
2.2.m: Viṣṇu said: / Fight with me without hesitation, O great hero! / Struck all over by your weapons, I shall go to my own abode.

2.2.s:
brahmovāca |
ityuktvā hi viramyāsau sannaddho'bhūd raṇāya ca |
svagaṇairvīrabhadro'pi sannaddho'bhūnmahābalaḥ ||
śrīgaṇeśāya namaḥ ||
śrīgaurīśaṅkarābhyāṃ namaḥ ||
śrīśivamahāpurāṇam ||
dvitīyāyāṃ rudrasaṃhitāyāṃ dvitīyaḥ satīkhaṇḍe
2.2.d:
ब्रह्मोवाच ।
इत्युक्त्वा हि विरम्यासौ सन्नद्धोऽभूद् रणाय च ।
स्वगणैर्वीरभद्रोऽपि सन्नद्धोऽभून्महाबलः ॥
श्रीगणेशाय नमः ॥
श्रीगौरीशङ्कराभ्यां नमः ॥
श्रीशिवमहापुराणम् ॥
द्वितीयायां रुद्रसंहितायां द्वितीयः सतीखण्डे
2.2.m:
Brahmā said: / Having spoken thus and paused, he prepared for battle, / and Vīrabhadra also, very powerful, prepared with his own attendants.

Thus ends the thirty-sixth chapter, named "The Dialogue between Viṣṇu and Vīrabhadra," in the second section, the Satīkhaṇḍa, of the second Rudrasaṃhitā in the glorious Śiva Mahāpurāṇa.

2.2.s:
brahmovāca |
vīrabhadro'tha yuddhe vai viṣṇunā sa mahābalaḥ |
saṃsmṛtya śaṅkaraṃ citte sarvāpadvinivāraṇam ||
2.2.d:
ब्रह्मोवाच ।
वीरभद्रोऽथ युद्धे वै विष्णुना स महाबलः ।
संस्मृत्य शङ्करं चित्ते सर्वापद्विनिवारणम् ॥
2.2.m: Brahmā said: / Then in that battle with Viṣṇu, that very powerful Vīrabhadra, / having remembered in his mind Śaṅkara, the remover of all distress,

2.2.s:
āruhya syandanaṃ divyaṃ sarvavairivimardanaḥ |
gṛhītvā paramāstrāṇi siṃhanādaṃ jagarja ha ||
2.2.d:
आरुह्य स्यन्दनं दिव्यं सर्ववैरिविमर्दनः ।
गृहीत्वा परमास्त्राणि सिंहनादं जगर्ज ह ॥
2.2.m: mounted a celestial chariot, he the crusher of all adversaries, / and taking supreme weapons, let out a lion's roar.

2.2.s:
viṣṇuścāpi mahāghoṣaṃ pāñcajanyābhidhaṃ nijam |
dadhmau balī mahāśaṅkhaṃ svakīyān harṣayanniva ||
2.2.d:
विष्णुश्चापि महाघोषं पाञ्चजन्याभिधं निजम् ।
दध्मौ बली महाशङ्खं स्वकीयान् हर्षयन्निव ॥
2.2.m: Viṣṇu also, mighty, blew his own great conch, / named Pāñcajanya, of loud resonance, as if cheering his own followers.

2.2.s:
tacchrutvā śaṅkhanirhrādaṃ devā ye ca palāyitāḥ |
raṇaṃ hitvā gatāḥ pūrvaṃ te drutaṃ punarāyayuḥ ||
2.2.d:
तच्छ्रुत्वा शङ्खनिर्ह्रादं देवा ये च पलायिताः ।
रणं हित्वा गताः पूर्वं ते द्रुतं पुनराययुः ॥
2.2.m: Hearing that sound of the conch, those gods who had fled, / having earlier abandoned the battle and left, swiftly returned once more.

2.2.s:
vīrabhadragaṇaiste tu lokapālāḥ savāsavāḥ |
yuddhaṃ cakrustathā siṃhanādaṃ kṛtvā balānvitāḥ ||
2.2.d:
वीरभद्रगणैस्ते तु लोकपालाः सवासवाः ।
युद्धं चक्रुस्तथा सिंहनादं कृत्वा बलान्विताः ॥
2.2.m: Those guardians of the quarters together with Indra, endowed with might, / roared like lions and fought with Vīrabhadra's attendants.

2.2.s:
gaṇānāṃ lokapālānāṃ dvandvayuddhaṃ bhayāvaham |
abhavattatra tumulaṃ garjatāṃ siṃhanādataḥ ||
2.2.d:
गणानां लोकपालानां द्वन्द्वयुद्धं भयावहम् ।
अभवत्तत्र तुमुलं गर्जतां सिंहनादतः ॥
2.2.m: A terrifying, tumultuous single combat took place there / between the attendants and the guardians of the quarters, roaring with lion-like shouts.

2.2.s:
nandinā yuyudhe śakro'nalo vai cāśmanā tathā |
kubero'pi hi kūṣmāṇḍapatinā yuyudhe balī ||
2.2.d:
नन्दिना युयुधे शक्रोऽनलो वै चाश्मना तथा ।
कुबेरोऽपि हि कूष्माण्डपतिना युयुधे बली ॥
2.2.m: Śakra fought with Nandin, and Agni indeed with Aśman; / the mighty Kubera also fought with the lord of the kūṣmāṇḍas.

2.2.s: tadendreṇa hato nandī vajreṇa śataparvaṇā ||
2.2.d: तदेन्द्रेण हतो नन्दी वज्रेण शतपर्वणा ॥
2.2.m: Then Nandin was struck by Indra with his hundred-jointed thunderbolt.

2.2.s: nandinā ca hataḥ śakrastriśūlena stanāntare ||
2.2.d: नन्दिना च हतः शक्रस्त्रिशूलेन स्तनान्तरे ॥
2.2.m: And Śakra was struck in the chest by Nandin with a trident.

2.2.s:
balinau dvāvapi prītyā yuyudhāte parasparam |
nānāghātāṃśca kurvantau nandiśakrau jigīṣayā ||
2.2.d:
बलिनौ द्वावपि प्रीत्या युयुधाते परस्परम् ।
नानाघातांश्च कुर्वन्तौ नन्दिशक्रौ जिगीषया ॥
2.2.m: Both mighty warriors fought gladly with each other, / dealing various blows out of a desire for victory, Nandin and Śakra.

2.2.s:
śaktyā jaghāna cāśmānaṃ śuciḥ paramakopanaḥ |
so'pi śūlena taṃ vegācchitadhāreṇa pāvakam ||
2.2.d:
शक्त्या जघान चाश्मानं शुचिः परमकोपनः ।
सोऽपि शूलेन तं वेगाच्छितधारेण पावकम् ॥
2.2.m: Śuci, extremely furious, struck Aśman with a spear, / and he in turn swiftly struck Agni with a sharp-edged pike.

2.2.s:
yamena saha saṅgrāmaṃ mahāloko gaṇāgraṇīḥ |
cakāra tumulaṃ vīro mahādevaṃ smaranmudā ||
2.2.d:
यमेन सह सङ्ग्रामं महालोको गणाग्रणीः ।
चकार तुमुलं वीरो महादेवं स्मरन्मुदा ॥
2.2.m: The heroic Mahāloka, leader of the attendants, fought a tumultuous battle / with Yama, joyfully remembering Mahādeva.

2.2.s:
nairṛtena samāgamya caṇḍaśca balavattaraḥ |
yuyudhe paramāstraiśca nairṛtiṃ niviḍambayan ||
2.2.d:
नैरृतेन समागम्य चण्डश्च बलवत्तरः ।
युयुधे परमास्त्रैश्च नैरृतिं निविडम्बयन् ॥
2.2.m: Having encountered the lord of the south-west, the very strong Caṇḍa / fought with supreme weapons, mocking Nairṛta.

2.2.s:
varuṇena samaṃ vīro muṇḍaścaiva mahābalaḥ |
yuyudhe parayā śaktyā trilokīṃ vismayanniva ||
2.2.d:
वरुणेन समं वीरो मुण्डश्चैव महाबलः ।
युयुधे परया शक्त्या त्रिलोकीं विस्मयन्निव ॥
2.2.m: The heroic and very powerful Muṇḍa fought together with Varuṇa / with supreme power, as if astonishing the three worlds.

2.2.s:
vāyunā ca hato bhṛṅgī svāstreṇa paramaujasā |
bhṛṅgiṇā ca hato vāyustriśūlena pratāpinā ||
2.2.d:
वायुना च हतो भृङ्गी स्वास्त्रेण परमौजसा ।
भृङ्गिणा च हतो वायुस्त्रिशूलेन प्रतापिना ॥
2.2.m: And Bhṛṅgin was struck by Vāyu with his own weapon of supreme power, / and the powerful Vāyu was struck by Bhṛṅgin with a trident.

2.2.s:
kubereṇaiva saṅgamya kūṣmāṇḍapatirādarāt |
yuyudhe balavān vīro dhyātvā hṛdi maheśvaram ||
2.2.d:
कुबेरेणैव सङ्गम्य कूष्माण्डपतिरादरात् ।
युयुधे बलवान् वीरो ध्यात्वा हृदि महेश्वरम् ॥
2.2.m: Approaching Kubera with respect, / the mighty and heroic lord of the Kūṣmāṇḍas fought, meditating on Maheśvara in his heart.

2.2.s:
yoginīcakrasaṃyukto bhairavīnāyako mahān |
vidārya devānakhilān papau śoṇitamadbhutam ||
2.2.d:
योगिनीचक्रसंयुक्तो भैरवीनायको महान् ।
विदार्य देवानखिलान् पपौ शोणितमद्भुतम् ॥
2.2.m: Accompanied by the circle of Yoginīs, the great leader of the Bhairavīs / tore apart all the gods and drank [their] wondrous blood.

2.2.s:
kṣetrapālāstathā tatra bubhukṣuḥ surapuṅgavān |
kālī cāpi vidāryaiva tānpapau rudhiraṃ bahu ||
2.2.d:
क्षेत्रपालास्तथा तत्र बुभुक्षुः सुरपुङ्गवान् ।
काली चापि विदार्यैव तान्पपौ रुधिरं बहु ॥
2.2.m: Likewise, the Kṣetrapālas there were eager to devour the foremost gods; / and Kālī, having torn them apart, drank much blood.

2.2.s:
atha viṣṇurmahātejā yuyudhe taiśca śatruhā |
cakraṃ cikṣepa vegena dahanniva diśo daśa ||
2.2.d:
अथ विष्णुर्महातेजा युयुधे तैश्च शत्रुहा ।
चक्रं चिक्षेप वेगेन दहन्निव दिशो दश ॥
2.2.m: Then Viṣṇu of great splendour, the slayer of foes, fought with them; / he hurled his discus with force, as if burning the ten directions.

2.2.s:
kṣetrapālaḥ samāyāntaṃ cakramālokya vegataḥ |
tatrāgatyāgato vīraścāgrasatsahasā balī ||
2.2.d:
क्षेत्रपालः समायान्तं चक्रमालोक्य वेगतः ।
तत्रागत्यागतो वीरश्चाग्रसत्सहसा बली ॥
2.2.m: Seeing the discus coming swiftly, the powerful hero Kṣetrapāla / rushed there and swallowed it at once.

2.2.s:
cakraṃ grasitamālokya viṣṇuḥ parapurañjayaḥ |
mukhaṃ tasya parāmṛjya tamudgālitavānarim ||
2.2.d:
चक्रं ग्रसितमालोक्य विष्णुः परपुरञ्जयः ।
मुखं तस्य परामृज्य तमुद्गालितवानरिम् ॥
2.2.m: Seeing the discus swallowed, Viṣṇu, conqueror of enemies' cities, / stroked his mouth and made him vomit it up, O enemy!

2.2.s:
svacakramādāya mahānubhāvaḥ cukopa cātīva bhavaikabhartā |
mahābalī tairyuyudhe pravīraiḥ saṅkruddhanānāyudhadhārako'straiḥ ||
2.2.d:
स्वचक्रमादाय महानुभावः चुकोप चातीव भवैकभर्ता ।
महाबली तैर्युयुधे प्रवीरैः सङ्क्रुद्धनानायुधधारकोऽस्त्रैः ॥
2.2.m: Taking his own discus, the illustrious one, the sole lord of existence, grew exceedingly wrathful; / mighty, he fought with those eminent heroes, wielding various weapons and furious with missiles.

2.2.s:
cakre mahāraṇaṃ viṣṇuḥ taiḥ sārdhaṃ yuyudhe mudā |
nānāyudhāni saṅkṣipya tumulaṃ bhīmavikramam ||
2.2.d:
चक्रे महारणं विष्णुः तैः सार्धं युयुधे मुदा ।
नानायुधानि सङ्क्षिप्य तुमुलं भीमविक्रमम् ॥
2.2.m: Viṣṇu waged a great battle, gladly fighting alongside them; / hurling various weapons, [the combat] was tumultuous and of terrifying valour.

2.2.s:
atha te bhairavādyāśca yuyudhustena bhūriśaḥ |
nānāstrāṇi vimuñcantaḥ saṅkuddhāḥ paramaujasā ||
2.2.d:
अथ ते भैरवाद्याश्च युयुधुस्तेन भूरिशः ।
नानास्त्राणि विमुञ्चन्तः सङ्कुद्धाः परमौजसा ॥
2.2.m: Then Bhairava and the others fought with him fiercely; / furious, they discharged various weapons with supreme might.

2.2.s:
itthaṃ teṣāṃ raṇaṃ dṛṣṭvā hariṇātulatejasā |
vinivṛtya samāgamya tānsvayaṃ yuyudhe balī ||
2.2.d:
इत्थं तेषां रणं दृष्ट्वा हरिणातुलतेजसा ।
विनिवृत्य समागम्य तान्स्वयं युयुधे बली ॥
2.2.m: Seeing their battle with Hari of matchless splendor, / the mighty one turned back, approached, and fought them himself.

2.2.s:
atha viṣṇurmahātejāścakramudyamya mūrcchitaḥ |
yuyudhe bhagavāṃstena vīrabhadreṇa mādhavaḥ ||
2.2.d:
अथ विष्णुर्महातेजाश्चक्रमुद्यम्य मूर्च्छितः ।
युयुधे भगवांस्तेन वीरभद्रेण माधवः ॥
2.2.m: Then the radiant Viṣṇu, Lord Mādhava, having raised his discus in a frenzy, / fought with that Vīrabhadra.

2.2.s:
tayoḥ samabhavadyuddhaṃ sughoraṃ romaharṣaṇam |
mahāvīrābdhipatyostu nānāstradharayormune ||
2.2.d:
तयोः समभवद्युद्धं सुघोरं रोमहर्षणम् ।
महावीराब्धिपत्योस्तु नानास्त्रधरयोर्मुने ॥
2.2.m: Between the two, O sage, there occurred a dreadful battle making the hair stand on end, / between those two lords of the ocean of great heroes, wielding various weapons.

2.2.s:
viṣṇoryogabalāttasya dehādeva sudāruṇāḥ |
śaṅkhacakragadāhastā asaṅkhyātāśca jajñire ||
2.2.d:
विष्णोर्योगबलात्तस्य देहादेव सुदारुणाः ।
शङ्खचक्रगदाहस्ता असङ्ख्याताश्च जज्ञिरे ॥
2.2.m: By the yogic power of Viṣṇu, from his very body arose / innumerable and very fierce beings holding conches, discuses, and maces in hand.

2.2.s:
te cāpi yuyudhustena vīrabhadreṇa bhāṣatā |
viṣṇuvat balavanto hi nānāyudhadharā gaṇāḥ ||
2.2.d:
ते चापि युयुधुस्तेन वीरभद्रेण भाषता ।
विष्णुवत् बलवन्तो हि नानायुधधरा गणाः ॥
2.2.m: They too, attendants as strong as Viṣṇu and bearing diverse weapons, / fought with that roaring Vīrabhadra.

2.2.s:
tānsarvānapi vīro'sau nārāyaṇasamaprabhān |
bhasmīcakāra śūlena hatvā smṛtvā śivaṃ prabhum ||
2.2.d:
तान्सर्वानपि वीरोऽसौ नारायणसमप्रभान् ।
भस्मीचकार शूलेन हत्वा स्मृत्वा शिवं प्रभुम् ॥
2.2.m: Having remembered Lord Śiva, that hero struck down / and turned to ashes with his trident all of them who equalled Nārāyaṇa in radiance.

2.2.s:
tataścorasi taṃ viṣṇuṃ līlayaiva raṇājire |
jaghāna vīrabhadro hi triśūlena mahābalī ||
2.2.d:
ततश्चोरसि तं विष्णुं लीलयैव रणाजिरे ।
जघान वीरभद्रो हि त्रिशूलेन महाबली ॥
2.2.m: Then on the battlefield, the mighty Vīrabhadra easily / struck that Viṣṇu upon the chest with his trident.

2.2.s:
tena ghātena sahasā vihataḥ puruṣottamaḥ |
papāta ca tadā bhūmau visaṃjño'bhūnmune hariḥ ||
2.2.d:
तेन घातेन सहसा विहतः पुरुषोत्तमः ।
पपात च तदा भूमौ विसंज्ञोऽभून्मुने हरिः ॥
2.2.m: Instantly felled by that blow, O sage, / Hari, the supreme person, fell unconscious to the ground.

2.2.s:
tato jajñe'dbhutaṃ tejaḥ pralayānalasannibham |
trailokyadāhakaṃ tīvraṃ vīrāṇāmapi bhīkaram ||
2.2.d:
ततो जज्ञेऽद्भुतं तेजः प्रलयानलसन्निभम् ।
त्रैलोक्यदाहकं तीव्रं वीराणामपि भीकरम् ॥
2.2.m: Then there arose a wondrous splendour resembling the fire of universal dissolution, / burning the three worlds, fierce, and terrifying even to heroes.

2.2.s:
krodharaktekṣaṇaḥ śrīmān punarutthāya sa prabhuḥ |
prahartuṃ cakramudyamya hyatiṣṭhatpuruṣarṣabhaḥ ||
2.2.d:
क्रोधरक्तेक्षणः श्रीमान् पुनरुत्थाय स प्रभुः ।
प्रहर्तुं चक्रमुद्यम्य ह्यतिष्ठत्पुरुषर्षभः ॥
2.2.m: With eyes red with fury, the glorious Lord, that bull among men, / rose again and stood, raising his discus to strike.

2.2.s:
tasya cakraṃ mahāraudraṃ kālādityasamaprabham |
vyaṣṭambhayadadīnātmā vīrabhadraḥ śivaḥ prabhuḥ ||
2.2.d:
तस्य चक्रं महारौद्रं कालादित्यसमप्रभम् ।
व्यष्टम्भयददीनात्मा वीरभद्रः शिवः प्रभुः ॥
2.2.m: Lord Vīrabhadra, the unyielding Śiva, paralyzed / his extremely terrifying discus, which shone like the sun of dissolution.

2.2.s:
mune śambhoḥ prabhāvāttu māyeśasya mahāprabhoḥ |
na cacāla hareścakraṃ karasthaṃ stambhitaṃ dhruvam ||
2.2.d:
मुने शम्भोः प्रभावात्तु मायेशस्य महाप्रभोः ।
न चचाल हरेश्चक्रं करस्थं स्तम्भितं ध्रुवम् ॥
2.2.m: O sage, by the power of Śambhu, the great Lord and master of illusion, / Hari’s discus remained motionless, firmly paralyzed in his hand.

2.2.s:
atha viṣṇurgaṇeśena vīrabhadreṇa bhāṣatā |
atiṣṭhat stambhitastena śṛṅgavāniva niścalaḥ ||
2.2.d:
अथ विष्णुर्गणेशेन वीरभद्रेण भाषता ।
अतिष्ठत् स्तम्भितस्तेन शृङ्गवानिव निश्चलः ॥
2.2.m: Then Viṣṇu, paralyzed by the roaring Vīrabhadra, the lord of attendants, / stood motionless like a mountain horn.

2.2.s:
tato viṣṇuḥ stambhito hi vīrabhadreṇa nārada |
yajvopamantraṇamanuṃ niḥstambhanakaraṃ japan ||
2.2.d:
ततो विष्णुः स्तम्भितो हि वीरभद्रेण नारद ।
यज्वोपमन्त्रणमनुं निःस्तम्भनकरं जपन् ॥
2.2.m: Then, being paralyzed by Vīrabhadra, O Nārada, Viṣṇu / recited the sacrificial invocation mantra that neutralizes paralysis.

2.2.s:
tataḥ stambhananirmuktaḥ śārṅgadhanvā rameśvaraḥ |
śārṅgaṃ jagrāha sa kruddhaḥ svadhanuḥ saśaraṃ mune ||
2.2.d:
ततः स्तम्भननिर्मुक्तः शार्ङ्गधन्वा रमेश्वरः ।
शार्ङ्गं जग्राह स क्रुद्धः स्वधनुः सशरं मुने ॥
2.2.m: Then, freed from paralysis, the Lord of Ramā, wielder of the bow Śārṅga, / angrily grasped his own bow Śārṅga along with an arrow, O sage.

2.2.s:
tribhiśca dharṣitaṃ bāṇaistena śārṅgadhanurhareḥ |
vīrabhadreṇa tattāta tridhābhūttatkṣaṇānmune ||
2.2.d:
त्रिभिश्च धर्षितं बाणैस्तेन शार्ङ्गधनुर्हरेः ।
वीरभद्रेण तत्तात त्रिधाभूत्तत्क्षणान्मुने ॥
2.2.m: Assailed by three arrows shot by Vīrabhadra, / that bow Śārṅga of Hari was instantly broken into three parts, O dear one, O sage.

2.2.s:
atha viṣṇurmahāvāṇyā bodhitastaṃ mahāgaṇam |
asahyavarcasaṃ jñātvā hyantardhātuṃ mano dadhe ||
2.2.d:
अथ विष्णुर्महावाण्या बोधितस्तं महागणम् ।
असह्यवर्चसं ज्ञात्वा ह्यन्तर्धातुं मनो दधे ॥
2.2.m: Then Viṣṇu, awakened by a great voice and realizing that great attendant / possessed unbearable lustre, set his mind on disappearing.

2.2.s:
jñātvā ca tatsarvamidaṃ bhaviṣyaṃ satīkṛtaṃ duṣprasahaṃ pareṣām |
gatāḥ svalokaṃ svagaṇānvitāstu smṛtvā śivaṃ sarvapatiṃ svatantram ||
2.2.d:
ज्ञात्वा च तत्सर्वमिदं भविष्यं सतीकृतं दुष्प्रसहं परेषाम् ।
गताः स्वलोकं स्वगणान्वितास्तु स्मृत्वा शिवं सर्वपतिं स्वतन्त्रम् ॥
2.2.m: Knowing all this future event brought about by Satī to be intolerable for others, / they went to their own world along with their attendants, remembering Śiva, the independent master of all.

2.2.s:
satyalokagataścāhaṃ putraśokena pīḍitaḥ |
acintayaṃ suduḥkhārto mayā kiṃ kāryamadya vai ||
2.2.d:
सत्यलोकगतश्चाहं पुत्रशोकेन पीडितः ।
अचिन्तयं सुदुःखार्तो मया किं कार्यमद्य वै ॥
2.2.m: And I, having gone to Satyaloka, tormented by sorrow for my son, / grieved with great distress, thinking: 'What must I do now?'

2.2.s:
viṣṇau mayi gate caiva devāśca munibhiḥ saha |
vinirjitā gaṇaiḥ sarve ye te yajñopajīvinaḥ ||
2.2.d:
विष्णौ मयि गते चैव देवाश्च मुनिभिः सह ।
विनिर्जिता गणैः सर्वे ये ते यज्ञोपजीविनः ॥
2.2.m: When Viṣṇu and I had departed, the gods along with the sages, / all those who subsisted on sacrifices, were conquered by the attendants.

2.2.s:
tamupadravamālakṣya vidhvastaṃ ca mahāmakham |
mṛgasvarūpo yajño hi mahābhīto'pi dudruve ||
2.2.d:
तमुपद्रवमालक्ष्य विध्वस्तं च महामखम् ।
मृगस्वरूपो यज्ञो हि महाभीतोऽपि दुद्रुवे ॥
2.2.m: Seeing that turmoil and the great sacrifice destroyed, / the Sacrifice, assuming the form of a deer, fled in great terror.

2.2.s:
taṃ tadā mṛgarūpeṇa dhāvantaṃ gaganaṃ prati |
vīrabhadraḥ samādāya viśiraskamathākarot ||
2.2.d:
तं तदा मृगरूपेण धावन्तं गगनं प्रति ।
वीरभद्रः समादाय विशिरस्कमथाकरोत् ॥
2.2.m: Then, seizing him as he fled toward the sky in the form of a deer, / Vīrabhadra made him headless.

2.2.s:
tataḥ prajāpatiṃ dharmaṃ kaśyapaṃ ca pragṛhya saḥ |
ariṣṭaneminaṃ vīro bahuputraṃ munīśvaram ||
2.2.d:
ततः प्रजापतिं धर्मं कश्यपं च प्रगृह्य सः ।
अरिष्टनेमिनं वीरो बहुपुत्रं मुनीश्वरम् ॥
2.2.m: Then, seizing the Prajāpati Dharma, Kaśyapa, / Ariṣṭanemi, and the lord of sages Bahuputra;

2.2.s:
munimaṅgirasaṃ caiva kṛśāśvaṃ ca mahāgaṇaḥ |
jaghāna mūrdhni pādena dattaṃ ca munipuṅgavam ||
2.2.d:
मुनिमङ्गिरसं चैव कृशाश्वं च महागणः ।
जघान मूर्ध्नि पादेन दत्तं च मुनिपुङ्गवम् ॥
2.2.m: and the sage Aṅgiras, Kṛśāśva, and the foremost sage Datta, / that great attendant struck them on the head with his foot.

2.2.s:
sarasvatyāśca nāsāgraṃ devamātustathaiva ca |
ciccheda karajāgreṇa vīrabhadraḥ pratāpavān ||
2.2.d:
सरस्वत्याश्च नासाग्रं देवमातुस्तथैव च ।
चिच्छेद करजाग्रेण वीरभद्रः प्रतापवान् ॥
2.2.m: The powerful Vīrabhadra cut off with the tip of his fingernail / the tip of the nose of Sarasvatī, and likewise that of the mother of the gods.

2.2.s:
tato'nyānapi devādīn vidārya pṛthivītale |
pātayāmāsa so'yaṃ vai krodhākrāntātilocanaḥ ||
2.2.d:
ततोऽन्यानपि देवादीन् विदार्य पृथिवीतले ।
पातयामास सोऽयं वै क्रोधाक्रान्तातिलोचनः ॥
2.2.m: Then, tearing apart other gods and beings on the surface of the earth, / he, whose eyes were filled with fury, hurled them down.

2.2.s:
vīrabhadro vidāryāpi devānmukhyānmunīnapi |
nābhūcchānto drutakrodhaḥ phaṇirāḍiva maṇḍitaḥ ||
2.2.d:
वीरभद्रो विदार्यापि देवान्मुख्यान्मुनीनपि ।
नाभूच्छान्तो द्रुतक्रोधः फणिराडिव मण्डितः ॥
2.2.m: Even after tearing apart the principal gods and sages, Vīrabhadra, / blazing with anger like an ornamented king of serpents, did not become pacified.

2.2.s:
vīrabhadroddhṛtārātiḥ kesarīva vanadvipān |
diśo vilokayāmāsa kaḥ kutrāstītyanukṣaṇam ||
2.2.d:
वीरभद्रोद्धृतारातिः केसरीव वनद्विपान् ।
दिशो विलोकयामास कः कुत्रास्तीत्यनुक्षणम् ॥
2.2.m: Vīrabhadra, having uprooted his enemies like a lion [uproots] wild elephants, / looked in all directions at every moment, [wondering] who was where.

2.2.s:
vyapothayad bhṛguṃ yāvanmaṇibhadraḥ pratāpavān |
padākramyorasi tadākārṣīttacchmaśruluñcanam ||
2.2.d:
व्यपोथयद् भृगुं यावन्मणिभद्रः प्रतापवान् ।
पदाक्रम्योरसि तदाकार्षीत्तच्छ्मश्रुलुञ्चनम् ॥
2.2.m: While the mighty Maṇibhadra was crushing Bhṛgu, / he trampled him upon the chest with his foot and plucked out his beard.

2.2.s:
caṇḍaścotpāṭayāmāsa pūṣṇo dantān pravegataḥ |
śapyamāne hare pūrvaṃ yo'hasaddarśayandataḥ ||
2.2.d:
चण्डश्चोत्पाटयामास पूष्णो दन्तान् प्रवेगतः ।
शप्यमाने हरे पूर्वं योऽहसद्दर्शयन्दतः ॥
2.2.m: And Caṇḍa forcefully wrenched out the teeth of Pūṣan, / who had formerly laughed showing his teeth while Hara was being cursed.

2.2.s:
nandī bhagasya netre hi pātitasya ruṣā bhuvi |
ujjahāra dakṣamakṣṇā yaḥ śapantamasūsucat ||
2.2.d:
नन्दी भगस्य नेत्रे हि पातितस्य रुषा भुवि ।
उज्जहार दक्षमक्ष्णा यः शपन्तमसूसुचत् ॥
2.2.m: Nandin gouged out the eyes of Bhaga, who had been thrown to the ground in wrath, / and who had gestured with his eye while Dakṣa was cursing.

2.2.s:
viḍambitā svadhā tatra sā svāhā dakṣiṇā tathā |
mantrāstantrāstathā cānye tatrasthā gaṇanāyakaiḥ ||
2.2.d:
विडम्बिता स्वधा तत्र सा स्वाहा दक्षिणा तथा ।
मन्त्रास्तन्त्रास्तथा चान्ये तत्रस्था गणनायकैः ॥
2.2.m: There Svadhā, Svāhā, Dakṣiṇā, / as well as the mantras, rituals, and others present were mocked by the leaders of the attendants.

2.2.s:
vavṛṣuste purīṣāṇi vitānāgnau ruṣā gaṇāḥ |
anirvācyaṃ tadā cakrurgaṇā vīrāstamadhvaram ||
2.2.d:
ववृषुस्ते पुरीषाणि वितानाग्नौ रुषा गणाः ।
अनिर्वाच्यं तदा चक्रुर्गणा वीरास्तमध्वरम् ॥
2.2.m: Furious, the attendants showered excrement into the sacrificial fire; / the heroic attendants made that sacrifice utterly indescribable.

2.2.s:
antarvedyantaragataṃ nilīnaṃ tadbhayād balāt |
ānināya samājñāya vīrabhadraḥ svabhūḥsutam ||
2.2.d:
अन्तर्वेद्यन्तरगतं निलीनं तद्भयाद् बलात् ।
आनिनाय समाज्ञाय वीरभद्रः स्वभूःसुतम् ॥
2.2.m: Finding that the son of the Self-born had gone inside the sacrificial enclosure and hidden out of fear of him, / Vīrabhadra forcibly dragged him forth.

2.2.s:
kapole'sya gṛhītvā tu khaḍgenopahṛtaṃ śiraḥ |
abhedyamabhavattasya tacca yogaprabhāvataḥ ||
2.2.d:
कपोलेऽस्य गृहीत्वा तु खड्गेनोपहृतं शिरः ।
अभेद्यमभवत्तस्य तच्च योगप्रभावतः ॥
2.2.m: Seizing him by the cheek, he struck at his head with a sword; / but by virtue of his yoga, it proved impossible to cut.

2.2.s:
abhedyaṃ tacchiro matvā śastrāstraiśca tu sarvaśaḥ |
kareṇa troṭayāmāsa padbhyāmākramya corasi ||
2.2.d:
अभेद्यं तच्छिरो मत्वा शस्त्रास्त्रैश्च तु सर्वशः ।
करेण त्रोटयामास पद्भ्यामाक्रम्य चोरसि ॥
2.2.m: Knowing that head to be impenetrable by all weapons and missiles, / he severed it with his hand while trampling his chest with both feet.

2.2.s:
tacchirastasya duṣṭasya dakṣasya haravairiṇaḥ |
agnikuṇḍe pracikṣepa vīrabhadro gaṇāgraṇīḥ ||
2.2.d:
तच्छिरस्तस्य दुष्टस्य दक्षस्य हरवैरिणः ।
अग्निकुण्डे प्रचिक्षेप वीरभद्रो गणाग्रणीः ॥
2.2.m: The leader of the attendants, Vīrabhadra, cast into the fire pit / that head of the wicked Dakṣa, the enemy of Hara.

2.2.s:
reje tadā vīrabhadrastriśūlaṃ bhrāmayankare |
kruddhā raṇākṣasaṃvartāḥ prajvālya parvatopamāḥ ||
2.2.d:
रेजे तदा वीरभद्रस्त्रिशूलं भ्रामयन्करे ।
क्रुद्धा रणाक्षसंवर्ताः प्रज्वाल्य पर्वतोपमाः ॥
2.2.m: Then Vīrabhadra shone as he brandished the trident in his hand; / the wrathful [attendants], resembling mountains, burned like fires of dissolution on the battlefield.

2.2.s:
anāyāsena hatvaitān vīrabhadrastato'gninā |
jvālayāmāsa sakrodho dīptāgniḥ śalabhāniva ||
2.2.d:
अनायासेन हत्वैतान् वीरभद्रस्ततोऽग्निना ।
ज्वालयामास सक्रोधो दीप्ताग्निः शलभानिव ॥
2.2.m: Having slain them effortlessly, the enraged Vīrabhadra / burned them with fire, as a blazing fire burns moths.

2.2.s:
vīrabhadrastato dagdhān dṛṣṭvā dakṣapurogamān |
aṭṭāṭṭahāsamakarot pūrayaṃśca jagattrayam ||
2.2.d:
वीरभद्रस्ततो दग्धान् दृष्ट्वा दक्षपुरोगमान् ।
अट्टाट्टहासमकरोत् पूरयंश्च जगत्त्रयम् ॥
2.2.m: Then, seeing Dakṣa and the others burnt, / Vīrabhadra let out a loud roar of laughter, filling the three worlds.

2.2.s:
vīraśriyā vṛtastatra tato nandanasambhavā |
puṣpavṛṣṭirabhūddivyā vīrabhadre gaṇānvite ||
2.2.d:
वीरश्रिया वृतस्तत्र ततो नन्दनसम्भवा ।
पुष्पवृष्टिरभूद्दिव्या वीरभद्रे गणान्विते ॥
2.2.m: Attended there by heroic glory, / a divine shower of flowers from the Nandana garden fell upon Vīrabhadra accompanied by the attendants.

2.2.s:
vavurgandhavahāḥ śītāḥ sugandhāḥ sukhadāḥ śanaiḥ |
devadundubhayo neduḥ samameva tataḥ param ||
2.2.d:
ववुर्गन्धवहाः शीताः सुगन्धाः सुखदाः शनैः ।
देवदुन्दुभयो नेदुः सममेव ततः परम् ॥
2.2.m: Cool, fragrant, and pleasant breezes blew softly; / celestial drums sounded immediately thereafter.

2.2.s:
kailāsaṃ sa yayau vīraḥ kṛtakāryastataḥ param |
vināśitadṛḍhadhvānto bhānumāniva satvaram ||
2.2.d:
कैलासं स ययौ वीरः कृतकार्यस्ततः परम् ।
विनाशितदृढध्वान्तो भानुमानिव सत्वरम् ॥
2.2.m: Then, having accomplished his task, the hero swiftly went to Kailāsa, / like the sun when it has destroyed deep darkness.

2.2.s:
kṛtakāryaṃ vīrabhadraṃ dṛṣṭvā santuṣṭamānasaḥ |
śambhurvīragaṇādhyakṣaṃ cakāra parameśvaraḥ ||
śrīgaṇeśāya namaḥ ||
śrīgaurīśaṅkarābhyāṃ namaḥ ||
śrīśivamahāpurāṇam ||
dvitīyāyāṃ rudrasaṃhitāyāṃ dvitīyaḥ satīkhaṇḍe
2.2.d:
कृतकार्यं वीरभद्रं दृष्ट्वा सन्तुष्टमानसः ।
शम्भुर्वीरगणाध्यक्षं चकार परमेश्वरः ॥
श्रीगणेशाय नमः ॥
श्रीगौरीशङ्कराभ्यां नमः ॥
श्रीशिवमहापुराणम् ॥
द्वितीयायां रुद्रसंहितायां द्वितीयः सतीखण्डे
2.2.m:
Seeing that Vīrabhadra had accomplished his task, / Śambhu, the supreme lord, his mind delighted, made him commander of the host of heroes.

Homage to glorious Gaurī and Śaṅkara.

In the second section, the Satīkhaṇḍa, of the second Rudrasaṃhitā:

2.2.s:
sūta uvāca |
ityākarṇya vacastasya vidheramitadhīmataḥ |
papraccha nāradaḥ prītyā vismitastaṃ dvijottamaḥ ||
2.2.d:
सूत उवाच ।
इत्याकर्ण्य वचस्तस्य विधेरमितधीमतः ।
पप्रच्छ नारदः प्रीत्या विस्मितस्तं द्विजोत्तमः ॥
2.2.m: Sūta said: / Hearing those words of the Creator of boundless intellect, / Nārada, the best of the twice-born, filled with wonder, asked him with affection:

2.2.s:
nārada uvāca |
śivaṃ vihāya dakṣasya surairyajñaṃ harirgataḥ |
hetunā kena tad brūhi yatrāvajñābhavattataḥ ||
2.2.d:
नारद उवाच ।
शिवं विहाय दक्षस्य सुरैर्यज्ञं हरिर्गतः ।
हेतुना केन तद् ब्रूहि यत्रावज्ञाभवत्ततः ॥
2.2.m: Nārada said: / Hari went to Dakṣa's sacrifice along with the gods, forsaking Śiva; / tell [me] for what reason disrespect toward him arose thereafter.

2.2.s:
jānāti kiṃ sa śambhuṃ no hariḥ pralayavikramam |
raṇaṃ kathaṃ ca kṛtavān tadgaṇairabudho yathā ||
2.2.d:
जानाति किं स शम्भुं नो हरिः प्रलयविक्रमम् ।
रणं कथं च कृतवान् तद्गणैरबुधो यथा ॥
2.2.m: Did Hari not know that Śambhu possesses valour [capable of] cosmic dissolution? / And how did he fight with his attendants, like a fool?

2.2.s:
eṣa me saṃśayo bhūyāṃstaṃ chindhi karuṇānidhe |
caritaṃ brūhi śambhostu cittotsāhakaraṃ prabho ||
2.2.d:
एष मे संशयो भूयांस्तं छिन्धि करुणानिधे ।
चरितं ब्रूहि शम्भोस्तु चित्तोत्साहकरं प्रभो ॥
2.2.m: This is a great doubt of mine; sever it, O treasure of compassion! / O lord, tell the deeds of Śambhu, which bring enthusiasm to the heart.

2.2.s:
brahmovāca |
dvijavarya śṛṇu prītyā caritaṃ śaśimaulinaḥ |
yatpṛcchate kurvataśca sarvasaṃśayahārakam ||
2.2.d:
ब्रह्मोवाच ।
द्विजवर्य शृणु प्रीत्या चरितं शशिमौलिनः ।
यत्पृच्छते कुर्वतश्च सर्वसंशयहारकम् ॥
2.2.m: Brahmā said: / O best of the twice-born, listen with delight to the deeds of the moon-crested [deity], / which removes all doubt for the one who asks and the one who recites.

2.2.s:
dadhīcasya muneḥ śāpād bhraṣṭajñāno hariḥ purā |
sāmaro dakṣayajñaṃ vai gataḥ kṣuvasahāyakṛt ||
2.2.d:
दधीचस्य मुनेः शापाद् भ्रष्टज्ञानो हरिः पुरा ।
सामरो दक्षयज्ञं वै गतः क्षुवसहायकृत् ॥
2.2.m: Formerly, Hari, having lost his knowledge through the curse of sage Dadhīca, / went with the immortals to Dakṣa's sacrifice, aiding Kṣuva.

2.2.s:
nārada uvāca |
kimarthaṃ śaptavānviṣṇuṃ dadhīco munisattamaḥ |
ko'pakāraḥ kṛtastasya hariṇā tatsahāyinā ||
2.2.d:
नारद उवाच ।
किमर्थं शप्तवान्विष्णुं दधीचो मुनिसत्तमः ।
कोऽपकारः कृतस्तस्य हरिणा तत्सहायिना ॥
2.2.m: Nārada said: / For what reason did Dadhīca, the best of sages, curse Viṣṇu? / What harm was done to him by Hari, who aided him?

2.2.s:
brahmovāca |
samutpanno mahātejā rājā kṣuva iti smṛtaḥ |
abhūnmitraṃ dadhīcasya munīndrasya mahāprabhoḥ ||
2.2.d:
ब्रह्मोवाच ।
समुत्पन्नो महातेजा राजा क्षुव इति स्मृतः ।
अभून्मित्रं दधीचस्य मुनीन्द्रस्य महाप्रभोः ॥
2.2.m: Brahmā said: / A king known as Kṣuva, of great splendour, was born; / he was a friend of Dadhīca, the great, powerful lord of sages.

2.2.s:
cirāttapaḥprasaṅgādvai vādaḥ kṣuvadadhīcayoḥ |
mahānarthakaraḥ khyātastrilokeṣvabhavatpurā ||
2.2.d:
चिरात्तपःप्रसङ्गाद्वै वादः क्षुवदधीचयोः ।
महानर्थकरः ख्यातस्त्रिलोकेष्वभवत्पुरा ॥
2.2.m: In the course of time, in the context of austerity, a dispute arose between Kṣuva and Dadhīca / in ancient times, famous in the three worlds, which caused great misfortune.

2.2.s:
tatra trivarṇataḥ śreṣṭho vipra eva na saṃśayaḥ |
iti prāha dadhīco hi śivabhaktastu vedavit ||
2.2.d:
तत्र त्रिवर्णतः श्रेष्ठो विप्र एव न संशयः ।
इति प्राह दधीचो हि शिवभक्तस्तु वेदवित् ॥
2.2.m: Dadhīca, a devotee of Śiva and knower of the Veda, declared: / 'Among the three social classes, the brahmin alone is superior; there is no doubt.'

2.2.s:
tacchrutvā vacanaṃ tasya dadhīcasya mahāmune |
kṣuvaḥ prāheti nṛpatiḥ śrīmadena vimohitaḥ ||
2.2.d:
तच्छ्रुत्वा वचनं तस्य दधीचस्य महामुने ।
क्षुवः प्राहेति नृपतिः श्रीमदेन विमोहितः ॥
2.2.m: Hearing those words of the great sage Dadhīca, / King Kṣuva, deluded by pride in his royal power, spoke:

2.2.s:
kṣuva uvāca |
aṣṭānāṃ lokapālānāṃ vapurdhārayate nṛpaḥ |
tasmānnṛpo variṣṭho hi varṇāśramapatiḥ prabhuḥ ||
2.2.d:
क्षुव उवाच ।
अष्टानां लोकपालानां वपुर्धारयते नृपः ।
तस्मान्नृपो वरिष्ठो हि वर्णाश्रमपतिः प्रभुः ॥
2.2.m: Kṣuva said: / 'A king bears the bodies of the eight guardians of the world; / therefore, the king is the most eminent, the master of the social classes and stages of life, the sovereign.

2.2.s:
sarvadevamayo rājā śrutiḥ prāheti tatparā |
mahatī devatā yā sā so'hameva tato mune ||
2.2.d:
सर्वदेवमयो राजा श्रुतिः प्राहेति तत्परा ।
महती देवता या सा सोऽहमेव ततो मुने ॥
2.2.m: The Vedic scripture, intent upon this, declares that a king embodies all deities; / therefore, O sage, I myself am that great deity.

2.2.s:
tasmādviprādvaro rājā cyāvaneya vicāryatām |
nāvamantavya evātaḥ pūjyo'haṃ sarvathā tvayā ||
2.2.d:
तस्माद्विप्राद्वरो राजा च्यावनेय विचार्यताम् ।
नावमन्तव्य एवातः पूज्योऽहं सर्वथा त्वया ॥
2.2.m: Therefore, O son of Cyavana, consider [this]: the king is superior to the brahmin. / Hence I must never be despised; I am to be worshipped by you in every way.'

2.2.s:
brahmovāca |
śrutvā tathā mataṃ tasya kṣuvasya munisattamaḥ |
śrutismṛtiviruddhaṃ taṃ cukopātīva bhārgavaḥ ||
2.2.d:
ब्रह्मोवाच ।
श्रुत्वा तथा मतं तस्य क्षुवस्य मुनिसत्तमः ।
श्रुतिस्मृतिविरुद्धं तं चुकोपातीव भार्गवः ॥
2.2.m: Brahmā said: / Hearing that opinion of Kṣuva, which contradicted the revealed and remembered texts, / the descendant of Bhṛgu, the best of sages, was exceedingly enraged.

2.2.s:
atha kruddho mahātejā gauravāccātmano mune |
atāḍayatkṣuvaṃ mūrdhni dadhīco vāmamuṣṭitaḥ ||
2.2.d:
अथ क्रुद्धो महातेजा गौरवाच्चात्मनो मुने ।
अताडयत्क्षुवं मूर्ध्नि दधीचो वाममुष्टितः ॥
2.2.m: Then, infuriated out of his own dignity, O sage, / Dadhīca of great splendour struck Kṣuva on the head with his left fist.

2.2.s:
vajreṇa taṃ ca ciccheda dadhīcaṃ tāḍitaḥ kṣuvaḥ |
jagarjātīva saṅkruddho brahmāṇḍādhipatiḥ kudhīḥ ||
2.2.d:
वज्रेण तं च चिच्छेद दधीचं ताडितः क्षुवः ।
जगर्जातीव सङ्क्रुद्धो ब्रह्माण्डाधिपतिः कुधीः ॥
2.2.m: Struck, Kṣuva cut Dadhīca with a thunderbolt; / that wicked ruler of the universe roared with intense rage.

2.2.s:
papāta bhūmau nihato tena vajreṇa bhārgavaḥ |
śukraṃ sasmāra kṣuvakṛdbhārgavasya kulandharaḥ ||
2.2.d:
पपात भूमौ निहतो तेन वज्रेण भार्गवः ।
शुक्रं सस्मार क्षुवकृद्भार्गवस्य कुलन्धरः ॥
2.2.m: Struck by that thunderbolt, the descendant of Bhṛgu fell to the ground; / having caused Kṣuva [this sorrow], the maintainer of Bhṛgu's lineage remembered Śukra.

2.2.s:
śukro'tha sandhayāmāsa tāḍitaṃ ca kṣuvena tu |
yogī dadhīcasya tadā dehamāgatya sa drutam ||
2.2.d:
शुक्रोऽथ सन्धयामास ताडितं च क्षुवेन तु ।
योगी दधीचस्य तदा देहमागत्य स द्रुतम् ॥
2.2.m: Then the yogin Śukra, arriving quickly at the body of Dadhīca / who had been struck down by Kṣuva, rejoined it.

2.2.s:
sandhāya pūrvavaddehaṃ dadhīcasyāha bhārgavaḥ |
śivabhaktāgraṇīrmṛtyañjayavidyāpravartakaḥ ||
2.2.d:
सन्धाय पूर्ववद्देहं दधीचस्याह भार्गवः ।
शिवभक्ताग्रणीर्मृत्यञ्जयविद्याप्रवर्तकः ॥
2.2.m: Having healed Dadhīca's body as before, the descendant of Bhṛgu, / foremost among devotees of Śiva and author of the lore that conquers death, spoke:

2.2.s:
śukra uvāca |
dadhīca tāta sampūjya śivaṃ sarveśvaraṃ prabhum |
mahāmṛtyuñjayaṃ mantraṃ śrautamagryaṃ vadāmi te ||
2.2.d:
शुक्र उवाच ।
दधीच तात सम्पूज्य शिवं सर्वेश्वरं प्रभुम् ।
महामृत्युञ्जयं मन्त्रं श्रौतमग्र्यं वदामि ते ॥
2.2.m: Śukra said: / 'O dear Dadhīca, having worshipped Śiva, the sovereign lord of all, / I shall tell you the supreme Vedic Mahāmṛtyuñjaya mantra:

2.2.s:
tryambakaṃ yajāmahe trailokyaṃ pitaraṃ prabhum |
trimaṇḍalasya pitaraṃ triguṇasya maheśvaram ||
2.2.d:
त्र्यम्बकं यजामहे त्रैलोक्यं पितरं प्रभुम् ।
त्रिमण्डलस्य पितरं त्रिगुणस्य महेश्वरम् ॥
2.2.m: "We worship Tryambaka, the sovereign father of the three worlds, / the father of the three realms, the great lord of the three guṇas,

2.2.s:
tritattvasya trivahneśca tridhābhūtasya sarvataḥ |
tridivasya tribāhośca tridhābhūtasya sarvataḥ ||
2.2.d:
त्रितत्त्वस्य त्रिवह्नेश्च त्रिधाभूतस्य सर्वतः ।
त्रिदिवस्य त्रिबाहोश्च त्रिधाभूतस्य सर्वतः ॥
2.2.m: the lord of the three realities and the three fires, omnipresent in three ways, / of the three heavens, of the three arms, omnipresent in three ways;

2.2.s:
tridevasya mahādevaḥ sugandhiṃ puṣṭivarddhanam |
sarvabhūteṣu sarvatra triguṇeṣu kṛtau yathā ||
2.2.d:
त्रिदेवस्य महादेवः सुगन्धिं पुष्टिवर्द्धनम् ।
सर्वभूतेषु सर्वत्र त्रिगुणेषु कृतौ यथा ॥
2.2.m: Mahādeva of the three deities, the fragrant one who increases nourishment; / as in all beings everywhere, in the three guṇas in creation,

2.2.s:
indriyeṣu tathānyeṣu deveṣu ca gaṇeṣu ca |
puṣpe sugandhivatsūraḥ sugandhiramareśvaraḥ ||
2.2.d:
इन्द्रियेषु तथान्येषु देवेषु च गणेषु च ।
पुष्पे सुगन्धिवत्सूरः सुगन्धिरमरेश्वरः ॥
2.2.m: so in the senses, in the other gods, and in the attendants, / like fragrance in a flower, the hero, the lord of immortals, is fragrant.

2.2.s:
puṣṭiśca prakṛteryasmātpuruṣād vai dvijottama |
mahadādiviśeṣāntavikalpaścāpi suvrata ||
2.2.d:
पुष्टिश्च प्रकृतेर्यस्मात्पुरुषाद् वै द्विजोत्तम ।
महदादिविशेषान्तविकल्पश्चापि सुव्रत ॥
2.2.m: And since nourishment [arises] from prakṛti and puruṣa, O best of the twice-born, / and also the varieties from the cosmic intellect down to particular elements, O you of noble vows,

2.2.s:
viṣṇoḥ pitāmahasyāpi munīnāṃ ca mahāmune |
indriyāṇāṃ ca devānāṃ tasmād vai puṣṭivardhanaḥ ||
2.2.d:
विष्णोः पितामहस्यापि मुनीनां च महामुने ।
इन्द्रियाणां च देवानां तस्माद् वै पुष्टिवर्धनः ॥
2.2.m: and of Viṣṇu, of the Grandfather, and of the sages, O great sage, / and of the senses and the gods; therefore, indeed, he increases nourishment.

2.2.s:
taṃ devamamṛtaṃ rudraṃ karmaṇā tapasāpi vā |
svādhyāyena ca yogena dhyānena ca prajāyate ||
2.2.d:
तं देवममृतं रुद्रं कर्मणा तपसापि वा ।
स्वाध्यायेन च योगेन ध्यानेन च प्रजायते ॥
2.2.m: That immortal god Rudra is attained by action or by austerity, / by private Vedic study, by yoga, and by meditation;

2.2.s:
satyenānyena sūkṣmāgrānmṛtyupāśādbhavaḥ svayam |
bandhamokṣakaro yasmādurvārukamiva prabhuḥ ||
2.2.d:
सत्येनान्येन सूक्ष्माग्रान्मृत्युपाशाद्भवः स्वयम् ।
बन्धमोक्षकरो यस्मादुर्वारुकमिव प्रभुः ॥
2.2.m: by truth, and through no other means, Bhava himself frees one from the bonds / of the subtle edge of death's fetters, as a sovereign frees a cucumber [from its stalk]."

2.2.s:
mṛtasañjīvanīmantro mama sarvottamaḥ smṛtaḥ |
evaṃ japaparaḥ prītyā niyamena śivaṃ smaran ||
2.2.d:
मृतसञ्जीवनीमन्त्रो मम सर्वोत्तमः स्मृतः ।
एवं जपपरः प्रीत्या नियमेन शिवं स्मरन् ॥
2.2.m: This Mṛtasañjīvanī mantra is considered my greatest; / one who is thus devoted to reciting it, remembering Śiva with love according to the rules,

2.2.s:
japtvā hutvābhimantryaivaṃ jalaṃ piba divāniśam |
śivasya sannidhau dhyātvā nāsti mṛtyubhayaṃ kvacit ||
2.2.d:
जप्त्वा हुत्वाभिमन्त्र्यैवं जलं पिब दिवानिशम् ।
शिवस्य सन्निधौ ध्यात्वा नास्ति मृत्युभयं क्वचित् ॥
2.2.m: after reciting, offering oblations, and consecrating water in this way, should drink it day and night; / meditating in the presence of Śiva, there is no fear of death anywhere.

2.2.s:
kṛtvā nyāsādikaṃ sarvaṃ sampūjya vidhivacchivam |
saṃvidhāyedaṃ nirvyagraḥ śaṅkaraṃ bhaktavatsalam ||
2.2.d:
कृत्वा न्यासादिकं सर्वं सम्पूज्य विधिवच्छिवम् ।
संविधायेदं निर्व्यग्रः शङ्करं भक्तवत्सलम् ॥
2.2.m: Having performed all the ritual placements and the rest, having worshipped Śiva according to the rules, / and having arranged this without distraction, [one should worship] Śaṅkara, affectionate toward devotees.

2.2.s:
dhyānamasya pravakṣyāmi yathā dhyātvā japenmanum |
siddhamantro bhaveddhīmān yāvacchambhuprabhāvataḥ ||
2.2.d:
ध्यानमस्य प्रवक्ष्यामि यथा ध्यात्वा जपेन्मनुम् ।
सिद्धमन्त्रो भवेद्धीमान् यावच्छम्भुप्रभावतः ॥
2.2.m: I shall declare his meditation, meditating on which a wise man should recite the mantra / until, by the power of Śambhu, he becomes accomplished in the mantra:

2.2.s:
hastāmbhojayugasthakumbhayugalāduddhṛtya toyaṃ śiraḥ siñcantaṃ karayoryugena dadhataṃ svāṅke sakumbhau karau |
akṣasraṅmṛgahastamambujagataṃ mūrdhasthacandrasravat-pīyūṣārdratanuṃ bhaje sagirijaṃ tryakṣaṃ ca mṛtyuñjayam ||
2.2.d:
हस्ताम्भोजयुगस्थकुम्भयुगलादुद्धृत्य तोयं शिरः सिञ्चन्तं करयोर्युगेन दधतं स्वाङ्के सकुम्भौ करौ ।
अक्षस्रङ्मृगहस्तमम्बुजगतं मूर्धस्थचन्द्रस्रवत्-पीयूषार्द्रतनुं भजे सगिरिजं त्र्यक्षं च मृत्युञ्जयम् ॥
2.2.m: "I worship the three-eyed conqueror of death, together with the daughter of the mountain, / who with a pair of hands sprinkles his head with water drawn from a pair of jars held in his lotus hands, whose hands rest on his lap holding the jars, / who holds a rosary and a deer, seated on a lotus, his body moistened with nectar flowing from the moon on his crest."

2.2.s:
brahmovāca |
upadiśyeti śukraḥ taṃ dadhīciṃ munisattamam |
svasthānamagamattāta saṃsmaran śaṅkaraṃ prabhum ||
2.2.d:
ब्रह्मोवाच ।
उपदिश्येति शुक्रः तं दधीचिं मुनिसत्तमम् ।
स्वस्थानमगमत्तात संस्मरन् शङ्करं प्रभुम् ॥
2.2.m: Brahmā said: / Having thus instructed that Dadhīca, the best of sages, / Śukra went to his own abode, my dear, constantly remembering the lord Śaṅkara.

2.2.s:
tasya tadvacanaṃ śrutvā dadhīco hi mahāmuniḥ |
vanaṃ jagāma tapase mahāprītyā śivaṃ smaran ||
2.2.d:
तस्य तद्वचनं श्रुत्वा दधीचो हि महामुनिः ।
वनं जगाम तपसे महाप्रीत्या शिवं स्मरन् ॥
2.2.m: Hearing those words of his, the great sage Dadhīca / went to the forest for austerity, remembering Śiva with great love.

2.2.s:
tatra gatvā vidhānena mahāmṛtyuñjayābhidham |
taṃ manuṃ prajapan prītyā tapastepe śivaṃ smaran ||
2.2.d:
तत्र गत्वा विधानेन महामृत्युञ्जयाभिधम् ।
तं मनुं प्रजपन् प्रीत्या तपस्तेपे शिवं स्मरन् ॥
2.2.m: Going there in accordance with rule, properly chanting that mantra / called the Mahāmṛtyuñjaya, he performed austerity, remembering Śiva with love.

2.2.s:
tanmanuṃ suciraṃ japtvā tapasārādhya śaṅkaram |
śivaṃ santoṣayāmāsa mahāmṛtyuñjayaṃ hi saḥ ||
2.2.d:
तन्मनुं सुचिरं जप्त्वा तपसाराध्य शङ्करम् ।
शिवं सन्तोषयामास महामृत्युञ्जयं हि सः ॥
2.2.m: Having chanted that mantra for a very long time, propitiating Śaṅkara through austerity, / he indeed pleased Śiva, the Great Conqueror of Death (Mahāmṛtyuñjaya).

2.2.s:
atha śambhuḥ prasannātmā tajjapādbhaktavatsalaḥ |
āvirbabhūva puratastasya prītyā mahāmune ||
2.2.d:
अथ शम्भुः प्रसन्नात्मा तज्जपाद्भक्तवत्सलः ।
आविर्बभूव पुरतस्तस्य प्रीत्या महामुने ॥
2.2.m: Then Śambhu, gracious in spirit, affectionate toward devotees, / appeared before him with affection because of his recitation, O great sage.

2.2.s:
taṃ dṛṣṭvā svaprabhuṃ śambhuṃ sa mumoda munīśvaraḥ |
praṇamya vidhivadbhaktyā tuṣṭāva sukṛtāñjaliḥ ||
2.2.d:
तं दृष्ट्वा स्वप्रभुं शम्भुं स मुमोद मुनीश्वरः ।
प्रणम्य विधिवद्भक्त्या तुष्टाव सुकृताञ्जलिः ॥
2.2.m: Seeing his own lord Śambhu, that foremost of sages rejoiced; / bowing down with devotion according to rule, his hands folded, he praised him.

2.2.s:
atha prītyā śivastāta prasannaścyāvaniṃ mune |
varaṃ brūhīti sa prāha suprasannena cetasā ||
2.2.d:
अथ प्रीत्या शिवस्तात प्रसन्नश्च्यावनिं मुने ।
वरं ब्रूहीति स प्राह सुप्रसन्नेन चेतसा ॥
2.2.m: Then with love, my dear, Śiva, pleased, said to Cyavana's son, / O sage, with an exceedingly gracious mind: 'Choose a boon!'

2.2.s:
tacchrutvā śambhuvacanaṃ dadhīco bhaktasattamaḥ |
sāñjalirnatakaḥ prāha śaṅkaraṃ bhaktavatsalam ||
2.2.d:
तच्छ्रुत्वा शम्भुवचनं दधीचो भक्तसत्तमः ।
साञ्जलिर्नतकः प्राह शङ्करं भक्तवत्सलम् ॥
2.2.m: Hearing that speech of Śambhu, Dadhīca, best of devotees, / bowing his head with folded hands, spoke to Śaṅkara, who is affectionate toward devotees.

2.2.s:
dadhīca uvāca |
devadeva mahādeva mahyaṃ dehi varatrayam |
vajrāsthitvamavadhyatvamadīnatvaṃ hi sarvataḥ ||
2.2.d:
दधीच उवाच ।
देवदेव महादेव मह्यं देहि वरत्रयम् ।
वज्रास्थित्वमवध्यत्वमदीनत्वं हि सर्वतः ॥
2.2.m: Dadhīca said: / 'O God of gods, O Mahādeva, grant me three boons: / having bones like adamantine vajra, invulnerability to death, and freedom from depression everywhere.'

2.2.s:
brahmovāca |
taduktavacanaṃ śrutvā prasannaḥ parameśvaraḥ |
varatrayaṃ dadau tasmai dadhīcāya tathāstviti ||
2.2.d:
ब्रह्मोवाच ।
तदुक्तवचनं श्रुत्वा प्रसन्नः परमेश्वरः ।
वरत्रयं ददौ तस्मै दधीचाय तथास्त्विति ॥
2.2.m: Brahmā said: / Hearing the words he spoke, the pleased Parameśvara / granted those three boons to Dadhīca, saying, 'So be it.'

2.2.s:
varatrayaṃ śivātprāpya sānandaśca mahāmuniḥ |
kṣuvasthānaṃ jagāmāśu vedamārge pratiṣṭhitaḥ ||
2.2.d:
वरत्रयं शिवात्प्राप्य सानन्दश्च महामुनिः ।
क्षुवस्थानं जगामाशु वेदमार्गे प्रतिष्ठितः ॥
2.2.m: Having obtained the three boons from Śiva, the great sage, filled with joy / and established in the Vedic path, quickly went to Kṣuva's abode.

2.2.s:
prāpyāvadhyatvamugrātsa vajrāsthitvamadīnatām |
atāḍayacca rājendraṃ pādamūlena mūrdhani ||
2.2.d:
प्राप्यावध्यत्वमुग्रात्स वज्रास्थित्वमदीनताम् ।
अताडयच्च राजेन्द्रं पादमूलेन मूर्धनि ॥
2.2.m: Having obtained invulnerability to death from the fierce god, bones like vajra, and freedom from dejection, / he struck the lord of kings on the head with the sole of his foot.

2.2.s:
kṣuvo dadhīcaṃ vajreṇa jaghānorasyatho nṛpaḥ |
krodhaṃ kṛtvā viśeṣeṇa viṣṇugauravagarvitaḥ ||
2.2.d:
क्षुवो दधीचं वज्रेण जघानोरस्यथो नृपः ।
क्रोधं कृत्वा विशेषेण विष्णुगौरवगर्वितः ॥
2.2.m: Then King Kṣuva struck Dadhīca on the chest with a vajra, / having become exceedingly angry and arrogant with pride in Viṣṇu.

2.2.s:
nābhūnnāśāya tadvajraṃ dadhīcasya mahātmanaḥ |
prabhāvātparameśasya dhātṛputro visismiye ||
2.2.d:
नाभून्नाशाय तद्वज्रं दधीचस्य महात्मनः ।
प्रभावात्परमेशस्य धातृपुत्रो विसिस्मिये ॥
2.2.m: That vajra did not lead to the destruction of the noble Dadhīca; / through the power of Parameśa, the son of the Creator was astonished.

2.2.s:
dṛṣṭvāpyavadhyatvamadīnatāṃ ca vajrasya cātyantaparaprabhāvam |
kṣuvo dadhīcasya munīśvarasya visismiye cetasi dhātṛputraḥ ||
2.2.d:
दृष्ट्वाप्यवध्यत्वमदीनतां च वज्रस्य चात्यन्तपरप्रभावम् ।
क्षुवो दधीचस्य मुनीश्वरस्य विसिस्मिये चेतसि धातृपुत्रः ॥
2.2.m: Having seen his invulnerability to death, his freedom from dejection, and the vajra's utter failure of supreme power, / Kṣuva, the son of the Creator, was astonished in his mind at Dadhīca, the foremost of sages.

2.2.s:
ārādhayāmāsa hariṃ mukunda-mindrānujaṃ kānanamāśu gatvā |
prapannapālaśca parājito hi dadhīcamṛtyuñjayasevakena ||
2.2.d:
आराधयामास हरिं मुकुन्द-मिन्द्रानुजं काननमाशु गत्वा ।
प्रपन्नपालश्च पराजितो हि दधीचमृत्युञ्जयसेवकेन ॥
2.2.m: Going swiftly to the forest, he propitiated Hari, Mukunda, / Indra's younger brother, the protector of the surrendered, having indeed been defeated by the servant of Mṛtyuñjaya, Dadhīca.

2.2.s:
pūjayā tasya santuṣṭo bhagavān madhusūdanaḥ |
pradadau darśanaṃ tasmai divyaṃ vai garuḍadhvajaḥ ||
2.2.d:
पूजया तस्य सन्तुष्टो भगवान् मधुसूदनः ।
प्रददौ दर्शनं तस्मै दिव्यं वै गरुडध्वजः ॥
2.2.m: Satisfied with his worship, the blessed slayer of Madhu, / having Garuḍa on his banner, granted him a divine vision of himself.

2.2.s:
divyena darśanenaiva dṛṣṭvā devaṃ janārdanam |
tuṣṭāva vāgbhiriṣṭābhiḥ praṇamya garuḍadhvajam ||
2.2.d:
दिव्येन दर्शनेनैव दृष्ट्वा देवं जनार्दनम् ।
तुष्टाव वाग्भिरिष्टाभिः प्रणम्य गरुडध्वजम् ॥
2.2.m: Having seen the divine Janārdana through that divine vision, / he bowed to him whose banner bears Garuḍa and praised him with chosen words.

2.2.s:
sampūjya caivaṃ tridaśeśvarādyaiḥ stutvā stutaṃ devamajeyamīśam |
vijñāpayāmāsa nirīkṣya bhaktyā janārdanāya praṇipatya mūrdhnā ||
2.2.d:
सम्पूज्य चैवं त्रिदशेश्वराद्यैः स्तुत्वा स्तुतं देवमजेयमीशम् ।
विज्ञापयामास निरीक्ष्य भक्त्या जनार्दनाय प्रणिपत्य मूर्ध्ना ॥
2.2.m: Having thus worshipped and praised the invincible lord, who is praised by Indra and the other gods, / he looked upon him with devotion, prostrated with his head to Janārdana, and addressed him:

2.2.s:
rājovāca |
bhagavan brāhmaṇaḥ kaściddadhīca iti viśrutaḥ |
dharmavettā vinītātmā sakhā mama purābhavat ||
2.2.d:
राजोवाच ।
भगवन् ब्राह्मणः कश्चिद्दधीच इति विश्रुतः ।
धर्मवेत्ता विनीतात्मा सखा मम पुराभवत् ॥
2.2.m: The king said: / 'O Lord, a certain brāhmaṇa known as Dadhīca, / a knower of dharma and disciplined in mind, was formerly my friend.

2.2.s:
avadhyaḥ sarvadā sarvaiḥ śaṅkarasya prabhāvataḥ |
tamārādhya mahādevaṃ mṛtyuñjayamanāmayam ||
2.2.d:
अवध्यः सर्वदा सर्वैः शङ्करस्य प्रभावतः ।
तमाराध्य महादेवं मृत्युञ्जयमनामयम् ॥
2.2.m: He is always invulnerable to death by anyone through the power of Śaṅkara, / having propitiated that Mahādeva, the conqueror of death, the flawless one.

2.2.s:
sāvajñaṃ vāmapādena mama mūrdhni sadasyapi |
tāḍayāmāsa vegena sa dadhīco mahātapāḥ ||
2.2.d:
सावज्ञं वामपादेन मम मूर्ध्नि सदस्यपि ।
ताडयामास वेगेन स दधीचो महातपाः ॥
2.2.m: Contemptuously with his left foot, even in the assembly, / that Dadhīca of great austerities struck my head with force.

2.2.s:
uvāca māṃ ca garveṇa na bibhemīti sarvataḥ |
mṛtyuñjayāptasuvaro garvito hyatulaṃ hare ||
2.2.d:
उवाच मां च गर्वेण न बिभेमीति सर्वतः ।
मृत्युञ्जयाप्तसुवरो गर्वितो ह्यतुलं हरे ॥
2.2.m: And with pride he said to me: “I have no fear from any quarter!” / Having obtained excellent boons from Mṛtyuñjaya, he is matchlessly haughty, O Hari.'

2.2.s:
atha jñātvā dadhīcasya hyavadhyatvaṃ mahātmanaḥ |
sasmārāsya maheśasya prabhāvamatulaṃ hariḥ ||
2.2.d:
अथ ज्ञात्वा दधीचस्य ह्यवध्यत्वं महात्मनः ।
सस्मारास्य महेशस्य प्रभावमतुलं हरिः ॥
2.2.m: Then, having learned of the noble Dadhīca's invulnerability to death, / Hari remembered the peerless power of this Maheśa.

2.2.s:
evaṃ smṛtvā hariḥ prāha kṣuvaṃ vidhisutaṃ drutam |
viprāṇāṃ nāsti rājendra bhayamaṇvapi kutracit ||
2.2.d:
एवं स्मृत्वा हरिः प्राह क्षुवं विधिसुतं द्रुतम् ।
विप्राणां नास्ति राजेन्द्र भयमण्वपि कुत्रचित् ॥
2.2.m: Remembering this, Hari quickly said to Kṣuva, the son of the Creator: / 'O lord of kings, brāhmaṇas have not the slightest fear anywhere.

2.2.s:
viśeṣād rudrabhaktānāṃ bhayaṃ nāsti ca bhūpate |
duḥkhaṃ karoti viprasya śāpārthaṃ sa surasya me ||
2.2.d:
विशेषाद् रुद्रभक्तानां भयं नास्ति च भूपते ।
दुःखं करोति विप्रस्य शापार्थं स सुरस्य मे ॥
2.2.m: Especially devotees of Rudra have no fear, O ruler of the earth. / If one brings grief to a brāhmaṇa, he utters a curse even against me, a god.

2.2.s:
bhavitā tasya śāpena dakṣayajñe sureśvarāt |
vināśo mama rājendra punarutthānameva ca ||
2.2.d:
भविता तस्य शापेन दक्षयज्ञे सुरेश्वरात् ।
विनाशो मम राजेन्द्र पुनरुत्थानमेव च ॥
2.2.m: By his curse, at the sacrifice of Dakṣa, there will be my destruction / by the lord of the gods, O lord of kings, and then my rising up again.

2.2.s:
tasmātsametya rājendra sarvayajño na bhūyate |
karomi yatnaṃ rājendra dadhīcavijayāya te ||
2.2.d:
तस्मात्समेत्य राजेन्द्र सर्वयज्ञो न भूयते ।
करोमि यत्नं राजेन्द्र दधीचविजयाय ते ॥
2.2.m: Therefore, even if all sacrifices were united, O lord of kings, it would not happen; / [yet] I will make an effort, O lord of kings, for your victory over Dadhīca.'

2.2.s:
śrutvā vākyaṃ kṣuvaḥ prāha tathāstviti harernṛpaḥ |
tasthau tatraiva tatprītyā tatkāmotsukamānasaḥ ||
śrīgaṇeśāya namaḥ ||
śrīgaurīśaṅkarābhyāṃ namaḥ ||
śrīśivamahāpurāṇam ||
dvitīyāyāṃ rudrasaṃhitāyāṃ dvitīyaḥ satīkhaṇḍe
2.2.d:
श्रुत्वा वाक्यं क्षुवः प्राह तथास्त्विति हरेर्नृपः ।
तस्थौ तत्रैव तत्प्रीत्या तत्कामोत्सुकमानसः ॥
श्रीगणेशाय नमः ॥
श्रीगौरीशङ्कराभ्यां नमः ॥
श्रीशिवमहापुराणम् ॥
द्वितीयायां रुद्रसंहितायां द्वितीयः सतीखण्डे
2.2.m:
Hearing Hari's speech, King Kṣuva said, 'So be it,' / and stayed right there out of love for him, his mind eager for that desired end.

Thus ends the thirty-eighth chapter, called 'The Description of the Dispute Between Kṣuva and Dadhīca,' in the Satī section, the second [part] of the Rudrasaṃhitā, in the glorious Śiva Mahāpurāṇa.

2.2.s:
brahmovāca |
kṣuvasya hitakṛtyena dadhīcasyāśramaṃ yayau |
viprarūpamathāsthāya bhagavān bhaktavatsalaḥ ||
2.2.d:
ब्रह्मोवाच ।
क्षुवस्य हितकृत्येन दधीचस्याश्रमं ययौ ।
विप्ररूपमथास्थाय भगवान् भक्तवत्सलः ॥
2.2.m: Brahmā said: / For the sake of Kṣuva's welfare, the Blessed One, affectionate toward devotees, / assumed the form of a brāhmaṇa and went to Dadhīca's hermitage.

2.2.s:
dadhīcaṃ prāha viprarṣimabhivandya jagadguruḥ |
kṣuvakāryārthamudyuktaḥ śaivendraṃ chalamāśritaḥ ||
2.2.d:
दधीचं प्राह विप्रर्षिमभिवन्द्य जगद्गुरुः ।
क्षुवकार्यार्थमुद्युक्तः शैवेन्द्रं छलमाश्रितः ॥
2.2.m: The teacher of the universe, dedicated to Kṣuva's purpose, / bowed to Dadhīca, the brāhmaṇa-sage, and addressed the foremost of Śaivas, resorting to deceit.

2.2.s:
viṣṇuruvāca |
bho bho dadhīca viprarṣe bhavārcanaratāvyaya |
varamekaṃ vṛṇe tvattastadbhavān dātumarhati ||
brahmovāca |
yācito devadevena dadhīcaḥ śaivasattamaḥ ||
2.2.d:
विष्णुरुवाच ।
भो भो दधीच विप्रर्षे भवार्चनरताव्यय ।
वरमेकं वृणे त्वत्तस्तद्भवान् दातुमर्हति ॥
ब्रह्मोवाच ।
याचितो देवदेवेन दधीचः शैवसत्तमः ॥
2.2.m:
Viṣṇu said: / 'O Dadhīca, O brāhmaṇa-sage, imperishable one devoted to worshipping Bhava, / I ask one boon from you; you ought to grant it.'

Brahmā said: / When Dadhīca, the best of Śaivas, was thus petitioned / by the God of gods who sought to accomplish Kṣuva's purpose,

2.2.s: kṣuvakāryārthinā śīghraṃ jagāda vacanaṃ harim ||
2.2.d: क्षुवकार्यार्थिना शीघ्रं जगाद वचनं हरिम् ॥
2.2.m: he quickly spoke these words to Hari:

2.2.s:
dadhīca uvāca |
jñātaṃ tavepsitaṃ vipra kṣuvakāryārthamāgataḥ |
bhagavān viprarūpeṇa māyī tvamasi vai hariḥ ||
2.2.d:
दधीच उवाच ।
ज्ञातं तवेप्सितं विप्र क्षुवकार्यार्थमागतः ।
भगवान् विप्ररूपेण मायी त्वमसि वै हरिः ॥
2.2.m: Dadhīca said: / 'What you desire is known, O brāhmaṇa. You have come for Kṣuva's sake. / In the form of a brāhmaṇa, you are indeed the Blessed One, the illusory Hari!

2.2.s:
bhūtaṃ bhaviṣyaṃ deveśa vartamānaṃ janārdana |
jñānaṃ prasādād rudrasya sadā traikālikaṃ mama ||
2.2.d:
भूतं भविष्यं देवेश वर्तमानं जनार्दन ।
ज्ञानं प्रसादाद् रुद्रस्य सदा त्रैकालिकं मम ॥
2.2.m: O God of gods, O Janārdana, through the grace of Rudra / my knowledge of the past, the future, and the present is ever threefold in time.

2.2.s:
tvāṃ jāne'haṃ hariṃ viṣṇuṃ dvijatvaṃ tyaja suvrata |
ārādhito'si bhūpena kṣuveṇa khalabuddhinā ||
2.2.d:
त्वां जानेऽहं हरिं विष्णुं द्विजत्वं त्यज सुव्रत ।
आराधितोऽसि भूपेन क्षुवेण खलबुद्धिना ॥
2.2.m: I know you are Hari, Viṣṇu! Cast aside your disguise as a brāhmaṇa, O you of good vows! / You have been propitiated by King Kṣuva of wicked mind.

2.2.s:
jāne tavaiva bhagavan bhaktavatsalatāṃ hare |
chalaṃ tyaja svarūpaṃ hi svīkuru smara śaṅkaram ||
2.2.d:
जाने तवैव भगवन् भक्तवत्सलतां हरे ।
छलं त्यज स्वरूपं हि स्वीकुरु स्मर शङ्करम् ॥
2.2.m: I know your affection toward devotees, O Lord, O Hari. / Cast off deceit, assume your own form, and remember Śaṅkara!

2.2.s:
asti cetkasyacidbhītirbhavārcanaratasya me |
vaktumarhasi yatnena satyadhāraṇapūrvakam ||
2.2.d:
अस्ति चेत्कस्यचिद्भीतिर्भवार्चनरतस्य मे ।
वक्तुमर्हसि यत्नेन सत्यधारणपूर्वकम् ॥
2.2.m: If I, devoted to the worship of Bhava, have fear of anyone, / you ought to say so carefully, holding to truth.

2.2.s:
vadāmi na mṛṣā kvāpi śivasmaraṇasaktadhīḥ |
na bibhemi jagatyasmindevadaityādikādapi ||
2.2.d:
वदामि न मृषा क्वापि शिवस्मरणसक्तधीः ।
न बिभेमि जगत्यस्मिन्देवदैत्यादिकादपि ॥
2.2.m: With my mind attached to remembering Śiva, I never speak falsely: / I do not fear anything in this world, even gods and demons!'

2.2.s:
viṣṇuruvāca |
bhayaṃ dadhīca sarvatra naṣṭaṃ ca tava suvrata |
bhavārcanarato yasmādbhavānsarvajña eva ca ||
2.2.d:
विष्णुरुवाच ।
भयं दधीच सर्वत्र नष्टं च तव सुव्रत ।
भवार्चनरतो यस्माद्भवान्सर्वज्ञ एव च ॥
2.2.m: Viṣṇu said: / 'Fear has indeed vanished everywhere for you, Dadhīca, O you of good vows, / because you are devoted to the worship of Bhava and are all-knowing.

2.2.s:
bibhemīti sakṛdvaktumarhasi tvaṃ namastava |
niyogānmama rājendra kṣuvāt pratisahādaham ||
2.2.d:
बिभेमीति सकृद्वक्तुमर्हसि त्वं नमस्तव ।
नियोगान्मम राजेन्द्र क्षुवात् प्रतिसहादहम् ॥
2.2.m: You ought to say “I am afraid” just once—salutations to you!— / at my command, O foremost of kings, so that I can face Kṣuva.'

2.2.s:
brahmovāca |
evaṃ śrutvāpi tadvākyaṃ viṣṇoḥ sa tu mahāmuniḥ |
vihasya nirbhayaḥ prāha dadhīcaḥ śaivasattamaḥ ||
2.2.d:
ब्रह्मोवाच ।
एवं श्रुत्वापि तद्वाक्यं विष्णोः स तु महामुनिः ।
विहस्य निर्भयः प्राह दधीचः शैवसत्तमः ॥
2.2.m: Brahmā said: / Hearing that speech of Viṣṇu, that great sage, / Dadhīca, best of Śaivas, laughed and fearlessly replied:

2.2.s:
dadhīca uvāca |
na bibhemi sadā kvāpi kutaścidapi kiñcana |
prabhāvāddevadevasya śambhoḥ sākṣātpinākinaḥ ||
2.2.d:
दधीच उवाच ।
न बिभेमि सदा क्वापि कुतश्चिदपि किञ्चन ।
प्रभावाद्देवदेवस्य शम्भोः साक्षात्पिनाकिनः ॥
2.2.m: Dadhīca said: / 'I am never afraid, anywhere, of anything whatsoever, / through the power of the God of gods, Śambhu himself, who bears the Pināka.'

2.2.s:
brahmovāca |
tatastasya muneḥ śrutvā vacanaṃ kupito hariḥ |
cakramudyamya santasthau didhakṣurmunisattamam ||
2.2.d:
ब्रह्मोवाच ।
ततस्तस्य मुनेः श्रुत्वा वचनं कुपितो हरिः ।
चक्रमुद्यम्य सन्तस्थौ दिधक्षुर्मुनिसत्तमम् ॥
2.2.m: Brahmā said: / Hearing the speech of that sage, Hari became enraged; / raising his discus, he stood ready, desiring to burn the foremost of sages.

2.2.s:
abhavatkuṇṭhitaṃ tatra vipre cakraṃ sudāruṇam |
prabhāvācca tadīśasya nṛpateḥ sannidhāvapi ||
2.2.d:
अभवत्कुण्ठितं तत्र विप्रे चक्रं सुदारुणम् ।
प्रभावाच्च तदीशस्य नृपतेः सन्निधावपि ॥
2.2.m: The terrifying discus became blunted against the Brahmin there, / and through the power of his Lord, even in the presence of the king.

2.2.s:
dṛṣṭvā taṃ kuṇṭhitāsyaṃ taccakraṃ viṣṇuṃ jagāda ha |
dadhīcaḥ sasmitaṃ sākṣātsadasadvyaktikāraṇam ||
2.2.d:
दृष्ट्वा तं कुण्ठितास्यं तच्चक्रं विष्णुं जगाद ह ।
दधीचः सस्मितं साक्षात्सदसद्व्यक्तिकारणम् ॥
2.2.m: Seeing that discus with its edge blunted, Dadhīca, / the cause of revealing the real and the unreal, smiled and addressed Viṣṇu in person:

2.2.s:
dadhīca uvāca |
bhagavan bhavatā labdhaṃ purātīva sudāruṇam |
sudarśanamiti khyātaṃ cakraṃ viṣṇoḥ prayatnataḥ |
bhavasya tacchubhaṃ cakraṃ na jighāṃsati māmiha ||
2.2.d:
दधीच उवाच ।
भगवन् भवता लब्धं पुरातीव सुदारुणम् ।
सुदर्शनमिति ख्यातं चक्रं विष्णोः प्रयत्नतः ।
भवस्य तच्छुभं चक्रं न जिघांसति मामिह ॥
2.2.m: Dadhīca said: / 'O lord, that very terrible discus renowned as Sudarśana / was formerly obtained by you, Viṣṇu, with great effort. / That auspicious discus belonging to Bhava does not wish to slay me here.'

2.2.s:
bhagavānatha kruddho'smai sarvāstrāṇi kramāddhariḥ |
brahmāstrādyaiḥ śaraiścāstraiḥ prayatnaṃ kartumarhasi ||
2.2.d:
भगवानथ क्रुद्धोऽस्मै सर्वास्त्राणि क्रमाद्धरिः ।
ब्रह्मास्त्राद्यैः शरैश्चास्त्रैः प्रयत्नं कर्तुमर्हसि ॥
2.2.m: [Viṣṇu thought:] 'Now the lord Hari is enraged at him with all his weapons in succession; / you ought to make an effort with arrows and weapons beginning with the Brahmāstra.'

2.2.s:
brahmovāca |
sa tasya vacanaṃ śrutvā dṛṣṭvā nirvīryamānuṣam |
sasarjātha krudhā tasmai sarvāstrāṇi kramāddhariḥ ||
2.2.d:
ब्रह्मोवाच ।
स तस्य वचनं श्रुत्वा दृष्ट्वा निर्वीर्यमानुषम् ।
ससर्जाथ क्रुधा तस्मै सर्वास्त्राणि क्रमाद्धरिः ॥
2.2.m: Brahmā said: / Hearing his words and seeing him as a powerless mortal, / Hari then in anger discharged all his weapons against him in succession.

2.2.s:
cakrurdevāstatastasya viṣṇoḥsāhāyyamādarāt |
dvijenaikena saṃyoddhuṃ prasṛtasya vibuddhayaḥ ||
2.2.d:
चक्रुर्देवास्ततस्तस्य विष्णोःसाहाय्यमादरात् ।
द्विजेनैकेन संयोद्धुं प्रसृतस्य विबुद्धयः ॥
2.2.m: Then the gods, having no sense, eagerly gave assistance / to that Viṣṇu who advanced to fight with a single twice-born.

2.2.s:
cikṣipuḥ svāni svānyāśu śastrāṇyastrāṇi sarvataḥ |
dadhīcopari vegena śakrādyā haripākṣikāḥ ||
2.2.d:
चिक्षिपुः स्वानि स्वान्याशु शस्त्राण्यस्त्राणि सर्वतः ।
दधीचोपरि वेगेन शक्राद्या हरिपाक्षिकाः ॥
2.2.m: The gods headed by Śakra, siding with Hari, swiftly hurled their own / arms and missiles from all sides upon Dadhīca with great speed.

2.2.s:
kuśamuṣṭimathādāya dadhīcaḥ saṃsmaran śivam |
sasarja sarvadevebhyo vajrāsthiḥ sarvato vaśī ||
2.2.d:
कुशमुष्टिमथादाय दधीचः संस्मरन् शिवम् ।
ससर्ज सर्वदेवेभ्यो वज्रास्थिः सर्वतो वशी ॥
2.2.m: Then, taking a handful of kuśa grass and remembering Śiva, / Dadhīca, whose bones were adamantine and who was self-controlled, hurled it all around at all the gods.

2.2.s:
śaṅkarasya prabhāvāttu kuśamuṣṭirmunerhi sā |
divyaṃ triśūlamabhavat kālāgnisadṛśaṃ mune ||
2.2.d:
शङ्करस्य प्रभावात्तु कुशमुष्टिर्मुनेर्हि सा ।
दिव्यं त्रिशूलमभवत् कालाग्निसदृशं मुने ॥
2.2.m: Through the power of Śaṅkara, O sage, that handful of kuśa grass belonging to the sage / became a divine trident, resembling the fire of cosmic dissolution.

2.2.s:
dagdhuṃ devān matiṃ cakre sāyudhān saśikhaṃ ca tat |
prajvalatsarvataḥ śaivaṃ yugāntāgnyadhikaprabham ||
2.2.d:
दग्धुं देवान् मतिं चक्रे सायुधान् सशिखं च तत् ।
प्रज्वलत्सर्वतः शैवं युगान्ताग्न्यधिकप्रभम् ॥
2.2.m: Flaming on all sides with splendor greater than the fire at the end of the age, / that trident of Śiva, along with its points, resolved to burn the gods together with their weapons.

2.2.s:
nārāyaṇendramukhyaistu devaiḥ kṣiptāni yāni ca |
āyudhāni samastāni praṇemustriśikhaṃ ca tat ||
2.2.d:
नारायणेन्द्रमुख्यैस्तु देवैः क्षिप्तानि यानि च ।
आयुधानि समस्तानि प्रणेमुस्त्रिशिखं च तत् ॥
2.2.m: All the weapons that were hurled by the gods, / headed by Nārāyaṇa and Indra, bowed down before that three-pronged [trident].

2.2.s:
devāśca dudruvuḥ sarve dhvastavīryā divaukasaḥ |
tasthau tatra harirbhītaḥ kevalaṃ māyināṃ varaḥ ||
2.2.d:
देवाश्च दुद्रुवुः सर्वे ध्वस्तवीर्या दिवौकसः ।
तस्थौ तत्र हरिर्भीतः केवलं मायिनां वरः ॥
2.2.m: And all the gods, the dwellers of heaven, fled, their valor shattered. / Only Hari, the best of illusionists, stood there terrified.

2.2.s:
sasarja bhagavān viṣṇuḥ svadehātpuruṣottamaḥ |
ātmanaḥ sadṛśān divyān lakṣalakṣāyutān gaṇān ||
2.2.d:
ससर्ज भगवान् विष्णुः स्वदेहात्पुरुषोत्तमः ।
आत्मनः सदृशान् दिव्यान् लक्षलक्षायुतान् गणान् ॥
2.2.m: Lord Viṣṇu, the Supreme Person, produced from his own body / divine hosts resembling himself by hundreds of thousands and tens of thousands.

2.2.s:
te cāpi yuyudhustatra vīrā viṣṇugaṇāstataḥ |
muninaikena devarṣe dadhīcena śivātmanā ||
2.2.d:
ते चापि युयुधुस्तत्र वीरा विष्णुगणास्ततः ।
मुनिनैकेन देवर्षे दधीचेन शिवात्मना ॥
2.2.m: And then those heroic attendants of Viṣṇu fought there, / O divine sage, against a single sage, Dadhīca, whose essence was Śiva.

2.2.s:
tato viṣṇugaṇāṃstānvai niyudhya bahuśo raṇe |
dadāha sahasā sarvān dadhīcaḥ śaivasattamaḥ ||
2.2.d:
ततो विष्णुगणांस्तान्वै नियुध्य बहुशो रणे ।
ददाह सहसा सर्वान् दधीचः शैवसत्तमः ॥
2.2.m: Having fought repeatedly in battle, Dadhīca, the best of Śaivas, / then instantly burned all those attendants of Viṣṇu.

2.2.s:
tatastadvismayārthāya dadhīcasya munerhariḥ |
viśvamūrtirabhūcchīghraṃ mahāmāyāviśāradaḥ ||
2.2.d:
ततस्तद्विस्मयार्थाय दधीचस्य मुनेर्हरिः ।
विश्वमूर्तिरभूच्छीघ्रं महामायाविशारदः ॥
2.2.m: Then, to astonish that sage Dadhīca, Hari, / who is skilled in great illusion, quickly assumed his universal form.

2.2.s:
tasya dehe hareḥ sākṣādapaśyad dvijasattamaḥ |
dadhīco devatādīnāṃ jīvānāṃ ca sahasrakam ||
2.2.d:
तस्य देहे हरेः साक्षादपश्यद् द्विजसत्तमः ।
दधीचो देवतादीनां जीवानां च सहस्रकम् ॥
2.2.m: In that body of Hari, Dadhīca, the best of the twice-born, / directly saw thousands of living beings beginning with the gods,

2.2.s:
bhūtānāṃ koṭayaścaiva gaṇānāṃ koṭayastathā |
aṇḍānāṃ koṭayaścaiva viśvamūrtestanau tadā ||
2.2.d:
भूतानां कोटयश्चैव गणानां कोटयस्तथा ।
अण्डानां कोटयश्चैव विश्वमूर्तेस्तनौ तदा ॥
2.2.m: and crores of beings, crores of attendants, / and crores of cosmic eggs in the body of the Universal Form at that time.

2.2.s:
dṛṣṭvaitadakhilaṃ tatra cyāvaniḥ satataṃ tadā |
viṣṇumāha jagannāthaṃ jagatstavamajaṃ vibhum ||
2.2.d:
दृष्ट्वैतदखिलं तत्र च्यावनिः सततं तदा ।
विष्णुमाह जगन्नाथं जगत्स्तवमजं विभुम् ॥
2.2.m: Seeing all this there, the son of Cyavana then constantly / addressed Viṣṇu, the lord of the universe, who is praised by the world, unborn, and all-pervading.

2.2.s:
dadhīca uvāca |
māyāṃ tyaja mahābāho pratibhāso vicārataḥ |
vijñātāni sahasrāṇi durvijñeyāni mādhava ||
2.2.d:
दधीच उवाच ।
मायां त्यज महाबाहो प्रतिभासो विचारतः ।
विज्ञातानि सहस्राणि दुर्विज्ञेयानि माधव ॥
2.2.m: Dadhīca said: / 'Cast off your illusion, O mighty-armed one! It is an appearance upon inquiry; / thousands [of things] that are difficult to comprehend have been known [by me], O Mādhava!

2.2.s:
mayi paśya jagatsarvaṃ tvayā yuktamatandritaḥ |
brahmāṇaṃ ca tathā rudraṃ divyāṃ dṛṣṭiṃ dadāmi te ||
2.2.d:
मयि पश्य जगत्सर्वं त्वया युक्तमतन्द्रितः ।
ब्रह्माणं च तथा रुद्रं दिव्यां दृष्टिं ददामि ते ॥
2.2.m: Look upon the entire universe within me, united with you, without sloth, / as well as Brahmā and Rudra; I grant you divine vision!'

2.2.s:
brahmovāca |
ityuktvā darśayāmāsa svatanau nikhilaṃ muniḥ |
brahmāṇḍaṃ cyāvaniḥ śambhutejasā pūrṇadehakaḥ ||
2.2.d:
ब्रह्मोवाच ।
इत्युक्त्वा दर्शयामास स्वतनौ निखिलं मुनिः ।
ब्रह्माण्डं च्यावनिः शम्भुतेजसा पूर्णदेहकः ॥
2.2.m: Brahmā said: / Having spoken thus, the sage, the son of Cyavana, whose body was filled with the fiery energy of Śambhu, / showed the entire universe within his own body.

2.2.s:
tadāha viṣṇuṃ deveśaṃ dadhīcaḥ śaivasattamaḥ |
saṃsmaran śaṅkaraṃ citte vihasan vibhayaḥ sudhīḥ ||
2.2.d:
तदाह विष्णुं देवेशं दधीचः शैवसत्तमः ।
संस्मरन् शङ्करं चित्ते विहसन् विभयः सुधीः ॥
2.2.m: Then Dadhīca, the best of Śaivas, remembering Śaṅkara in his heart, / smiling, fearless, and wise, spoke to Viṣṇu, the lord of the gods:

2.2.s:
dadhīca uvāca |
māyayā tvanayā kiṃ vā mantraśaktyātha vā hare |
satkāmanāmimāṃ kṛtvā yoddhumarhasi yatnataḥ ||
2.2.d:
दधीच उवाच ।
मायया त्वनया किं वा मन्त्रशक्त्याथ वा हरे ।
सत्कामनामिमां कृत्वा योद्धुमर्हसि यत्नतः ॥
2.2.m: Dadhīca said: / 'What is to be gained by this illusion, or by the power of mantras, O Hari? / Having made this noble desire, you ought to fight with effort.'

2.2.s:
brahmovāca |
etacchutvā munestasya vacanaṃ nirbhayastadā |
śambhutejomayaṃ viṣṇuḥ cukopātīva taṃ munim ||
2.2.d:
ब्रह्मोवाच ।
एतच्छुत्वा मुनेस्तस्य वचनं निर्भयस्तदा ।
शम्भुतेजोमयं विष्णुः चुकोपातीव तं मुनिम् ॥
2.2.m: Brahmā said: / Hearing these fearless words of that sage at that time, / Viṣṇu became exceedingly angry with that sage who was filled with Śambhu's fiery energy.

2.2.s:
devāśca dudruvurbhūyo devaṃ nārāyaṇaṃ ca tam |
yoddhukāmāśca muninā dadhīcena pratāpinā ||
2.2.d:
देवाश्च दुद्रुवुर्भूयो देवं नारायणं च तम् ।
योद्धुकामाश्च मुनिना दधीचेन प्रतापिना ॥
2.2.m: And the gods fled once again, and that god Nārāyaṇa, / wishing to fight with the glorious sage Dadhīca, [stood ready].

2.2.s:
etasminnantare tatrāgamanmatsaṅgamaḥ kṣuvaḥ |
avārayantaṃ niśceṣṭaṃ padmayoniṃ hariṃ surān ||
2.2.d:
एतस्मिन्नन्तरे तत्रागमन्मत्सङ्गमः क्षुवः ।
अवारयन्तं निश्चेष्टं पद्मयोनिं हरिं सुरान् ॥
2.2.m: In the meantime, Kṣuva, who was united with me, came there; / he restrained the motionless lotus-born [Brahmā], Hari, and the gods.

2.2.s:
niśamya vacanaṃ me hi brāhmaṇo na vinirjitaḥ |
jagāma nikaṭaṃ tasya praṇanāma muniṃ hariḥ ||
2.2.d:
निशम्य वचनं मे हि ब्राह्मणो न विनिर्जितः ।
जगाम निकटं तस्य प्रणनाम मुनिं हरिः ॥
2.2.m: Hearing my word that the Brahmin could not be conquered, / Hari approached him and bowed down to the sage.

2.2.s:
kṣuvo dīnataro bhūtvā gatvā tatra munīśvaram |
dadhīcamabhivādyaiva prārthayāmāsa viklavaḥ ||
2.2.d:
क्षुवो दीनतरो भूत्वा गत्वा तत्र मुनीश्वरम् ।
दधीचमभिवाद्यैव प्रार्थयामास विक्लवः ॥
2.2.m: Kṣuva, becoming most humble, went there to the lord of sages, / Dadhīca, and having saluted him, agitatedly prayed:

2.2.s:
kṣuva uvāca |
prasīda muniśārdūla śivabhaktaśiromaṇe |
prasīda parameśāna durlakṣyo durjanaiḥ sadā ||
2.2.d:
क्षुव उवाच ।
प्रसीद मुनिशार्दूल शिवभक्तशिरोमणे ।
प्रसीद परमेशान दुर्लक्ष्यो दुर्जनैः सदा ॥
2.2.m: Kṣuva said: / 'Be gracious, O tiger among sages, O crest-jewel of Śiva's devotees! / Be gracious, O supreme lord, always difficult to be perceived by evil people!'

2.2.s:
brahmovāca |
ityākarṇya vacastasya rājñaḥ suragaṇasya hi |
anujagrāha taṃ vipro dadhīcastapasāṃ nidhiḥ ||
2.2.d:
ब्रह्मोवाच ।
इत्याकर्ण्य वचस्तस्य राज्ञः सुरगणस्य हि ।
अनुजग्राह तं विप्रो दधीचस्तपसां निधिः ॥
2.2.m: Brahmā said: / Hearing these words of that king and of the host of gods, / the Brahmin Dadhīca, a treasury of austerities, showed favor to him.

2.2.s:
atha dṛṣṭvā rameśādīn krodhavihvalito muniḥ |
hṛdi smṛtvā śivaṃ viṣṇuṃ śaśāpa ca surānapi ||
2.2.d:
अथ दृष्ट्वा रमेशादीन् क्रोधविह्वलितो मुनिः ।
हृदि स्मृत्वा शिवं विष्णुं शशाप च सुरानपि ॥
2.2.m: Then, seeing the Lord of Ramā and the others, the sage, overcome with anger, / remembered Śiva in his heart and cursed Viṣṇu and the gods as well.

2.2.s:
dadhīca uvāca |
rudrakopāgninā devāḥ sadevendrā munīśvarāḥ |
dhvastā bhavantu devena viṣṇunā ca samaṃ gaṇaiḥ ||
2.2.d:
दधीच उवाच ।
रुद्रकोपाग्निना देवाः सदेवेन्द्रा मुनीश्वराः ।
ध्वस्ता भवन्तु देवेन विष्णुना च समं गणैः ॥
2.2.m: Dadhīca said: / 'May the gods, along with the lord of gods and the lords of sages, / be destroyed by the fire of Rudra's wrath, together with the god Viṣṇu and his attendants!'

2.2.s:
brahmovāca |
evaṃ śaptvā surān prekṣya kṣuvamāha tato muniḥ |
devaiśca pūjyo rājendra nṛpaiścaiva dvijottamaḥ ||
2.2.d:
ब्रह्मोवाच ।
एवं शप्त्वा सुरान् प्रेक्ष्य क्षुवमाह ततो मुनिः ।
देवैश्च पूज्यो राजेन्द्र नृपैश्चैव द्विजोत्तमः ॥
2.2.m: Brahmā said: / Having cursed the gods in this manner and looked at Kṣuva, the sage then said: / 'The best of the twice-born is worthy of worship by gods and by kings, O king of kings.

2.2.s:
brāhmaṇā eva rājendra balinaḥ prabhaviṣṇavaḥ |
ityuktvā sa sphuṭaṃ vipraḥ praviveśa nijāśramam ||
2.2.d:
ब्राह्मणा एव राजेन्द्र बलिनः प्रभविष्णवः ।
इत्युक्त्वा स स्फुटं विप्रः प्रविवेश निजाश्रमम् ॥
2.2.m: Only Brahmins are mighty and powerful, O king of kings!' / Having spoken clearly thus, the Brahmin entered his own hermitage.

2.2.s:
dadhīcamabhivandyaiva kṣuvo nijagṛhaṃ gataḥ |
viṣṇurjagāma svaṃ lokaṃ suraiḥ saha yathāgatam ||
2.2.d:
दधीचमभिवन्द्यैव क्षुवो निजगृहं गतः ।
विष्णुर्जगाम स्वं लोकं सुरैः सह यथागतम् ॥
2.2.m: Having saluted Dadhīca, Kṣuva went to his own home; / Viṣṇu went to his own realm along with the gods, just as he had come.

2.2.s:
tadevaṃ tīrthamabhavat sthāneśvara iti smṛtam |
sthāneśvaramanuprāpya śivasāyujyamāpnuyāt ||
2.2.d:
तदेवं तीर्थमभवत् स्थानेश्वर इति स्मृतम् ।
स्थानेश्वरमनुप्राप्य शिवसायुज्यमाप्नुयात् ॥
2.2.m: In this way, that place became a sacred ford known as Sthāneśvara; / reaching Sthāneśvara, one attains communion with Śiva.

2.2.s:
kathitastava saṅkṣepādvādaḥ kṣuvadadhīcayoḥ |
nṛpāptaśāpayostāta brahmaviṣṇvoḥ śivaṃ vinā ||
2.2.d:
कथितस्तव सङ्क्षेपाद्वादः क्षुवदधीचयोः ।
नृपाप्तशापयोस्तात ब्रह्मविष्ण्वोः शिवं विना ॥
2.2.m: The dispute between Kṣuva and Dadhīca has been told to you in brief, / O dear one, [and the dispute] between Brahmā and Viṣṇu who incurred the king's curse, devoid of Śiva.

2.2.s:
ya idaṃ kīrtayennityaṃ vādaṃ kṣuvadadhīcayoḥ |
jitvāpamṛtyuṃ dehānte brahmalokaṃ prayāti saḥ ||
2.2.d:
य इदं कीर्तयेन्नित्यं वादं क्षुवदधीचयोः ।
जित्वापमृत्युं देहान्ते ब्रह्मलोकं प्रयाति सः ॥
2.2.m: Whoever constantly recites this dispute between Kṣuva and Dadhīca, / having conquered untimely death, goes to the world of Brahmā at the end of the body.

2.2.s:
raṇe yaḥ kīrtayitvedaṃ praviśettasya sarvadā |
mṛtyubhītirbhavennaiva vijayī ca bhaviṣyati ||
śrīgaṇeśāya namaḥ ||
śrīgaurīśaṅkarābhyāṃ namaḥ ||
śrīśivamahāpurāṇam ||
dvitīyāyāṃ rudrasaṃhitāyāṃ dvitīyaḥ satīkhaṇḍe
2.2.d:
रणे यः कीर्तयित्वेदं प्रविशेत्तस्य सर्वदा ।
मृत्युभीतिर्भवेन्नैव विजयी च भविष्यति ॥
श्रीगणेशाय नमः ॥
श्रीगौरीशङ्कराभ्यां नमः ॥
श्रीशिवमहापुराणम् ॥
द्वितीयायां रुद्रसंहितायां द्वितीयः सतीखण्डे
2.2.m:
For one who enters a battle having recited this, / there shall never be fear of death, and he will become victorious.

Thus ends the thirty-ninth chapter, titled 'The Description of the Battle between Viṣṇu and Dadhīca,' in the Satīkhaṇḍa, the second [part] of the Rudrasaṃhitā, in the glorious Śiva Mahāpurāṇa.

2.2.s:
nārada uvāca
vidhe vidhe mahāprājña śaivatattvapradarśaka |
śrāvitā ramaṇīprāyā śivalīlā mahādbhutā ||
2.2.d:
नारद उवाच
विधे विधे महाप्राज्ञ शैवतत्त्वप्रदर्शक ।
श्राविता रमणीप्राया शिवलीला महाद्भुता ॥
2.2.m: Nārada said: / 'O creator, O creator of great wisdom, revealer of the truth of Śiva, / the most delightful and most wonderful sporting of Śiva has been related [by you].

2.2.s:
vīreṇa vīrabhadreṇa dakṣayajñaṃ vināśya vai |
kailāsādrau gate tāta kimabhūttadvadādhunā ||
2.2.d:
वीरेण वीरभद्रेण दक्षयज्ञं विनाश्य वै ।
कैलासाद्रौ गते तात किमभूत्तद्वदाधुना ॥
2.2.m: After the heroic Vīrabhadra destroyed Dakṣa's sacrifice / and went to Mount Kailāsa, tell [me] now, dear father, what happened then?'

2.2.s:
brahmovāca |
atha devagaṇāḥ sarve munayaśca parājitāḥ |
rudrānīkairvibhinnāṅgā mama lokaṃ yayustadā ||
2.2.d:
ब्रह्मोवाच ।
अथ देवगणाः सर्वे मुनयश्च पराजिताः ।
